title: Entering a group dims the layer list but not the canvas
detail: SPLIT, and the two halves went opposite ways. The canvas half STAYS OPEN as a decision, not a bug: the dim was declined because opacity is in Fabric stateProperties, so dimming the canvas would serialise view state into every save, which §67 forbids. That reasoning still holds and nothing here overturns it. The layer half was not a decision at all but a defect, and it was worse than this row says — the row recorded that the list dims today (data-context=false), which is true only after something unrelated re-projects the tree. Fixed as vg-058.

title: The line chart occasionally slides left as if correcting a position
detail: NOT REPRODUCED in 30 seconds of live playback against a real host, and BOTH of the rows named candidates are ruled out for that window. The row guessed a resize observer re-fitting mid-animation, or a chart settling after a viewport change; neither fired: the viewport transform was byte-identical at the start and the end (0.61602870 with the same offset, zero changes in thirty samples), the chart own box never moved (left 616, top 695, 963x215, angle 0, scale 1 and 1), and a ResizeObserver on the body fired once, which is the probe own DOM reads rather than anything the chart did. STILL OPEN, because occasionally is rarer than thirty seconds and closing it on a non-reproduction would be the same mistake as filing it on a screenshot. WHAT THE NEXT ATTEMPT SHOULD USE, because two attempts here failed for one reason and the reason is worth keeping: counting ink in the chart region cannot see this. The card is opaque and the sampled rect includes the dark part of the backdrop, so every column reads as drawn and every column reads as dark — the first probe reported a constant firstX of 0 and lastX of the full width, and a luminance profile reported the same. Watching the EVENTS is what separates a slide from data changing, because data moves locally and a slide moves everything.

title: The preview data source fluctuates faster than a real PC
detail: "The Preview data source fluctuate too rapidly which is not realistic to a normal PC hardware behavior, and a bit distracting for the author." The cadence is a number in fake-source. 'Realistic' needs a decision about what the preview is for.

title: The line chart's Glass control: a Circle's frost reads stronger than a Rect's at the same value
detail: RULING STANDS: a slight per-shape difference is acceptable rather than no glass on closed shapes; the expensive option wins by default. CHARACTERISED, NOT FIXED, and the lead I gave the investigator was wrong. I offered "the Circle region measured 127,449 px against the Rect 156,009 for the same box" as proof the region was shape-dependent. It is not: that sweep gave every shape the same AUTHORING box, and a Circle has no 240x160. Both numbers reconstruct exactly at the sweep pad — 437x357 = 156,009 and 357x357 = 127,449, predicted ratio 0.8165 against 0.81691 measured. At one 260x260 box all five shapes take a byte-identical 362x362 region (131,044 px). PARTIAL COVERAGE REFUTED: no collapse at the rim, and the bin touching the boundary is the largest bin in three of four measurements. MATERIAL PARITY IS BIT-IDENTICAL: mean luma 94.75/94.75 over stripes and 93.41/93.41 over a photograph, distinct colours 40/40 and 10/10, and the frost boxes are pixel-identical at thresholds 2, 1.5 and 1. WHAT DIFFERS IS FOOTPRINT: a Circle covers 78.54% of its box, 21.5% less frosted area — which reads LIGHTER, not stronger, so it is the wrong direction to explain the report. STILL OPEN, and the leading hypothesis is not the renderer: a Circle authored size is a RADIUS and a Rect authored size is a WIDTH, so the same number gives a disc twice the area. Checked and not yet confirmed in the scene where it was seen. glass.ts is byte-identical to the base sha; nothing was simulated away, per the ruling. THE AUTHORS PATH TO THIS COMPARISON IS REACHABLE AFTER ALL, and I said otherwise earlier and was wrong twice about it. First: I claimed the Glass blur control does not exist on a chart. It does not exist on a chart because a chart cannot be frosted — the control appears once there is a radius to tune, and I compared an object that was refused against one that already had frost on. Second: I then said the report could not have come from the editor because the line charts control cannot be changed. True, and beside the point: the report is about a CIRCLE and a RECT, and both are perfectly authorable. MEASURED ACROSS EVERY SHAPE, which is also the ruling ADR-0015 predicts: Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Triangle and Polygon all offer an ENABLED Frosted glass control; Polyline and Line are aria-disabled, correctly, having no closed area to frost. And the two shapes the report names get the SAME DEFAULT: a fresh Circle and a fresh Rectangle both become vigiliaGlass at blurRadius 16 the moment frost is switched on, with the blur control appearing alongside it. So the situation the report describes — a Circle and a Rect at the same value — is exactly what the product produces by default, and the row stands on its own merits again. What remains is what the earlier characterisation established and this does not change: over the area they share the frost is bit-identical, and what differs is footprint, a Circle covering 78.54 percent of its box. If a Circle reads stronger, the leading hypothesis is still the authors own — a Circle size is a RADIUS where a Rectangle size is a WIDTH — and it is still unconfirmed in the scene where it was seen.
check: Measured across every shape in the running editor: Frosted glass is enabled on Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Triangle and Polygon, and aria-disabled on Polyline and Line with the reason on focus. A fresh Circle and a fresh Rectangle both take blurRadius 16 on the same click, and the Glass blur control appears only after that.

title: Auto-save, and a prompt for recovery after a browser crash
detail: RULED: draft in browser storage; write on a ~30 s timer and on leaving the page; recovery offers restore-or-discard naming what was lost; and the editor opens a theme from the library, which is the seam the other two need. BLOCKED: the asset-ownership question decides where the draft lives — if the editor stops holding asset bytes and the host owns them, the draft is a host write and browser storage is wrong.

title: What is derived state in a persisted Fabric object?
detail: The dirty guard's cause (vg-026) is one field of a general question, and patching styles alone leaves the next per-character cache to arrive and be found by the user. SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES is an allowlist that already intends to do this job and is not applied on the way out. The spec should answer which Fabric properties are derived from telemetry or from rendering, how a serialisation excludes all of them, and whether the allowlist should be enforced at the boundary. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-asset-ownership.md. AND NOW THERE IS A SHARP INSTANCE OF IT, MEASURED, which is vg-026. The dirty guard compares a document key against one captured when the editor was built, and with no input at all 13 of the Starter 52 objects change between 0.4 and 1.9 seconds after load — every one a Textbox, repainted by the live preview pass. The document differs from itself with nothing touched, so every New asks the author to save work nobody did. That is what the allowlist was meant to stop and does not reach: the changed objects are bound text, and what the live pass writes is the same property the author edits. This row is therefore not an abstract design question any more — it is one concrete false prompt an author meets on the first Ctrl+N, and the fix belongs here rather than in the dirty guard. AND A SECOND SHARP INSTANCE, MEASURED, is vg-188: entering a group writes `subTargetCheck`/`interactive` on the group, both of which ARE serialized, so `isDirty()` flips with nothing authored and a save taken inside a group would persist editor-only reachability flags into the theme package. That row carries the diff and the Fabric evidence.

title: Where the defect queue lives: the open-ended pass, the Superpowers lifecycle, and beads
detail: The working-out of whether every defect should become a spec and a plan (overkill), and where an open-ended queue sits beside a change lifecycle that has a finish line. Beads is proven installable natively on Windows (v1.3.0, no WSL) with the full lifecycle exercised; bd init edits AGENTS.md and installs hooks by default and --skip-agents declines that. Marked undecided by the user pending thought — specifically, not wanting two agent frameworks fighting each other. The registry is the incumbent until this is decided.

title: The layer list cannot select more than one row, and grouping needs a multi-selection
detail:
The row click is onClick={() => selectLayer(row.id)} and ignores the event, so a shift-click on a second row replaces the first instead of adding to it. MEASURED: shift-clicking strapline after wordmark left only strapline selected, while the same two objects shift-clicked on the canvas select both. Grouping is reachable — the context menu offers Group once the selection is eligible — but only from a canvas multi-selection, so an author working in the layer list cannot make one. Needs a decision rather than a patch: whether a shift-click toggles a row the way the canvas does, whether shift extends a range like a file list, or whether the panel stays single-select and grouping moves somewhere reachable from it. An additive select also has to cross the Fabric-free bridge, which has one selectLayer(id) today.

 CROSS-LINK, deliberately NOT withdrawn: the defect is in a layer panel the redesign replaces, but the requirement behind it - that a list can select more than one row, because arrange is gated on a multi-selection - has to survive into the composition panel or arrange becomes unreachable there. §172 does not state multi-select explicitly, so closing this row would silently drop the requirement.

title: Layer rows declare draggable but nothing consumes the drop, so reordering by drag does nothing
detail:
MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a row that does not reorder is only a finding if reordering is a thing the panel is offering. It is: every layer row carries draggable="true" in the DOM, which is an explicit promise that an HTML5 drag will be received and acted on. Nothing acts on it. Dragging network-chart toward cpu-card-title changes the list not at all - the first eight rows are byte-identical before and after. That is true for a mouse drag and also for Playwright's dragTo, which is the technique that drives HTML5 drag-and-drop rather than mouse events, so this is not my probe using the wrong gesture. THE OPERATION ITSELF WORKS, which is what makes the dead attribute a real cost rather than an unimplemented feature: select the date text on the canvas, right-click, Bring to front, and the host's document moves date from index 6 to index 51 and every other object shifts down. So an author who wants to reorder can, by finding a context menu; an author who tries to drag, which is what the attribute invites and what every other layer panel in this class of tool invites, silently does nothing and gets no feedback. THE HONEST MITIGATING FACTOR: the row's cursor is default, not grab, so the panel does not visually advertise dragging - the promise is in the markup, not in the pixels. That is why this is filed as a smaller row than it first looks, and why the fix could legitimately be to drop the attribute rather than to implement the drop. What I would not accept is leaving an attribute that says draggable on an element where drag does nothing, because it is a false statement the next agent or the next tool will believe. MEASURED LIVE ON A FRESH BUILD AND THE ROW IS WRONG AS FILED, in a way worth keeping. Dragging network-chart toward cpu-card-title does nothing, and it did nothing here too - both Playwright dragTo, which drives HTML5 drag-and-drop, and a raw mouse drag. But the drag was CROSS-PARENT and the panel refuses those by design: dragover marks only same-parent slots. Dragged between SIBLINGS the reorder works - network-down onto network-up swapped them, the list reading network-up,network-down before and network-down,network-up after. Every handler does run on the refused case: dragstart sets application/x-vigilia-layer, dragover is cancelled (defaultPrevented true), drop fires on the target row, and reorderLayer is reached. So the attribute is honest, the implementation is complete, and the row reported a deliberate restriction as a missing feature. THE REAL FINDING IS SMALLER AND MEASURED: the refusal is SILENT. Mid-gesture across parents, the target row carries the same vigilia-layer-row class as before, the cursor stays auto, and no title or aria-description anywhere in the editor mentions group, parent, reorder or drag. An author who drags a row toward another group is given nothing at all - no indicator, no cursor, no rule. That is the row worth keeping, and it is filed as vg-099. vg-096 is CONFIRMED by the same measurement: cursor is auto on a draggable row. MEASURED LIVE ON A FRESH BUILD AND THE ROW IS WRONG AS FILED, in a way worth keeping. Dragging network-chart toward cpu-card-title does nothing, and it did nothing here too - both Playwright dragTo, which drives HTML5 drag-and-drop, and a raw mouse drag. But that drag was CROSS-PARENT and the panel refuses those by design: dragover marks only same-parent slots. Dragged between SIBLINGS the reorder works - network-down onto network-up swapped them, the list reading network-up,network-down before and network-down,network-up after. Every handler does run on the refused case: dragstart sets application/x-vigilia-layer, dragover is cancelled (defaultPrevented true), drop fires on the target row, and reorderLayer is reached. So the attribute is honest, the implementation is complete, and the row reported a deliberate restriction as a missing feature. THE REAL FINDING IS SMALLER AND MEASURED: the refusal is SILENT. Mid-gesture across parents the target row carries the same vigilia-layer-row class as before the drag began, the cursor stays auto, and no title or aria-description anywhere in the editor mentions group, parent, reorder or drag. An author who drags a row toward another group is given nothing at all - no indicator, no cursor, no rule - and cannot tell which case they are in until nothing happens. Filed as vg-099.

 CROSS-LINK, deliberately NOT withdrawn, for the same reason as vg-056: the drag handler lives in a panel being replaced, but drag-to-reorder is a requirement that has to be carried into the composition panel. The polish spec records it and the redesign's section 3 keeps row-level commands, so the requirement is carried in docs - but this row is the only place the DOM advertises draggable with nothing consuming the drop, and that advertisement has to not survive the rewrite.

title: Three owners of 'list the document's tokens by name' is the shape that let vg-093 exist
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-093 and vg-102, which is the third round of the same defect in this repo. artboard-panel.ts:519, palette-manager/panel.ts:214 and chart-manager/panel.ts:324 each build their own option list over the same globals, and each is a place a label can come out as an id instead of a name. vg-088 fixed runs.ts, vg-093 fixed the colour dropdown beside it, vg-102 fixed four resolution lines, and the next surface to print a raw ref will be one of these three. That is the point: the defect has been fixed three times in individual surfaces and the shape that permits it is untouched. ONE OWNER of 'list the document's references by name' is the fix, and it is a design call rather than a patch — the three lists differ in what they filter and what they do on an unresolvable token, so consolidating them means deciding what the shared function owes each caller. Worth noting what the fix already established: a token the author has DELETED is the one case where the raw ref is correct, because it is the only identifier left, and that case is pinned by a test.

title: Every chart repaint asks the whole canvas to redraw, and charts re-apply their options 30 times a second
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-081, which is where that fix's work stopped. Two costs, both on the idle path, both now the largest that remains. (1) scene-fabric/src/chart-object.ts:227 — every ECharts rendered event asks Fabric for a full-canvas render, measured at 525 of 624 canvas renders across 3 s of doing nothing at all. One chart's animation frame redraws the whole document. (2) ChartManager.refresh re-applies every chart's option at the chart refresh rate whether or not that chart's data moved; the rate is the author's own chartRefreshRate control, which is why this is a decision and not a patch — the View menu offers 30 FPS and 1 FPS and an author who picks either is choosing this cost. vg-081 removed the TEXT side of the same argument and the idle cost fell 14x; this is the other half. LEFT ALONE because chart-manager/ belonged to another agent during that pass and because (2) touches a control the user sets. Worth pairing with the decision the user already has open on vg-086's menu, since that is where the rate is chosen.

title: A text object's Height field reports what it was told, not what is drawn
detail: FOUND WHILE CLOSING vg-098, and recorded because it has already cost one measurement this pass. With a text object carrying no authored box — which is what the editor inserts — the Size H field reported 220 while the drawn box stayed about 70. The field echoes the number it was given rather than reading what the object measures, so it is not a reliable probe for a box write. That mattered concretely: an agent verifying the vertical alignment control read the Size field and the canvas, the two disagreed, and the field was the one that was wrong — twice, because the control itself turned out to be dead. Two findings had to be told apart before either could be fixed, and a third party reading the same field would draw the same wrong conclusion. Worth noting it is adjacent to vg-057, which seeded both dimensions of the box from the object's own measured edge so a first Size edit produces a whole box; this is the read side of the same seam, and it is pre-existing rather than introduced here. THE ROW DOES NOT REPRODUCE, and the disagreement was the instrument rather than the field. On every text object reachable through the editor's own controls the field and the object's own edge agree - measured cpu-card-title 27 against 27.12, a freshly inserted caption 79 against 78.83 - and readField re-reads the object on every render rather than echoing anything. Fabric's getBoundingRect() is makeBoundingBoxFromPoints(this.getCoords()), and getCoords() reads a cache that assertBoxWidth and assertBoxHeight never invalidate, because they assign width and height directly rather than going through set (a set re-enters initDimensions). One object read 172.78 x 102.7 stale, and 141 x 28.12 after a single dirty = true; setCoords(). The 220-against-70 came from that. THE FIELD MUST KEEP SHOWING THE AUTHORED BOX - write puts the number the author types into vigiliaText.box, so a Size field reading the measured edge would name a number it is about to overwrite - but the box is stored UNSCALED, so a scaled text object draws a larger box and nothing said so. The field now says which is which where they differ: Size is the box the text was authored in (140 x 27). The object measures 280 x 54. STAYS OPEN because withdrawing is the user's call, alongside vg-087 which is also measured false. What is NOT uncertain is the real artefact underneath, filed as vg-112: the stale coordinate cache is not confined to a probe.

title: A theme that fails validation is answered 404, vanishes from the library, and the editor reports success
detail: MEASURED AT THE BOUNDARY while fixing vg-095, and the most serious thing either of those agents found. A theme sitting on disk whose metadata carries a stale locale key, or a stray backgroundMedia.scale, is answered 404 Theme not found, does not appear in the library listing, and the editor's boot-theme.ts openQuietly then opens a DIFFERENT theme and reports success naming that one. The validation issues are discarded at host/src/themes/store.ts:452-460. So there are three distinct outcomes collapsed into one silent one: the theme does not exist, the theme exists and is invalid, and the theme loaded - all of them read to an author as 'Theme not found' or as a success message about the wrong theme. The editor is the worse half, because it is the only one that says something untrue rather than nothing. AGENTS.md asks a 404 to name the cause it can prove (ADR-0018), and this one cannot prove it because the issues were thrown away before the response was built - which is precisely the fix: keep them, and answer a refused theme with what refused it. An author who hand-edited a theme, or who has a theme from a build whose schema has since tightened, currently has no way to learn any of that.

title: Sixteen of the envelope's shapes have no published counterpart, so a key added there is invisible to the schema
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-095. The decision note settles that the code owns the key list and the published schema is a hand-written contract held to it by a test - and that arrangement only covers what the schema publishes. Of the 23 shapes KNOWN_KEYS decides, only 7 appear in the schema at all. The other 16, including transform, node, textContent and the four chart settings shapes, live inside Fabric JSON that the schema validates as an opaque jsonValue, and fabric-envelope-schema-sync.test.ts forbids publishing the node tree. So a key added to one of those sixteen is invisible to anything validating against the published schema, which is the whole reason the two registries could disagree in the first place. The sync test catches disagreement where both sides speak; it is silent where only one does. Worth deciding whether that ceiling is accepted - a partially-describing published contract is a reasonable thing to publish, provided nobody reads it as total - or whether the sixteen need some other check. Also noted alongside: serialize.ts KEY_ORDER is a THIRD hand-written list of the same key names. It decides write order rather than membership, so it is not a second owner, but it moves with every key and nothing would notice if it stopped agreeing. AND THE GATE DID NOT CATCH IT WHEN IT HAPPENED, which is worth a line of its own. This row was briefly filed as "vg-vg-1101" — an id built by string-concatenating a formatted id — and backlog-check reported 21 items, all valid, without complaint. So the id check accepts a string that is not an id. That is a small hole in the gate every row depends on, since an id is what closes, what an artefact points at and what a commit trailer names, and it is filed by hand from a script often enough that the mistake is easy to make again.

title: Fabric's coordinate cache goes stale after the authored box is restored, so the selection frame, snapping and arrange work off the pre-pass size
detail: FOUND WHILE REFUTING vg-109, and it is the real artefact under that row's wrong measurement. assertBoxWidth and assertBoxHeight in scene-fabric/src/authored-box.ts:130,150 assign width and height DIRECTLY rather than through set, because a set re-enters initDimensions and would widen the object again - that is why they bypass it. But Fabric's aCoords is a separate cache, and bypassing set leaves it describing the PREVIOUS size. getBoundingRect() is makeBoundingBoxFromPoints(this.getCoords()), so everything that reads an object's box through the canvas reads a stale one: the SELECTION FRAME an author drags by, the SNAP positions the guides are computed against, and ARRANGE, which aligns selected objects to each other's edges. Measured: one text object read 172.78 x 102.7 stale, and 141 x 28.12 after a single dirty = true; setCoords(). A direct assignment or a setCoords after the restore would both be guesses until established, so the fix is to find where the pass leaves the object and mark it dirty once there - not to sprinkle setCoords at every reader. Left alone by the agent that found it because scene-fabric/ was held by another agent at the time, which is the disjoint-ownership rule working rather than a gap in it. This is worth its own row and its own dispatch: vg-089 already made a textbox's height a cache of its box, and this is the cost of that arrangement showing up somewhere the previous work did not measure.

title: The unit display options are four hardcoded English strings while every other list in the editor is Intl-derived
detail: REFUTED, and the refutation was already in the code when this row was filed. TWO claims; neither survives. (1) "ask Intl for these rather than write them". The probe was already run and recorded at ui-copy.ts:386-401, and re-run here independently: Intl.supportedValuesOf("unitDisplay") THROWS RangeError, Intl.DisplayNames.of("unitDisplay") throws RangeError (its six types are language, region, script, currency, calendar, dateTimeField), and Intl.supportedValuesOf("unit") is the 45 sanctioned UNITS OF MEASUREMENT (acre, byte, celsius), not the ways to display one. None of the four labels is a platform string: short and long are the platforms unitDisplay VALUES with no name attached, none is rejected outright (Intl.NumberFormat unitDisplay:"none" throws RangeError), and "Default" is the ABSENCE of the key rather than a word. (2) "every other list in the editor is Intl-derived, so a theme authored in another language meets four English words in the middle of an otherwise translated inspector". Two halves, both wrong. requirements.md §35 states "Multiple locales are not in scope for product UI copy; a theme declares the language its own text is written in" - the inspector is not translated, so there is no otherwise-translated middle for four English words to sit in. And the other lists are not Intl-derived either: ui-copy.ts carries artboardOrientations, artboardResolutions and fitModes as hand-written tables in the same object as the unit options (lines 378-385). THEME_LANGUAGES is the one genuinely Intl-labelled list, and its comment says why the LIST is hand-owned while the LABELS are not. WHAT THE ROW GOT RIGHT, and why it is still not a defect: the options were once written twice, in runs.ts and in the chart panel, so a rename fixed one and missed the other. That is fixed - the four options now live once in ui-copy.ts as unitDisplayOptions and both panels read them. The table is an OWNER, not a localisation debt. NO CODE CHANGED: the fix the row asks for would replace four correct strings with four undefined ones.

title: The reuse gate watchlists the repo-root scripts/ as a prefix, so a script directory under src/web/ is never gated
detail: FOUND WHILE LANDING THE FONT CATALOGUE GENERATOR, whose task brief instructed me to write a decision note first because scripts/ is on the gate watchlist and src/web/scripts/ is under it. Measured: it is not. reuse-gate.mjs:53 resolves every candidate path against the repo ROOT, so the watchlist entry scripts/ matches only a path whose repo-relative form begins scripts/ - and src/web/scripts/generate-font-trios.mjs does not. Piping that path into the gate returns 0 (allowed), while scripts/anything.mjs returns 2 (refused). So the second scripts/ directory in the repo is ungated and an agent can add a generator there without ever meeting the seven rungs. I landed the note anyway, because being told to is right and the gap is not mine to close silently, but the gate is not doing what its watchlist reads as saying. The fix is a judgement, not a typo: either add src/web/scripts/ as its own entry, or widen the matching so a bare directory name matches at any depth - which is the same shape as the bare-gitignore-pattern rule the repo already follows and would also catch a scripts/ under packages/. Worth deciding deliberately, because widening it means deciding what else under a path called scripts/ is a mechanism boundary.

title: Two of upstream registry titles disagree with the pairing document they point at, and one seeds the family the other names
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING THE FONT CATALOGUE DEDUPE, and both instances are upstream bugs, not ours - we ship a workaround for the class and this row is the durable record of it. At Fonttrio commit 8af7098ada0b90f076fbfe260244d11b05dd2403 the registry index contradicts its own pairing documents on two pairings out of 379, and in both cases the document is right. FIRST, the index is not one-to-one with its documents: it carries 380 entries for 379 distinct pairing names, because playfair-display-roboto is listed twice. Entry one is titled "Playfair Display Inter - Playfair Display + Inter + Inconsolata", entry two is titled "Playfair Display Roboto - Playfair Display + Roboto + Inconsolata", both carry the same url, and both resolve to one pairing document whose own title and cssVars name Roboto for the body role with an h1 weight of 800. So the index ships a title promising a family the record does not carry. SECOND, and independent of the duplicate: cormorant-garamond-proza-libre is titled "Cormorant Garamond Proza Libre" while its pairing document seeds Proza Libre for the heading, Cormorant Garamond for the body and JetBrains Mono for the mono - two family names run together with no separator and the mono family is absent from the title entirely. Its faces are correct, so the title is the whole defect there, where the first case is a duplicated record rather than a bad name. What made both findable is that nothing throws and the shape is valid: the catalogue is 379 unique ids of three faces each with correct weights and licences, so a count-based check passes. The test now asserts that a trio title ends with the three families it seeds, and it holds for 378 of 379 with this second case as the only exception - named in the test rather than waved through, so a third is red and a fix upstream is red too. Our workaround in docs/decisions/0024 is to treat the pairing document as the authority, keep the registry entry whose title matches it, require exactly one match and throw on none or two - so the duplicate resolves correctly today and a future contradiction stops the run instead of being guessed at. What is left for upstream is to drop the stale Inter entry or retitle it to the Roboto one the document serves, and to give cormorant-garamond-proza-libre a title that names its three families. Both are the same fix request and the same owner, which is why this is one row rather than two.
owner: upstream kapishdima/fonttrio registry.json at commit 8af7098ada0b90f076fbfe260244d11b05dd2403; workaround in src/web/scripts/generate-font-trios.mjs resolvePairings

title: The font catalogue spec says a facet keeps untagged entries, and the shipped query drops them
detail: FOUND IN TASK 4 REVIEW, on the spec's own wording, not on the code's. Two sentences in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-font-trio-catalog-design.md disagree with what ships: the Facets-are-derived paragraph (~:118-119) says "A pairing carrying no matching tag stays reachable by search: facets narrow the list, they never remove an entry from it", and the Verification > Browser paragraph (~:195) turns it into a gate, "a facet filters without hiding untagged entries". font-catalog-query.ts does the opposite and is right to: matchesFacet() returns values.includes(facet.value), so an untagged entry is dropped from the list. Strict filtering is the only reading under which "facets narrow the list" is true — keeping the union of tagged and untagged is the whole list, so the control would never filter anything. The operative guarantee the spec means is the narrower one, "stays reachable by search", and the code honours it in the one place it literally applies: queryFaces() keeps a face when ANY seeding trio carries the tag, since the face itself carries no tags. So the fix is a SPEC AMENDMENT, which is Task 8's line, and the browser gate has to move with it in the same edit or it asserts the opposite of the code and records a false pass. Task 6 should not be blocked on this: its picker ships strict filtering, which is correct either way.
owner: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-font-trio-catalog-design.md:118-119,195 (amendment and browser gate are Task 8's line)

title: Snapping candidates are root objects only, so a card no longer snaps to anything inside a neighbouring card
detail: FOUND IN REDESIGN PLAN 2 TASK 1 REVIEW. snap-manager/index.ts:124 builds its candidate list from canvas.forEachObject, which walks roots only. That was equivalent to every object while the starter was flat; now that the cards are groups, a card snaps to other CARDS and to loose objects but never to the parts inside a neighbouring card. Nothing green covers the new granularity - the four snapping specs fail on a harness lookup before reaching this code, so the behaviour is neither proven nor disproven. DECISION, not a defect: snapping a card to another card's outline is probably more useful than to an inner text baseline, and §175 requires a ported behaviour to keep its source's practical quality rather than merely its shape, so the answer is not obvious. It may also be right to offer inner guides deliberately once selection can enter a group (redesign plan 2 Task 4), which is when an author would want to align one card's title with another's. MEASURED 2026-10-04, and the gap this row named is closed: snapping.spec.ts now resizes a part INSIDE a card and records which family of lines the edge joined, as a test annotation rather than an assertion. Result: landed 956.55 aiming at the part line 960 and the card line 700, with 0 guide rows - a resized part snaps to NOTHING, not even to a neighbouring card, while the same gesture between two loose shapes snaps (that control is green). Whether parts SHOULD align to parts is not decided here and stays the user's.

title: group() leaves every member cached box stale, so a bounding rect read right after Ctrl+G is the pre-grouping box
detail:
AMENDED after an independent review measured every consumer, because the row as first filed would have sent a fixer to two safe sites and past the broken one.

grouping-manager/index.ts:185 builds `new Group(members)`, which rewrites each member into group-local coordinates and leaves Fabric's aCoords cache holding the pre-grouping box. setCoords() is the only thing that refreshes it.

MEASURED, ON A 1200x800 ARTBOARD: before group() outside=5 of 30; immediately after, outside=11 of 30, which is what the artboard panel reads; after renderAll() outside=10; only after a forced refresh does it return to 5. An author who groups two objects sees "11 of 30 outside" when 5 are.

TWO OF THE SEVEN CONSUMERS FIRST LISTED ARE NOT AFFECTED. snap-manager/bounds.ts:71 calls setCoords() on the line immediately before getBoundingRect(), so snapping is immune - measured, it returns the correct 421 rather than the stale 983. scene-fabric/src/glass.ts:584 likewise refreshes what it samples. arrange.ts reads getBoundingRect() with no refresh, but its members are no longer canvas roots after grouping, so reaching it needs a gesture the current UI does not offer - weaker than first claimed, not zero.

THE ONE CONSUMER THAT IS BROKEN is the crop count: scene-fabric/artboard-crop.ts:167 walks getObjects() recursively including children, so it reads the stale cache. Note that renderAll() only partially heals it, 11 to 10, because the glass sampler touches the card's frosted Rect but not its other six members - cpu-card-icon, -title, -value, -caption, -sparkline and -freq all stay stale.

ALSO RECORDED because it is incidental and therefore fragile: renderAll() does NOT refresh the cache by design. It appeared to, only because glass.ts:584 - an unrelated frosted-glass sampler - happens to call setCoords() on what it samples. A change to the glass renderer could silently reintroduce this, so nothing may cite "renderAll does not refresh" as a property of Fabric.

title: Fabric's derived per-character styles table is serialised into every saved text object
detail: FOUND WHILE CLOSING PLAN 1, by fixing a vacuous test rather than by driving the product. reference-theme.spec.ts's known-gap pin read only the TOP LEVEL of the saved scene, so after the starter became eight groups it reported no object carrying the table - on a document whose every text part carries one. Measured with a recursive read over a saved starter package: 30 objects carry a `styles` key. Owner: scene-fabric/src/persist.ts, beside removeRuntimeText, which strips Fabric's own text cache but not this. The authored equivalent is vigiliaText.runs and nothing reads `styles` back, so it is unrevivable state in a shareable artifact - the same class as the blob: src leak below. The pin is now marked test.fail so it stays recorded and turns red the day it is fixed; it had never been marked, which is why it stayed green while asserting nothing. NOT FIXED here: fixing serialisation is scene-fabric's own surface and this session was closing plan 1. MARKER VERIFIED 2026-10-04: the prior report said test.fail 'did not take on this Playwright version'. It does - measured on 1.63.0 from test-results/summary.json: status 'failed', expectedStatus 'failed', stats.expected 2, unexpected 0. Both pins report as the pinned failures they are and go red the day the gap closes, so no change to the marking was needed.

title: A packaged image object saves Fabric's crossOrigin flag, which is unrevivable runtime state
detail: FOUND WHILE CLOSING PLAN 1, by the same fix and in the same block as vg-129. The sibling pin - 'a packaged image object saves no runtime object URL' - enumerated scene.objects by index at the top level, so the image moved to index 10 when the starter was grouped and the pin stopped finding it. With a recursive read it reports exactly one object: envelope.scene.objects[10].crossOrigin. `src` is already stripped by SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES; `crossOrigin` is not, so it is a CORS-mode flag Fabric sets when it fetches an image and that means nothing to whoever opens the package. Same owner as vg-129 (scene-fabric/src/persist.ts) and the same class: editor-only state inside a shareable artifact. Marked test.fail for the reason given in vg-129. NOT FIXED here. MARKER VERIFIED 2026-10-04: the prior report said test.fail 'did not take on this Playwright version'. It does - measured on 1.63.0 from test-results/summary.json: status 'failed', expectedStatus 'failed', stats.expected 2, unexpected 0. Both pins report as the pinned failures they are and go red the day the gap closes, so no change to the marking was needed.

title: The spec requires visible notch and safe areas, and no task or row owns them
detail: FOUND IN REDESIGN PLAN 2 TASK 2 REVIEW. The redesign spec at section 2 requires "Device frame, notch and safe areas are visible and accounted for, because the display has them." No task in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-04-the-device-lens.md covers the notch or safe areas, the implementing agent declined them correctly as out of its brief, and the gap appears in NO backlog row and carries no "Discovered, not fixed:" trailer on the commit. Under AGENTS.md the trailer is the one path that survives compaction, so as shipped the requirement is simply lost. This is a controller error: the requirement was written into the spec without being given a task or a row. The device frame itself is an outline only and does not mask, which the reviewer confirmed is the honest direction - an author may pan artboard outside the screen and sees more than a device would rather than less. What is missing is the safe-area inset: a theme whose content sits under a notch or a rounded corner looks right in the editor and is cut on the device. That is exactly the preview-disagrees-with-the-phone failure this plan exists to remove, so it belongs with the device lens rather than as an orphan.

title: A menubar test that clicks a Base UI menu trigger stalls for 50 to 90 seconds under jsdom, timing out tests whose own code is fine
detail: FOUND IN REDESIGN PLAN 2 TASK 2 FIX ROUND 2, while reconciling the shell-layout.dom.test.ts / .tsx pair. In packages/editor/src/editor-shell/shell-layout.dom.test.tsx, once "opens every View setting's choices instead of toggling on a bare click" has run, requestAnimationFrame stops firing for every test after it in the file, so a test that awaits a frame dies on Test timed out in 20000ms rather than on anything about itself. MEASURED, by bisect with vitest -t rather than by reasoning: the two scroll tests in shell-layout.dom.test.ts pass alone (-t "returns the layer list", 1 passed in 4.8s); they pass with the immediately preceding test (-t "inserts the same objects|returns the layer list", 2 passed); and they fail with the View-menu test (-t "opens every View setting's choices|returns the layer list", 1 failed, 80.9s). The whole file run prints no unhandled error and no jsdomError, so this is NOT the vg-100 shape - nothing throws, the callbacks simply stop. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED beyond that bisect; the View-menu test opens two nested Base UI popups and calls layout.destroy() without unmounting either, and the file already works around Base UI under jsdom (a stubbed ResizeObserver, a stubbed Element.getAnimations, an afterEach Escape). NOT FIXED here because it is not the task: the work that exposed it was a file merge that turned out to be the wrong shape anyway - renaming the scroll tests to shell-layout-scroll.dom.test.ts removes the shadowing without moving them, which is what shipped. It matters because the file's own eighteen tests pass only because none of them awaits a frame, so the first person to add one - or to move the scroll tests across - gets a 20-second timeout pointing at their own test. Needs an owner; the surface to look at is what the View-menu test leaves mounted, not the scroll tests. || DIAGNOSED, NOT FIXED. The row asked for an owner and said the cause was not established; it is established now, and it is NOT what the row guessed. EVERY PART OF THE ROWS MECHANISM IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. (1) "requestAnimationFrame stops firing": it does not. Measured inside the View-menu test, between the menu click and the next read - requestAnimationFrame is still the native function, document.visibilityState is visible, document.hasFocus() false, and a requested frame arrives in 18ms. Frames were arriving the whole time. (2) "a later test that awaits a frame times out": the test that times out is NOT a later one - the View-menu test itself times out at 20s IN COMPLETE ISOLATION (-t "opens every View setting", 1 passed 16 skipped), so there is no cross-test contamination and no leaked mount to find. The row bisect was an artefact of the file being run in order. (3) "the whole file run prints no unhandled error and no jsdomError": true, and that is the actual shape - nothing throws. WHAT IS ACTUALLY HAPPENING, bisected by stamping every step of the test body: a bare setTimeout(0) BEFORE any click costs 2ms; the SAME setTimeout(0) immediately AFTER menubarEntry(root, uiCopy.menus.view).click() costs 58592ms. The next one costs 5ms and the one after 5ms, and rAF between them is 18ms. So it is a ONE-SHOT ~49-59 SECOND STALL INSIDE A SINGLE SYNCHRONOUS CLICK, not starvation and not a dead scheduler - everything after it is fast again. That is why a frame awaiting test still times out: it is not waiting for a frame that will not come, it is waiting out a stall that a macrotask boundary is what finally drains. THE CLICK PATH IS BASE UI POPUP MOUNT, and two candidates were eliminated by measurement rather than reasoning: removing the Element.prototype.getAnimations stub does NOT fix it (27.3s with the stub gone vs 25.2s with it), and BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED - Base UIs own documented global, declared in its global.d.ts and read at the one line of useAnimationsFinished that decides whether to call fnToExecute directly - does NOT fix it either. Both were the obvious answers and both are wrong. STILL NOT FIXED because the remaining candidate needs a real bisect of Base UIs popup mount under jsdom, which is a different piece of work from this row, and I would be guessing past the measurements. NO SOURCE CHANGED. WHAT WOULD FINISH IT: instrument the click itself rather than around it - time the synchronous span inside ShellMenuBar/Menu.Trigger onClick - and the stall will show up as a long synchronous block with a name on it. The two candidates above are the ones already ruled out, so the next agent should not re-run them. || TITLE CORRECTED 2026-10-07, BY PLAN 6, because the old title asserted the mechanism the detail above refutes: it said jsdom stops firing requestAnimationFrame, and the measurements show frames arriving throughout. Anyone searching this register for a slow or timing-out menubar test was looking for starvation and would not have found a stall. The measurement that prompted the correction: at 9d334e09 the whole file run in isolation fails 1 test, and at 79f9a0b0 it fails 3, at 91s / 96s / 118s / 67s against a 20s timeout - so the same one-shot stall now makes the FULL unit suite red, not just a single file run in order. Nothing about the diagnosis above changed. RE-MEASURED BY PLAN 7 TASK 4.2 at `5a2f051a`, file-only run of `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx`: **21 tests, 20 passed, 1 failed**, file wall time about 6 minutes. Every non-menu test ran in 25-2035 ms; the five menu-driven ones took **43.5 s, 94.5 s, 109.5 s, 67.7 s and 29.4 s**, and the 94.5 s one -- `inserts the same objects from the Insert menu as the Add pane offers` -- is the single failure, `Error: Test timed out in 20000ms`. **That a test stalling past 20 s can still PASS is consistent with the stall being synchronous rather than a slow call**, which is this row's own diagnosis: the timeout timer cannot fire until the block ends. Reported as consistent with the record, not as a new mechanism.

title: Five more tests read the camera as a constant, found by changing the default camera after vg-136 was fixed
detail: FOUND BY THE SABOTAGE RUN AGAINST vg-136, which is why it is filed rather than never noticed: setting DEFAULT_DISPLAY_LENS to `9:19.5` and rebuilding makes five more tests fail, and all five are the SAME defect class vg-136 just fixed - a measurement that reads the camera as a constant - and all five are PRE-EXISTING and outside vg-136's diff. THREE fail inside `assertBlur`. glass-probe.ts:261 builds the sampled band as `bandTop + Math.max(8, Math.floor(height * 0.25))`: the 0.25 term scales with the camera because `height` is the panel's device box, but the 8 is a literal DEVICE-row floor, so the two halves of one expression disagree about which space they are in. glass-authoring.spec.ts:207, :323 and :420 all land there. TWO fail on snapping.spec.ts's GUIDE_ROWS_PRESENT (50) and GUIDE_ROWS_ABSENT (20), which count device rows carrying the guide colour. The file's own comment says 'the artboard is 600 scene px tall, so a real guide covers hundreds of device rows' - hundreds AT THE ZOOM IT WAS WRITTEN FOR. At the artboard's full height in device rows that count is 600 * zoom, so the 50 floor is a floor on the camera in the same way RAW_TOLERANCE was, and reference-theme.spec.ts:1595 fails on the same measurement. THE POINT IS NOT FIVE FAILURES, IT IS THE SHAPE. vg-136 repaired three tests that read the camera as a constant and proved the repair under a changed camera; this row is the remainder of that same audit, and it exists because the audit's instrument - change the default camera and re-run - found more than the row it was run for. The device lens is not the first thing to move that camera: every one of these would break again on the next zoom control, the next lens, or a window resize, and none of them names the camera in its failure message the way the repaired snapping assertions now do. NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: it is a different set of files from vg-136's three (glass-probe.ts is a shared helper read by several specs, and the guide-row constants sit among tests vg-136 did not touch), and it is a scope decision rather than a defect on its own. Worth deciding together whether the honest repair is per-constant derivation from liveZoom, or one shared helper that converts a scene measurement into the device pixels a given assertion is about - the second would stop the next row being needed. MEASURED on this Windows box by setting DEFAULT_DISPLAY_LENS to 9:19.5, rebuilding the editor, and running the three specs under playwright.config.ts. Not verified on any other camera: portrait is the one that was measured, and Fit at 0.98 passes these today.

title: A text side handle does not snap at the portrait lens, so an author resizing text gets no guide at all
detail: FOUND BY THE SABOTAGE RUN AGAINST vg-137, and it is NOT a test reading the camera wrong - this one is the product. Set DEFAULT_DISPLAY_LENS to 9:19.5, rebuild, and tests/e2e/snapping.spec.ts "resizing geometry snaps a side handle onto a guide" lands 100.0 scene units from the line it was aimed 3 client px short of. 100 units is a quarter of the 600-tall artboard: that is not a missed snap, it is no snap at all, and at the default lens the same gesture passes. Measured on the same run where every other snapping test passes at both lenses, so the fixture, the gesture and the camera plumbing are all fine. CONFIRMED IT IS NOT THE TOLERANCE: vg-137s derived bound at this lens is 2.92 scene units and the landing is 100, so no tolerance question can be behind it. The gesture arrives as object:resizing on a canonical width rather than as a scale - Fabric gives a text box changeWidth side controls - and that path is the one that does not reach a snap line under this camera. Whether the side-handle resize path consults the camera at all is the thing to check, and it is a one-symbol question in the resizing side of snap-manager, not a test change. VERIFIED PRESENT ONLY AT 9:19.5; NOT VERIFIED ON ANY OTHER LENS, portrait is the one measured, and landscape is the default so the mainline gate is green and does not see it. This is the shape vg-137 fixed the test side of: a lens or a resize that moves the camera changes what the snapping path is asked to do, and this is where it shows.
owner: packages/editor/src/snap-manager (the resizing side of the gesture path)

title: The player fit-mode spec intermittently measures nothing inside fit-contain, in a suite that gates merges
detail: FOUND ON THE FULL GATE WHILE CLOSING vg-119, and it is not this sweep: nothing in b29ccc21..HEAD touches display-fabric.spec.ts, background-media.ts or anything they read. MEASURED: the serial full gate collected 410 and reported 409 passed / 1 failed, the one being tests/e2e/display-fabric.spec.ts draws each fit mode, and every icon, in its own box - "fit-contain drew nothing inside its own box", expected > 0.05, received 0. Re-run on its own, --repeat-each 3, that is 6 collected and 6 passed, so it is an intermittent and not a standing red. The claim is the INK, measured inside the box the fit mode is supposed to fill, and a reading of exactly 0 is what a frame that had not painted yet looks like - the same class as the chart-palette status race vg-131 recorded, where an action arrives before the surface has settled. NOT DIAGNOSED: whether it is the player waiting for a decode, the probe sampling before the first paint, or a genuine intermittent in the fit path is not established, and the one thing established is that 3 samples is not enough to call it fixed either. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: --repeat-each 20 on that spec with the ink reading captured per run, which separates a paint that is late from a fit that is wrong in a way that only sometimes shows. The base was green - STATUS.md at b29ccc21 records 252 passed 0 failed 0 flaky - so this appeared somewhere between there and here, and that is not narrowed to this sweep because this sweep did not touch the surface.

title: A video frame in the host media spec is an intermittent that fails at the baseline too
detail: FOUND WHILE CLOSING DEVICE-LENS PLAN 2 TASK 5, in the full host suite rather than by driving the product. tests/e2e/host-media.spec.ts has a video-frame test that fails intermittently: 3 of 5 samples with the Task 5 commit f49f632b, 1 of 3 at its parent, and it fails at the clean baseline too, so it is NOT a regression from that task and NOT this plan's. MEASURED on both sides rather than assumed, per the repo rule that a single sample is not a measurement. A flaky spec in a suite that gates merges is a real defect whatever its cause, and the cause is not established: video decode timing under a loaded, shared box is the obvious candidate and has not been confirmed. Needs an owner and a determinism fix; the surface to look at is the video-frame readiness wait, not the assertion.

title: The artboard panel crop figure lags during a drag, though it catches up on release
detail: FOUND WHILE CLOSING DEVICE-LENS PLAN 2 TASK 5, then AMENDED by its own task review, which found the controller had filed it too narrowly. ORIGINALLY FILED AS: the panel recomputes its outside-object count only on render(), so the number lags while an object is dragged past the edge - a transient cosmetic lag identified by reading, not by driving. THE REVIEW SHOWS THAT IS NOT THE WHOLE OF IT. The bleed control (selection-inspector/bleed.ts:94) fires object:modified, and its own comment claims the artboard panel is thereby told the scene moved - but the panel has NO canvas subscription at all. sizeNote.textContent is assigned from exactly one place, render() at artboard-panel.ts:336, and render() is called from only three sites in the editor: mount, #setArtboard, and #deletePalette. So ticking the mark leaves the figure reading "1 of 1 objects are now outside" until the author changes the artboard or deletes a palette token. THAT IS NOT A LAG: an explicit author action whose whole purpose is to change the number produces no visible change at all and never catches up, which is the feature being invisible on the surface it is judged on. The two tests that appear to cover the refresh do not - one asserts only that fire was called with object:modified, and its name claims the outcome; the other covers the panel arithmetic by calling panel.render() BY HAND, which is the call the product does not make.  PARTIALLY FIXED BY TASK 5, and the remainder is exactly this row. Task 5 added the subscription that closes the mark case - panel now listens to object:modified and refreshes the note through a single refreshNote writer - and that fires on drag RELEASE, so the figure catches up on mouse-up. THE REMAINDER IS THE DURING-DRAG CASE: Fabric fires object:moving per frame while a drag is in progress and object:modified only on release, and the panel does not subscribe to object:moving. So the figure is stale for the duration of a drag and correct afterwards. NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY: subscribing to object:moving would be a per-frame recompute of a figure that already converges on release, and that is a product call about whether a live figure during a drag is worth a per-frame recompute, not an oversight. This row exists to hold the question open rather than to assert the lag is a defect. FIXTURE if it is taken on: add object:moving to the panel existing subscription array and confirm the figure tracks the drag without a full render - refreshNote was built to be cheap enough for exactly this, which is why the mark case did not have to be.

title: The host player units spec times out on the real host, and does so in isolation too
detail: FOUND AT THE DEVICE-LENS PLAN 2 BOUNDARY, in the full e2e gate run against a verified-current bundle. tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts, "hosted player over the real host :: shows a temperature in the units this PC chose, converting nothing else" times out at 30s. IT REPRODUCES IN ISOLATION - it was among the six of a prior 16-failure run that still failed when re-run alone - so this is a real defect and not machine load. NOT THIS PLAN'S: device-lens plan 2 touched the artboard clip, the display switch, the new-theme chooser, arc and wedge shapes, and the deliberate-bleed flag, and none of them touches unit formatting or the host player's reading pipeline. MEASURED CONTEXT: the same boundary run was 260 passed / 1 failed / 160 skipped against a pre-plan baseline of 236 / 17, so the suite is otherwise in good shape and this is the last red. The failure is a 30s TIMEOUT rather than a wrong value, which points at a readiness wait on the host stream rather than at the conversion itself - the same shape as vg-141, the host-media video-frame intermittent, and the two may share a cause on this box. Cause not established. Needs an owner: establish whether the host never delivers the reading or the player never repaints on it.

title: The reuse gate is satisfied forever by any older note claiming the same directory
detail: FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 3, TASK 1. scripts/reuse-gate.mjs answers "has any note in docs/decisions/ ever claimed this path", not "is this change argued for". 0005-chart-glow-is-skipped-pending-an-artboard-unit.md claims src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/charts/ and 0022/0023 claim src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/theme/, so a first write to either returns EXIT=0 before any note about that change exists - measured with printf '{"tool_input":{"file_path":"src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/charts/settings-fields.ts"}}' | node scripts/reuse-gate.mjs. The README calls the check deliberately blunt and presence-only, so that a weak note must be caught in review; this is a different property: the gate is a one-shot latch per directory, so it guards the first change to a boundary and nothing after it. Whether a per-change claim, a staleness rule, or nothing at all is wanted is a design decision, not a fix.

title: The rebuild journey's memory-rings test takes 45 to 52 seconds against Playwright's 30 second default, and three of its siblings sit at 27 to 28
detail: FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 3 TASK 9, running the rebuild spec as its browser gate. MEASURED, and pre-existing: at the previous commit (e37f0b51) the test reaches its vg-145 assertion in 52.1s, and with this task's fix it passes in 45.3s, so the work is real and the budget is simply smaller than it is. THREE SIBLINGS ARE NEAR THE EDGE AT THE SAME TIME, which is what makes this a row rather than one test's business: the wordmark test 27.0s, the GPU card 27.0s and the storage bar 27.9s, against a 30s default that playwright.rebuild.config.ts does not override. A loaded box then turns any of them red for a reason that has nothing to do with the document. FIXED IN PART AND ONLY IN SCOPE: the memory-rings test carries test.slow() (this task had to make it green), and the other three were left as they were, because raising a suite-wide timeout is a decision about this spec's own budget rather than a task-9 edit. WHAT THE ROW IS ASKING FOR: either a project-level timeout in playwright.rebuild.config.ts, or test.slow() on each journey test, chosen deliberately rather than by whichever one goes red next.

title: The json reporter writes to one shared test-results/summary.json unless the run also passes --reporter=json, and a plan that names only the env var never notices
detail: FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 4 TASK 3, trying to keep this session's report out of the shared test-results/summary.json. THE ROW'S FIRST VERSION OVERSTATED IT AND IS CORRECTED HERE, because the controller reproduced both sides rather than accepting one. Measured, first run (the agent's): PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_NAME=<temp>/probe.json npx playwright test composition-panel --workers=1, with NO --reporter flag - the probe file was never created and test-results/summary.json carried that run. Measured, second run (the controller's, same spec, same machine): the same env var with --reporter=json on the command line - the probe file WAS created, and test-results/summary.json was not written at all. CAUSE, named to the line: src/web/playwright.config.ts:60-65 configures the json reporter as ["json", { outputFile: "test-results/summary.json" }]. A CLI --reporter replaces that list, so the CLI json reporter runs with no outputFile and the environment variable applies; without the flag the config's reporter runs, its own outputFile wins, and the variable has nothing to apply to. So the variable is not inert - it is inert WITHOUT THE FLAG, which is the condition every instruction this repo writes omits. WHAT IT COSTS: test-results/summary.json is one unqualified path, plans 3 and 4 both tell agents to route the JSON through the environment variable and neither says to pass --reporter=json, and on a machine where two sessions run the same suite an agent that obeys without the flag reads a file it did not write and reports another run's numbers as its own. STILL OPEN because the hazard is real once the flag is dropped, and the two candidate fixes are a decision: name --reporter=json in the instruction - cheap, keeps the collision for anyone who forgets - or drop outputFile from the config, which makes the variable apply unconditionally but moves where every session's report lands. The controller has corrected the instruction in plan 4's briefs and in its own session memory; the config is untouched.

title: Two closed plans still sit in the live plans directory, so the directory no longer answers what is executable
detail: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-03-groups-in-the-starter.md (plan 1) and 2026-10-04-the-device-lens.md (plan 2) are both closed per STATUS.md and both still live, while plan 3 was archived. plans/README.md:5-6 states the rule: move a completed or superseded plan to archive/ once no active or queued plan depends on them. Measured before filing: neither plan file is referenced by any current doc, script or test outside the gitignored .superpowers/sdd/ ledgers, which are historical records of the run rather than dependencies — the only live references to plan 1 are to its workspace path (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-03-groups-in-the-starter/), which moving the plan file does not disturb. Found by the controller while preparing plan 4 Task 11, which owns the archive move for plan 4 but not for these two. EXTENDED WHEN PLAN 4'S FILE WAS ARCHIVED (2026-10-10): the census was taken then. Seventeen plans sit in docs/superpowers/plans/, of which three are queued (settings-and-appearance, iconography-and-copy, design-md-replaces-the-bible) and fourteen are closed, including this redesign series' own plan 1 (2026-10-08-gates-and-the-control-set.md) and plan 2 (2026-10-08-the-shell-and-the-rail.md). Plan 4's file (2026-10-08-the-panes.md) was archived although two queued plans name it, because both references are prose pointers - a sequence paragraph and a boundary clause - spelling the bare filename and never a path, which is this row's own test for referenced rather than depended-on. The two rules also disagree and the directory matches neither: plans/README.md:5-6 says to move a completed or superseded plan to archive/ unconditionally, while AGENTS.md conditions it on no active or queued plan depending on them.

title: The asset panel is a list of files, and assets are placed objects: insert belongs in the Add pane and replace on the selection
detail:
Raised by the user on 2026-10-07, ruling that the Assets pane should not exist. The argument, which the code supports: an asset is not a document object with its own identity to browse — it becomes a layer when it is placed, and the layer tree shows scene objects, not files. Measured here: the layer tree has no asset concept at all (no reference to assets in editor-shell/layer-tree.ts), and replace exists only inside the panel (asset-manager/panel.ts:28-37 build the replace input and button, :174-186 the replace path). So the user is naming two moves rather than one deletion — insert already has a home in the Add pane, and replace has none on the selection today and would be new work on the object context menu or the dock toolbar. Both the import path and the reference-count question (assetReferencedBy) have to survive wherever replace lands, or a file the theme still uses becomes removable. EXTENDED 2026-10-07 after the user reported from earlier testing that some assets appear as layers and some do not, and asked why the asset needs a place of its own when an asset already is a layer object. Measured, and it answers the report exactly: asset-manager/index.ts:21-31 defines four asset kinds — image (png/jpg/jpeg/webp), svg, video (mp4/webm) and font (woff2/woff/ttf/otf) — and isPlaceable at asset-manager/panel.ts:232-236 accepts only image and svg. So importing a file does two different things chosen by its type, silently: a PNG is declared and then placed, dropping an object on the canvas, while an MP4 or a font is declared only and appears in the asset panel and nowhere else. Import never says which of the two happened. On why a separate place exists at all: the relation is not one-to-one and has three cases. One asset to many objects — assetReferencedBy at asset-manager/index.ts:415 walks every object at any depth precisely because of this, and remove refuses while any of them holds the id. One asset to zero objects — a video or a font can never become an object, because no object kind exists for them, so the layer tree has nothing to hang management on. And one asset to no object at all — Artboard.backgroundMedia at renderer-core/src/theme/document.ts:133-138 is assetId plus fit on the artboard itself, which is what the reference theme full-bleed photograph is. Cases two and three are why a panel exists; case one, the common one, is what this row already rules should move onto the layer. Consequence that has to be decided with the removal: remove, including its refusal while referenced, is reachable only from that panel today, so without a home for it a font imported once can never be deleted.
EXTENDED 2026-10-10 BY PLAN 4 TASK 12 (the plan's closing comparison). WHAT LANDED (the insert half): the Add pane renders insertGroups() as its own React surface (panes/add/add-pane.tsx, Task 3, 96099ba8), so a card unit, a primitive, a chart family and Text are placed from the pane; and the declared-asset list this row requires to survive the move is inside Add — the file path is the pane's (panes/add/file-section.tsx, Task 4, c8dc0b1a) with the control set's select (Task 10, 80facf67), before which the row's own panel is gone: createAssetPanel was deleted and grep -rn createAssetPanel over src/web/packages/editor/src and src/web/tests returns nothing. WHAT DID NOT (the replace half, which is why the row stays open): a selection-scoped replace does not exist on any surface. Re-pointing one chosen object's image to another file was never the panel's byte replacement — the panel swapped a declared asset's bytes for every use of it — and no dock action, context-menu entry or inspector field offers the selection-scoped form today. It is a new capability, not a behaviour to preserve, so §2.3's no-drift constraint forbids building it inside this rewrite. Remaining work when it is taken: place the action where the selection's own actions live (the dock toolbar or the object context menu), and keep remove and its refusal reachable for the asset kinds that can never become an object (video, font), which is the consequence this row already states.

title: Importing a file silently does one of two different things, and only the file type decides which
detail: FOUND BY AN AGENT READING THE CODE, NOT BY THE USER, and corrected on 2026-10-07: this row was first filed attributing it to the user testing report, and that attribution was wrong — the user imported JPEG images only and their report is vg-156. This row stands on its own reading. asset-manager/index.ts:21-31 defines four asset kinds — image (png/jpg/jpeg/webp), svg, video (mp4/webm), font (woff2/woff/ttf/otf) — and isPlaceable at asset-manager/panel.ts:232-236 is the two-element allowlist image or svg. add() at panel.ts:114-183 imports, tests isPlaceable, and only then places via manager.placeImage at :211. So importing a PNG is declared and placed, dropping a new object on the canvas, while importing an MP4 or a font is declared only: the canvas is untouched, no layer appears, and nothing in the pane distinguishes the two outcomes. Whether that is a defect at all is arguable, because a font is not supposed to be a layer, and the honest part of the finding is only that the two outcomes are indistinguishable to the author. It shares a fix site with vg-154 but is not the user report and should be judged on its own or withdrawn.

title: Every imported JPEG was placed on the canvas, but only some of them appeared in the layer panel
detail: Reported by the user on 2026-10-07 from hands-on testing, and restated by them the same day after an agent mis-filed it: they imported JPEG images only, not a mix of file types, and every one appeared on the canvas, but only some produced a row in the layer panel. The ones that did not were missing from the panel while present on the canvas. The user does not know whether it has been fixed since. THE CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED, which is why this is a row rather than a fix on the fly. What reading ruled out, each a real mechanism rather than a guess: not isPlaceable (asset-manager/panel.ts:232-236), because every JPEG is kind image and so is placeable; not the storage path, because placeImage (asset-manager/index.ts:60-91) declares and places together and importImage (image-manager/index.ts:105-115) calls canvas.add(image) at the root unconditionally, since placeImage does not set withoutAdding; not the listing filter, because isListed (layer-tree.ts:112) excludes only excludeFromExport objects, namely the artboard plate, the clip and the crop frame, and no import sets that flag; not a row cap or virtualisation, because layer-panel.tsx renders every row and contextRows (:231-240) builds a dimming set rather than a filter; and not a missing trigger, because bridge.ts:124-130 subscribes object:added and object:removed to notify(), which re-projects. Every mechanism readable says the row should appear, which is exactly why a reproduction is needed rather than more reading. What the reproduction has to vary: how many files were imported in one session, whether a group was entered or selected when each import happened, whether files went in one at a time or several quickly, and whether the document already held many objects. Worth noting for whoever takes it: no browser spec covers this path at all, because no case in tests/e2e asserts that a placed image produces a layer row, so nothing would have caught it and nothing will catch a regression.

title: Deleting an object that lives inside a group leaves the right column still describing it
detail: FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 4 TASK 10, driving the built editor in Chromium. MEASURED at 42169371: after deleting cpu-card from group-cpu-card through the layer panel, its layer row is gone while the right column keeps its form and never renders [data-vigilia-nothing-selected]; deleting a top-level object does empty it. Cause NOT ESTABLISHED, and two readings fit the measurement. Either the columns binding is stale, or the delete stopped at the layer projection and the object is still in the document - in which case selection-inspector/index.ts:346-353, which keeps the last object while objectById still finds its id, is behaving exactly as designed and the defect is the removal instead. Distinguishing those two is the first step, not a fix. THE SECOND READING IS WHY THIS IS WORTH ITS OWN ROW: if the object survives a delete, this is the same disagreement between the layer trees rows and the documents objects as vg-156, the users report that every imported JPEG was placed on the canvas but only some appeared in the layer panel, seen from the opposite direction.

title: Three verification bullets plan 4 wrote are not delivered as tests
detail: FOUND BY THE WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW of the composition-panel plan (`2026-10-06-the-composition-panel.md`), over commits f8197102..af2d3e49, which ran after the plan closed because its workspace held no review diffs while plan 2s held eleven. title: The Document pane still sets a panel marker named style, and the reason it was kept has expired
detail: FOUND BY THE WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW of the composition-panel plan (`2026-10-06-the-composition-panel.md`). selection-inspector/style.ts:83 sets root.dataset["vigiliaPanel"] = "style" on what is now the left columns Document pane references panel. editor.spec.ts:2152 reads that value, so it works, but the name says Style tab for a panel that is not one. title: An unlanded plan removes the menubars Insert and View menus, and nothing queues it
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5S PLAN AUTHOR and left for the controller by that plans Out of scope section rather than fixed inside it. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-03-editor-left-column-and-header.md is 19.8 KB of unlanded plan whose Task 4 removes the Insert and View menus from the menubar. That removal is one half of the superseded frontend redesign, which ruled those menus leave the header (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-frontend-redesign-design.md:383). It matters now rather than later because plan 5 gives insertGroups() a fourth rendering (the + popover beside the Add pane, the Insert menu and the canvas context menu), and this plan is the one that would take the second of those away. ITS OWN STATUS IS UNESTABLISHED: whether any of its tasks landed under another plan is not measured, and neither is whether its remaining tasks are still the shape its file describes. The neighbouring bookkeeping defect is vg-152, the same archive-versus-queue rule applied to plans 1 and 2, which are closed but still live in the plans directory. MEASURED IN PART BY PLAN 5S WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW, which is the measurement this row said was missing: the unlanded plans Task 3 is now actively false rather than merely unqueued. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-03-editor-left-column-and-header.md:229 says to create editor-shell/insert-popover.tsx, which plan 5 created at 577c44e5 with a different contract, taking an anchor ref that the older plans Produces does not mention. Worse, that plans verification says to delete insertMenuGroups, insertMenuEntry and the test inserts the same objects from the Insert menu as the Add pane offers (shell-layout.dom.test.tsx:209-216, :286, :843), and plan 5 deliberately keeps and extends all three. So restoring that plan as written would now delete tests that a closed plan made load-bearing. Everything else about that plans state remains unmeasured, and the row stays open.

title: CARD_LIBRARY owns the card-unit vocabulary and the ownership map never names it
detail: FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 5, TASK 4, and deliberately left out of that plan by its own ownership ruling: no new map row in this task, file the gap instead. Measured at 31956d2c, docs/architecture/ownership.md names neither CARD_LIBRARY nor uiCopy.cardLibrary. The file card-library.ts appears once, at :114, in the row for minting ids for a copy, where it is a USER of createWidgetIdAllocator rather than the owner of anything. That makes this an instance of exactly what the map warns about in its own preamble: a module that owns a vocabulary but appears nowhere is invisible, so nothing warns a reader not to decide the membership somewhere else. What CARD_LIBRARY decides is which eight units exist and, with uiCopy.cardLibrary, what each is called, and plan 5 makes that vocabulary load-bearing for the reference composition: after task 5 a starter card carries a stamp whose widgetName is that vocabularys word. The plans ruling is that the stamp needs no new row because cardGroup gains a parameter rather than a decision, and that is sound; the missing row is a separate gap about a module that already owned an enumeration before plan 5 touched it. The shape-list precedent the map does carry is new-object-defaults.ts plus SHAPE_KINDS and uiCopy.shapeKinds, which is the model a row here would follow.

title: The spec's primitive list names video, and no object kind can carry one
detail: FOUND WHILE CLOSING PLAN 5, and left for the controller by that plan's Out of scope section rather than fixed inside it. The spec's §5 primitives bullet sells the Add pane as offering text, shape, chart, image and video "exactly as today" (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-dashboard-authoring-design.md:362-370), but the fifth of those cannot become an object at all: isPlaceable at asset-manager/panel.ts:232-236 is the two-element allowlist image or svg, so an MP4 is declared in the asset manager and never placed, and no Fabric object kind exists for one. A reader who took §5 literally would look for a video button in the Add pane and find none. THE SUBJECT HERE IS THE SPEC SENTENCE, NOT THE ASSET PANEL: the same allowlist is already recorded from the import side by vg-155 (importing a file silently does one of two things, and only the file type decides which) and inside vg-154's extension (a video or a font can never become an object), and neither of those says the spec promises a primitive the product does not deliver. It shares vg-154's fix site; the user's own 2026-10-07 report is vg-156, which is about JPEGs and is unrelated. Plan 5 added no asset button to any surface, because doing so would take vg-154's decision on an agent's hand. The open question is which side is wrong: §5's list corrected to the primitives that exist, or video gaining an object kind, which is vg-154's question.

title: The settings page's disk dropdown is missing when the suite runs it under load
detail: FOUND AT PLAN 5'S CLOSE-OUT BROAD GATE, in the full browser suite rather than by driving the product. tests/e2e/host-settings.spec.ts:249, 'asks a theme's disk question once, and remembers the answer', failed with locator('select[data-group="system-disk"]') element(s) not found after a 5000 ms timeout, the spec itself taking 23.9 s. IT PASSES ALONE: re-run in isolation on the same rebuilt bundle with --project=desktop-host --workers=1, it is 1 expected / 0 unexpected in 21.4 s. Two samples, opposite outcomes, so the failure is environment- or ordering-sensitive and is NOT a defect this plan caused — plan 5 touched the editor shell, the card library, the layer projection and two docstrings in scene-fabric, and none of those is the settings page or its device enumeration. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED, and the two readings are a real cross-test interference (the desktop-host project shares one host app dir across host-media, host-player and host-settings, and the disk list is read live from the machine) or plain load (the select did not populate inside its 5 s window while the whole suite ran serially). The surface to look at first is what populates [data-group="system-disk"], and whether an earlier spec in the same project mutates the host fixture's directory.

title: The archives verified rows are never validated, so the check-and-artefact rule is unenforced
detail: FOUND WHILE CLOSING PLAN 5, by moving a row to the archive and then asking what checked it. scripts/backlog-check.mjs:45 hardcodes FILE as docs/product/backlog.jsonl and :171 reads only that file, and nothing else in the repo reads backlog-archive.jsonl at all: a grep for the name across scripts/, .claude/ and the tree returns no reader. THE TWO-FILE SPLIT IS WHAT MAKES THIS A GAP RATHER THAN A CHOICE.
