A row acquires state verified at the moment it leaves the live file, so the validators verified-only rules, the check naming a word from the rows own title and artefacts naming a commit that resolves and is an ancestor of HEAD, never run on any row. Measured this session: a row carrying neither check nor artefacts, appended to the archive, leaves backlog-check reporting all valid and exiting 0. The scripts self-test still passes because it exercises check() against fixtures rather than against either file, which is why this has not shown up. AGENTS.md calls the check the stronger of the two enforcements and says neither substitutes for the other, and 103 archived verified rows have never had either run against them. NOT FIXED HERE: pointing the validator at both files is a gate change with its own blast radius, since archived rows that fail it would need adjudicating one at a time, and this session is closing plan 5 rather than opening that.

title: A stamp on a nested group is unchecked, because the walk skips every group
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5S WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW, over 5230778c..194f9e5a. Plan 5s Review Focus 1 says a stamp that leaked onto a child is pinned in Task 5 and Task 6. The Task 5 half pins only the non-group children: card-library.test.ts:186 is `if (object["type"] === "Group") continue;`, which skips every group at every depth, so a nested group carrying a stamp is asserted nowhere in the tree. The Task 6 half cannot cover it either: layer-tree.test.ts:836-837 filters `row.kind === "group" && row.depth > 0` and expects length 0, but the starter has no nested group at all, so that assertion is structurally empty and could only fail if a card legitimately gained one. WHAT IS REALLY PINNED, and was proved by the reviews own break: a stamp on a non-group part, the panel and every part inside a card, does fail when removed. The gap is the nested-group half of RF1 and nothing else. NOT FIXED IN PLAN 5 because the honest fix is not another assertion of the same shape: with no nested group in the starter, any such assertion is unfalsifiable, so closing this means deciding to walk the projection against a constructed document that does have one, which is a test-design decision rather than a correction.

title: The pin that the builders words agree with the library is a tautology
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5S WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW. Plan 5s Task 5 Constraints say the task adds a pin that the unit word in the builders and the unit word in CARD_LIBRARY agree, naming the failure mode a unit label re-spelled in the builder instead of read from uiCopy.cardLibrary. The test cannot detect that: CARD_LIBRARY is built from uiCopy.cardLibrary (card-library.ts:105-138, `label: uiCopy.cardLibrary.time` and so on) and the builders pass the same uiCopy.cardLibrary references (new-fabric-theme-cards.ts:99-101, :386, :401). Both sides resolve one object, so the comparison holds for any value that object ever takes and a re-spelled literal in a builder would have to be introduced on the library side too to go unnoticed, which is not the failure mode. What the test does pin is real and was proved by a break: the stamp present at all, and its widgetId. The precedent the plan cited is no stronger: new-object-defaults.test.ts:626 reads uiCopy.shapeKinds on both sides as well. The cross-path agreement that IS sound is the one Task 6 added, layer-tree.test.ts:820-834, which compares a revived document against CARD_LIBRARY. NOT FIXED HERE because closing it means asserting on the builders source rather than on a value, which is a shape assertion and a decision about how much source-reading this suite wants, not a correction to a wrong test.

title: The plus cannot dismiss the chooser it opened, though it announces that it can
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5S WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW, reasoned from source and not measured in a browser. shell-layout.tsx:487 is `onInsert={() => setInsertOpen(true)}`, unconditional, and InsertPopover renders no Menu.Trigger because it anchors to addRef instead (insert-popover.tsx:87-89). Pressing the + while the chooser is showing therefore cannot close it: the handler only ever sets true, and the outside-press dismissal is the only thing that closes the popup. That contradicts the buttons own contract, which Task 1 added: pane-bar.tsx:80-84 sets aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded from the same state, so a screen reader is told this is a menu button that toggles when it does not. Low severity and unclaimed rather than contradicted by the spec, which says only that the + offers both halves. NOT FIXED AFTER THE CLOSE because it is a behaviour change to a closed plan, and the register owns it: the fix is to make the handler toggle, and it then needs a browser case proving the second press closes rather than reopening.

title: A browser spec hard-codes a copy object id that the sibling spec states is the allocators to choose
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5S WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW. tests/e2e/insert-popover.spec.ts:129 locates a card this test inserted as `[data-vigilia-layer="card-group-time-card"]`, and tests/e2e/composition-panel.spec.ts:1002 states the rule that breaks: a copys id is the allocators to choose. It is deterministic today, because card-library.ts:97 sets COPY_PREFIX to card and createWidgetIdAllocator mints past what the destination already holds, so the first copy of the clock into an empty starter is card-group-time-card. The objection is not flakiness but ownership: the id is a product decision restated in a second place, so a change to the copy prefix or to the allocator moves the product and leaves this spec asserting a string it no longer controls. Low severity. The review also noted that this case now overlaps Task 6s second composition-panel case, both inserting a Clock from the + and reading its row, because the plan ordered Task 3 before Task 6.

title: lanAddress() returns the first non-internal IPv4 with no preference for a physical adapter, so the header can name an address no phone can reach
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 6'S TASK 1.3, which was told to file it and instead left a Discovered, not fixed trailer, because its dispatch forbade writing the register. src/web/packages/host/src/cli/net.ts:90-100 iterates os.networkInterfaces() and returns the first non-internal IPv4. A laptop that also carries a Hyper-V virtual switch, a WSL adapter, a Docker bridge or a VPN routinely enumerates one of those first, so GET /api/hosting hands the editor header an address no phone on the Wi-Fi can reach, and the QR encodes it. Nothing on this machine shows the mistake -- the header renders a plausible dotted quad and the failure appears only on the phone that cannot connect. That address is the header's entire payload, so this is a correctness defect and not a cosmetic one. Not fixed there: the fix needs a decision that task did not own -- which interface wins, how to rank them, and what to do when three are plausible -- and it belongs to lanAddress()'s owner rather than to the route that reads it. Reproduction: run the host on a machine with any virtual adapter present and compare the address printed after Phones on this Wi-Fi with the physical adapter's own.

title: The editor header overflows horizontally at 390 px, putting the publish surface off-screen
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 6'S TASK 2.3 while capturing the rendered proof for the header's publish surface, and left as a Discovered, not fixed trailer because its dispatch forbade writing the register. Measured, not inferred: at 390 px the header overflows horizontally and PHONE ADDRESS, the §145 warning, the pairing expiry and the QR are all off-screen. Evidence is src/web/test-results/publish/header-390.png beside header-desktop.png at 1680 px, where the same surface renders correctly. THOSE FILES DO NOT PERSIST and should not be looked for: Playwright clears its output directory at the start of every run, so the PNGs exist only until the next suite runs. Task 3.5 regenerated and described them and they are gone again. The durable evidence is the measurement, not the file -- at 390 px documentElement.scrollWidth equals innerWidth, so there is no horizontal scrollbar and the overflow is CLIPPED rather than scrollable-to; the publish root is 327.3 px wide starting at left 232.5, the address code runs from 243.5 to 401.9 with its last ~12 px cut off, and the QR begins at 413.9, wholly past the right edge and unseen. Anyone who wants a lasting picture has to put it under docs/evidence/ and register it, which is what that directory is for. Nothing pins a phone-width header, and tests/e2e/surface.ts gates every editor spec to a desktop surface, so no test covers this and none would have caught it. Not fixed there: the header's layout is not that task's owner, and whether the editor should have a usable phone-width header at all is a design question rather than a layout bug -- the editor is a desktop surface by decision, so the honest answer may be that this is acceptable and should be said out loud rather than fixed. It matters more than a cosmetic overflow because the surface that goes off-screen is the one that tells an author where their phone should point. WIDENED ON 2026-10-07 by Task 3.3: the publish control now renders its off state on every host, including a loopback-only one, where it previously rendered nothing at all — so the header carries a button, the §145 warning and (when the LAN is on) the address and a 135 px code, and the pressure this row describes is now on every editor, not only a LAN-bound one. Task 3.5 is the first browser proof that reads this surface at 390 px.

title: A GET that arrives while a LAN move is in flight waits for a move that is waiting for it, and the host never listens again
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 6'S TASK 3.4, which reasoned it, could not reproduce it, and left it unfiled because its cause was not established; filed here because the consequence is a permanently dead host rather than a slow answer. The mechanism, read from the code rather than observed: server.ts:770 has the GET await binding?.idle(); cli/hosting.ts:86 has the move await server.close(), which does not complete until every existing connection ends. A GET whose handler is parked on idle() is one of those connections and will not end until it answers, so the move never finishes, bind(next) never runs, and the server never listens again -- every editor and every display on that host is dead until the process is restarted. It is NOT a slow editor re-read, which is how it was first described. That is the whole reason it is worth a row. Reachability is narrow and the narrowness is the honest part: `finish` -> setLan -> server.close() runs in one synchronous run with no await between them, so no connection can be ACCEPTED in that window, and closeIdleConnections() has already taken the idle keep-alive sockets. What remains is a request already sitting on an accepted connection when close() is called -- a second editor tab, a display reconnecting, anything issued concurrently with the PUT rather than after it. Ordinary single-client use cannot reach it, which is why no reproduction was found. The fix is a design decision between two hazards, and they are not symmetric: the move could destroy connections instead of waiting on them -- closeAllConnections() is now safe precisely BECAUSE the answer is already flushed, which is what Task 3.4's Step 5 accidentally proved when putting it back did not break anything -- at the cost of an empty reply to whichever request was unlucky, which the editor's bounded re-read already tolerates; or the GET could bound its wait and answer from state(), at the cost of answering before the move settles. The first is the smaller change and the failure it trades for is bounded; somebody should still choose rather than inherit.

title: themes/store.test.ts 'holds read and write to the same asset count' times out at 20359 ms inside the full suite and passes alone
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 6'S TASK 3.5 broad gate, which could not file it: its dispatch barred docs/product/**, so it reported the failure instead and left the row to the root. `npx vitest run` from src/web at 6bec889c: 3083 passed, 4 failed, 432 s. Three of the four are vg-135's insert tests in shell-layout.dom.test.tsx, stalling 67-113 s against a 20 s limit. The fourth is this one, in packages/host/src/themes/store.test.ts, and it is NOT vg-135 and not named anywhere in the plan. Re-run alone immediately afterwards: 54/54 pass, exit 0. So it is load-sensitive rather than deterministic, and the load is measurable -- vg-135's stalls alone account for about 404 s of the 432 s run. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED. The plausible reading is that vg-135's synchronous jsdom stall starves the event loop that this test's 20 s timeout is measured against, which would make it a symptom of vg-135 rather than a second defect, and would mean it disappears when vg-135 is fixed. That is a hypothesis, not a measurement, and the alternative -- that the store test has its own slow path under contention -- is not excluded. SAME CLASS AS vg-164, the settings page's disk dropdown that was not found in the full suite and passes alone, and worth the same treatment: a test whose verdict depends on what else is running is not evidence either way, which is how a real regression hides in a suite that is expected to be noisy. Nobody should 'fix' the timeout upward without first measuring which of the two readings is true.

title: renderer-core's plan.ts carries a raw NUL byte in an Intl.NumberFormat cache key, so grep and ripgrep treat the file as binary and silently return no matches for it
detail: FOUND WHILE VERIFYING vg-176, in the file the fix had just changed. renderer-core/src/scene/plan.ts:604 builds a composite cache key for Intl.NumberFormat as `${themeLanguage}\0${minimumFractionDigits}\0${maximumFractionDigits}` -- and the two separators are RAW NUL BYTES in the file, not the escape `\u0000`. TypeScript accepts them and the cache behaves correctly; nothing fails at runtime. THE HARM IS NAVIGATION, and it was demonstrated rather than reasoned: the Grep tool reports "binary file matches (found \"\\0\" byte around offset 17257)" and SUPPRESSES the matching lines. A grep for `planArtboard` across packages returned hits in five files and none in plan.ts, which read as "the extracted helper has no call site" and would have had the controller report a working fix as broken. It is the only NUL-bearing tracked source file in src/web/packages, so the blind spot is exactly one file -- the one an agent most needs to read when working on the plan. git is unaffected: its binary sniff reads only the first 8000 bytes and the NUL is at 17257, so `git diff` and `git diff --stat` render normally and the fix commit was reviewable. THE FIX IS A REPRESENTATION CHANGE, not a behaviour change: writing the escape `\u0000` produces the identical string, so the cache key, the grouping options and every caller are unchanged. One owner (renderer-core), no design decision, and it does not block anything -- which is why it is a row rather than a same-commit fix inside a reviewed fix commit. NO REGRESSION TEST IS OBVIOUS, and that is the honest reason it is not fixed on the fly: the check that would catch it is a repo-wide source-hygiene sweep for NUL bytes, which no script in scripts/ performs today.

title: @radix-ui/react-popover is a direct dependency of the editor and appears in neither THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md nor docs/engineering/dependencies.md, so the repo ships a licence obligation it never recorded
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 7'S AUTHORING PASS at the reuse gate's rung 2, and verified here against the package metadata rather than taken from the agent's report. `src/web/packages/editor/package.json:16` declares `"@radix-ui/react-popover": "^1.1.23"`, and `grep -ci radix THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` is 0 and the same reading holds for docs/engineering/dependencies.md -- neither file has ever carried a Radix row, although the popover has been a direct dependency since the colour picker landed (vg-031, which recorded the cost of a second headless library in view when the user ruled for it). AGENTS.md makes the duty explicit -- 'Before adding a shipped dependency, verify its licence from package metadata and update THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and docs/engineering/dependencies.md' -- so this is a missed obligation rather than an unstated one. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED ON THE FLY: the fix needs a scope decision, not a licence lookup. Nineteen Radix packages are installed for the popover's closure, and whether these two files list DIRECT dependencies only or the installed closure is a policy neither file currently states; writing 19 rows where the convention is 1 would be inventing a rule. That question is about to become load-bearing rather than academic, because section 8 rules Radix the single primitive library and plan 7 adds `@radix-ui/react-dialog` on top -- plan 7's Task 3.1 carries the licence row for the new dependency, and it will set the convention the popover row then follows. NOTHING FAILS AT RUNTIME and no test can redden on this: it is a compliance and provenance gap, which is why it has survived four plans.

title: colour-picker.tsx reaches past the vendored popover to @radix-ui/react-popover directly, so two wrappers own one primitive and the spec's own "incoherence" survives the plan that was written to end it
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 9'S AUTHORING PASS while verifying what §8 left it, and verified here against the source rather than taken from the report. `packages/editor/src/components/ui/colour-picker.tsx:1` and `packages/editor/src/components/ui/popover.tsx:1` both import `* as PopoverPrimitive from "@radix-ui/react-popover"`, so the colour picker does not go through the vendored shadcn wrapper that the rest of the editor uses. WHY IT MATTERS: the spec names this as its motivating example -- §8's table row reads `popover | both -- the incoherence` (`:429`), and the paragraph above it says the app has 'two primitive libraries and two popover implementations'. Plan 9 migrates the five Base UI imports to Radix, which ends the two-LIBRARY half of that. It does not end the two-WRAPPER half, and plan 9's author named it Out of scope rather than folding it in. THE COST IS NOT COSMETIC: a change to the shared wrapper -- its accessibility attributes, its positioning, or a `--shell-*` token it should carry -- does not reach the colour picker, and nothing reddens when the two drift apart, because each is correct in isolation. That is the same shape as the two-ScenePlan-builders defect (vg-176) that this session fixed one layer down: duplication is invisible until the copies disagree. NOT A BLOCKER and not part of the redesign's acceptance: this is a pre-release internal duplication the repo may break cleanly, which is why it is a row and not a task inside plan 9. Whoever takes it should decide which wrapper is the owner -- keeping colour-picker's direct use and deleting the vendored one, or routing the picker through the wrapper -- and that is a small design decision rather than a rename.

title: packages/editor/src/ui-copy.ts states its own module contract twice, so the file has two doc comments claiming one thing and neither is marked as the owner
detail: FOUND BY TASK 1.2 OF PLAN 7 and verified here at the source rather than taken from its report. `ui-copy.ts:1-2` is the file header: `/** Typed package-local visible editor copy (§35). Authored theme text, telemetry values and developer errors stay outside this module. */`. `ui-copy.ts:85-86` repeats that sentence **word for word** as the doc comment on `export const uiCopy`, which is the file's entire export. (The executor reported `:83-84`; the verified lines were `:82-83`. **Task 1 of plan 6 re-measured them at `:85-86`** -- the file grew above them, so this citation drifts with every insertion, and it is why these line numbers are a location to re-check rather than a fact.) WHY IT MATTERS, and it is small: this is the module that claims every visible editor word, so its contract is the thing a contributor reads before adding a string. Two copies mean a later edit to one leaves the other asserting something the file no longer does, and nothing detects it. It is the same shape as a duplicated constant, minus the compiler. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED ON THE FLY, and this is the reason: AGENTS.md allows a fix without a row only when a regression test is obvious, and **no test can catch a duplicated comment without a bespoke lint rule** -- so the fix would leave nothing behind that stops it recurring, which is the exact condition the rule exists to prevent. It is also not this task's region: Task 1.2 added one `shortcuts` block further down the file and correctly left this alone. Cosmetic in effect and it blocks nothing. One of the two copies should go; **which one is a judgement rather than a lookup** -- dropping `:85-86` leaves the export undocumented in an editor that shows hover text, and dropping `:1-2` leaves the module without a header -- which is the second reason it is a row and not a drive-by edit.

title: ui-copy.ts carries a display cap for Escape that nothing can reach, because the module that owns displayable bindings and the one that owns the vocabulary disagree about whether Escape is displayable
detail: FOUND BY TASK 1.3 OF PLAN 7, and noticed independently by Task 1.2s executor one task earlier, which is why it is written down rather than left to be noticed a third time. Two facts, both verified here at the source. `ui-copy.ts:300` has `escape: "Esc"` in `uiCopy.shortcuts.named`, the map `display.ts:48-52` reads to print a named key. And `display.ts:75-84` builds every label from `PRODUCT_SHORTCUTS` **only**, so `shortcutLabel("view.exit-group")` filters an empty list and returns `""`. `view.exit-group` is bound on `Escape`, but it lives in `CONTEXT_SHORTCUTS` (`index.ts:67-71`), whose own comment says those bindings are never displayed. So the string is unreachable and stays unreachable after Task 3.3, which binds `?` and not Escape. WHY IT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN NOTHING: the two modules disagree about one fact. `index.ts` holds that Escape is deliberately undisplayable; `ui-copy.ts` holds a display cap for it. Neither is wrong alone and the pair is incoherent, which is the same shape as vg-179 (`colour-picker.tsx` bypassing the vendored popover) one layer down. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the correct behaviour is not specified, which is the condition AGENTS.md turns on. Keeping the entry is defensible -- `named` is a vocabulary keyed by *key name*, Escape is a key the product binds, and the entry is correct the moment anything renders a context binding -- and deleting it is equally defensible as dead copy. Picking one is a decision about whether that map describes keys or surfaces, not a lookup. No test can catch it either way. Cosmetic in effect: nothing renders wrong, and no author can see the difference. RE-MEASURED BY TASK 1 OF PLAN 6 (2026-10-11), and the title's premise has moved. The first of the two facts is gone: `uiCopy.shortcuts.named` no longer exists -- that block now holds `reference`, `close`, `alternativeSeparator` and `groups` -- so nothing in `ui-copy.ts` claims Escape is displayable and the two-module disagreement the title asserts is no longer in the code. `escape: "Esc"` now lives at `shortcut-manager/display.ts:57` in `NAMED_KEYS`, with `"Escape"` at `:74` in `SPOKEN_NAMED_KEYS`: the vocabulary's own home, seen by nothing else. The residual survives and is narrower than the title says. `CONTEXT_SHORTCUTS` (`shortcut-manager/index.ts:86-90`) binds `{ key: "escape", modifier: false, action: "view.exit-group" }` under a comment saying those bindings are never displayed, so `shortcutLabel("view.exit-group")` filters an empty list and returns `""`. That is now **by design rather than by disagreement**, which collapses the two readings this row posed into one question: whether a context-only binding should be labelable at all. The row stays OPEN with its cause still not established; the title is left as written because it is this row's identity, and retitling it is the closing edit's to make.

title: the ownership sweep cannot see an exported id vocabulary spelled as a type union or a dot-separated id, though ownership.md claims it finds every one
detail: FOUND BY TASK 2.2 OF PLAN 7 while adjudicating a hit the plan told it to expect and the sweep never produced. Verified here at the source, not taken from the report. THE CONTRACT IT BREAKS: `docs/architecture/ownership.md:22-23` says the sweep "finds every module exporting an id vocabulary and reports any other module re-spelling two or more of those ids" -- unqualified. `shortcut-manager/index.ts:2-21` exports exactly that: `ProductShortcutId`, a nineteen-member id vocabulary, with `PRODUCT_SHORTCUTS` the table that binds it. Task 2.2 put eight of those ids into `object-actions.ts`, and `npm run ownership:sweep` exits 0 naming neither module. BOTH HALVES OF THE MECHANISM MISS IT, and they miss for different reasons. `discriminatorsIn` (`scripts/ownership-sweep.mjs:84`) matches `"([a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+)"` -- the `(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+` group requires **at least one hyphen**, so `"edit.duplicate"` is never a candidate at all. `exportedVocabularies` (`:91-101`) parses two shapes only: `const NAME = [ ... ]` with three or more quoted ids, and `Readonly<Record<string, ...>>` records. `ProductShortcutId` is a `type` union, so it is never seen as anyone vocabulary. A vocabulary that is a union *and* dotted is invisible twice over. THE SWEEP IS NOT BROKEN, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS PRECISE: the same run finds two genuine collisions -- `packages/host/src/settings/devices.ts` against `main.ts` and against `server.ts`, sharing `system-disk` and `data-disk`. So the mechanism works; it is blind to one shape, not failing generally. WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY COVERED: `ownership.md:122-123` records a blindness, and it is a *different* one -- the seven object-creation sites "each inline a string literal" and so export no vocabulary at all. That is a module with no vocabulary. This is a module with a vocabulary the sweep cannot read, and the doc gives no sign of knowing that shape exists. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: it is a verification gate, so widening it is a decision about precision against recall, not a bug fix. Dropping the hyphen requirement would make every dotted string in the tree a candidate discriminator and flood the report -- and `ownership.md:48` already carries the hard-won lesson that a gate flagging most of the tree gets ignored, which is why the count floor exists. Accepting type unions means writing a third parser for a syntax the sweep currently reads as data. Neither has an obvious regression test. Consequence for the plan that found it: Task 2.2s constraint told the executor the sweep would report this change and required it to adjudicate the hit as a consumer. There was no hit. The plan asserted a gate watched something the gate cannot see, which is worse than the gate being absent -- it reads as verification and is not.

title: plan 7 Task 2.4's constraint contradicts itself: three File menu rows satisfy its own rule for a chord, and the reason it excludes them is false in the source
detail: FOUND BY THE ROOT WHILE VERIFYING TASK 2.4 (`f6335fff`), by reading what each row actually dispatches rather than by reading the executor's report. The plan's own rule is right and its enumeration is wrong, because the parenthetical the enumeration rests on is false. THE CONTRACT, `docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-07-keyboard.md:1471-1475`: "Only the six Edit items have one (`edit.undo`, `edit.redo`, `edit.copy`, `edit.cut`, `edit.duplicate`, `edit.delete`); the File and Insert items do **not**, because `session.savePackage()` has no binding while `file.save` exists, and pairing them by eye is how a menu starts teaching a key that runs something else. Add one only if the id in `PRODUCT_SHORTCUTS` runs the same call the item runs, and say which in a comment." THE PREMISE IS FALSE IN THE SOURCE, and the file it names is the proof. `session.savePackage()` is not a row with no binding behind it: the bridge method is `savePackage: () => this.#save(options)` (`editor-session.ts:566`) and the shortcut is `this.#shortcuts.register("file.save", () => { void this.#save(options); })` (`:461-463`). Both reach `#save` (`:703`) with the same argument, and `this.#options` is the constructor's own `options` (`:272`), so the receiver and the argument are identical rather than merely equal. The same holds twice more: `file.open` (`:464`) and the row's `openPackage()` (`:567`) both reach `#open`, and `file.new` (`:467`) and `newDocument()` (`:565`) both reach `#new`. SO THE PLAN'S OWN RULE GIVES NINE ROWS, NOT SIX. Applying "add one only if the id in `PRODUCT_SHORTCUTS` runs the same call the item runs" to the source yields the six Edit rows plus `file.new`, `file.open` and `file.save` on the File menu -- the three rows it excludes are the three that satisfy its rule most plainly. The rows that carry none are right, and for the reason the plan gives: `newFromStarter`, `releasePackage`, `openLibrary` and `saveLibrary` have no binding in `PRODUCT_SHORTCUTS`, and no Insert row does either, since the table binds nothing under `insert`. WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN THE TREE: `f6335fff` ships six chorded rows, matching the plan's enumeration, and a comment at `shell-layout.tsx:265-269` that repeats the false premise verbatim -- "`session.savePackage()` is not `file.save`" -- so the falsehood is in shipped source and not only in the plan, and the commit message's second paragraph says it a third time. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: AGENTS.md's on-the-fly test requires that "the correct behaviour is already specified", and here it is not. The contract states a rule and an enumeration that disagree, and resolving them changes user-visible behaviour. §7 of the spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-dashboard-authoring-design.md:401,482`) says only "shortcuts in tooltips; `?`" and is silent on menu rows, so the plan is the sole contract and it contradicts itself. Whether a File row teaches Ctrl+S is a product decision, not a bug fix. TWO SMALLER THINGS THE SAME READING FOUND, not filed separately: the comment's one worked example is the one that is wrong, so any rewrite of the comment pre-judges this row and belongs with the decision; and the plan's file handle is stale for the third time in this phase, citing `item` at `shell-layout.tsx:268-272` where Task 2.3 left it at `:233`.

title: a Base UI menu opened earlier in shell-layout.dom.test.tsx stalls a later dialog's unmount, so the sheet test only passes because of where it sits in the file
detail: FOUND BY TASK 3.4 OF PLAN 7 while placing its own test, and reported in that commit as `Discovered, not fixed:`. MEASURED BY THE EXECUTOR, NOT REPRODUCED BY THE ROOT: the root verified the test passes (361 ms, exit 0) and verified its position at `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx:180`, ahead of every menu-opening test in the file, but did not re-run the failure itself. The row is open on that basis. THE MEASUREMENT: with the sheet test appended last, a file-only run of `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx` gives **4** failures; with the same test placed after `it("mounts the editorial palette, menus, pane bar, inspector and dock hosts")` the same run gives exactly the **3** expected `vg-135` timeouts, and the sheet test passes. Bisected by moving it: preceded by `it("prints the chord on the menu rows the shortcut table binds")` -- the file's last menu test -- the sheet test times out at 20 s; preceded by a non-menu test such as `it("shows one pane at a time and routes the dock through the bridge")` it is green. THE FAILING STEP IS THE CLOSE, NOT THE OPEN: the test's first read is synchronous and succeeds, and what times out is the `vi.waitFor` waiting for `[role="dialog"]` to become null after the close button is clicked. So the dialog opens and never finishes unmounting. THE CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and the hypothesis below is the executor's rather than a finding: Radix unmounts through `Presence`, which waits for a frame; a Base UI menu opened earlier in the same jsdom environment is said to leave that frame pipeline stalled, so the frame `Presence` waits on is never delivered. That is plausible and untested -- what is measured is the ordering, not the mechanism. WHY IT IS THE SAME FAMILY AS `vg-135` BUT NOT THAT ROW: `vg-135` is one Base UI menu-trigger *click* blocking 50-90 s synchronously in whatever test opens it. This is a *later, different* test failing because an earlier one opened a menu -- a cross-test leak through shared jsdom state rather than a slow call. The two were also observed to be independent in the same session: the three `vg-135` timeouts did **not** reproduce in the executor's `npx vitest run packages/editor` run (where only `ui-copy.test.ts` was red) and appeared only in the file-only run, so `vg-135` is intermittent while this one was reproducible by test order. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the fix needs a decision about which mechanism to change -- isolating the DOM between tests, giving the sheet test its own file, driving Radix's unmount without `Presence`, or finding the Base UI leak -- and more than one owner could make it. THE WORKAROUND NOW IN THE TREE IS AN ORDERING DEPENDENCY, which is the part that will bite: the test passes because of where it sits, so inserting a menu-opening test above it, or running the file with a shuffled order, silently turns it into a 20 s timeout that reads as a regression in the sheet. The test carries a doc comment saying so, which keeps it from being a trap, but the dependency is real. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-08 BY PLAN 9 TASK 1.1, AFTER THE DIALOG MOVED FROM RADIX TO BASE UI (decision 0038), because the change removed the mechanism this row's hypothesis named. **The ordering dependency survives; only the symptom softened, and the hypothesis is now weaker rather than stronger.** Same file, same command, two runs on one commit: with the sheet test in its guarded place it is green in **126 ms**, and appended last -- after every menu test -- it is green in **20 656 ms**, up from the hard 20 s timeout the executor measured. That is a 164x stall inside the same test, on the same assertion (`vi.waitFor` for `[role='dialog']` to go null after the close), so the close still does not settle promptly when a menu ran earlier, and the ordering guard is still doing real work rather than guarding a dead hazard. WHAT THAT SAYS ABOUT THE CAUSE: the row's hypothesis was Radix's `Presence` waiting on a frame the stalled pipeline never delivers, and **Base UI has no `Presence`** -- its dialog keeps the popup in the document behind a `hidden` attribute until the close settles. A different implementation stalling the same way, in the same place, is evidence that the shared jsdom frame state is the cause and the library was the messenger. That is an inference from two implementations, not a measurement of the pipeline, so the cause is still **not established**. THE TITLE WAS CORRECTED rather than left describing a library the file no longer uses; the ordering dependency it names is unchanged. Nothing else in the row is affected -- the root still has not reproduced the executor's 4-failure run itself.

title: Entering a group marks the document unsaved, because the grouping manager's reachability flags reach the serialized scene
detail: FOUND BY THE ROOT WHILE PLACING TASK 4.1 OF PLAN 7's second capture, from an `Unsaved changes` mark in the footer that the task's first capture does not have. Pre-existing and not plan 7's: `grouping-manager` predates the plan and plan 7 does not touch it. THE MEASUREMENT, TAKEN IN THE BROWSER AND PROBED STEP BY STEP: reading `.editor-shell-save-state[data-dirty]` after each act gives after-load `false`, after-enterLayer `true`, and `true` for every act after it (selecting a part, pressing `?`, `Delete`, `Control+z`, `Escape`). So the keypresses behind the sheet change nothing -- the deferral being proved -- and entering the group is what flips the marker. THE CAUSE IS MEASURED, not inferred: diffing `canvas.toJSON()` across `enterLayer` gives 8 changed paths, `objects[3].subTargetCheck`, `objects[3].interactive`, and `objects[4|5|6|8|9].objects`. Both of the first two are set by `makeSelectableThrough` (`grouping-manager/index.ts:92-97`) and **both are serialized by Fabric**. THE COMMENT THAT SAYS OTHERWISE IS NARROWER THAN THE CODE: `grouping-manager/index.ts:75-78` claims '`selectable`/`evented` are not in Fabric's `stateProperties`, so this never reaches a save', and at `:111-119` 'neither key is in Fabric's `stateProperties`, so it stays view state (SS67)'. The `stateProperties` claim is TRUE -- verified against `node_modules/fabric/dist/index.mjs`, whose `stateProperties` list is top/left/scaleX/scaleY/flipX/flipY/originX/originY/angle/opacity/globalCompositeOperation/shadow/visible/skewX/skewY, with neither key in it. But the comment reasons only about `applyReachability`, which sets `selectable`/`evented`; **`makeSelectableThrough` sets two different keys, `subTargetCheck` and `interactive`, and the comment never covers them.** So the guard the comment believes it has does not exist for those two. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE MARKER: if the author saves while inside a group, the reachability flags this manager set are written into the theme package, which is the same class as `vg-129`/`vg-130` -- editor-only state reaching a shareable artifact -- and SS67 says view state is never authored history and never a Fabric write. The six changed `objects` arrays are measured but NOT explained: the cause of those is not established, and they may be a consequence of the same flag write or something else in the path. THE FIX NEEDS A DECISION AND IS NOT TAKEN HERE: it is the general question `vg-041` owns -- which Fabric properties are derived or editor-only, and how serialisation excludes them -- and `vg-026` is that row's other measured instance, a text object repainted by the live pass. Filed as its own row rather than folded into `vg-041` because that is the pattern this register already uses for `vg-026`: the instance is independently fixable and independently verifiable, and the general row points at it.

title: The host re-spells the assignable-device-id union inline in server.ts rather than deriving it from the settings module that owns it
detail: FOUND BY TASK 4.2 OF PLAN 7, the judgement walk, while adjudicating what `npm run ownership:sweep` reported. Pre-existing, in `packages/host`, and outside every plan of the current redesign. THE MEASUREMENT: `cd src/web && npm run ownership:sweep` exits 0 with `mapRows: 99`, `sourceFiles: 257`, and reports exactly two vocabulary hits plus the same two pairs again as `subsetReSpellings` -- vocabulary 'Device assignment and display names', owner `packages/host/src/settings/devices.ts`, re-spelled in `packages/host/src/main.ts` and `packages/host/src/server.ts`, sharing `system-disk`/`data-disk` (2 of 3). THE OWNER IS `ASSIGNABLE_GROUPS` at `devices.ts:15`. THE TWO HITS ARE NOT THE SAME: `main.ts:203-208` only INDEXES `storedDevices.assigned["system-disk"|"data-disk"]`, which is a consumer reading the owner's ids and is the rule working; `server.ts:394` writes the union out again as a parameter type, `group: "gpu" | "system-disk" | "data-disk"`, and `server.ts:398-399` repeats the literals. That second one is a genuine second owner of the vocabulary: adding a fourth assignable group to `devices.ts` can never reach it, and nothing would fail. Adjudicated by the walk and re-read by the root; the sweep's own output is the evidence. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: it is not this plan's task, it is in another package, and the fix is a small question about where the type should be exported from rather than a one-line change in place. Cross-reference `vg-184`, which is the sweep being unable to see a vocabulary spelled as a type union at all -- the reason this row had to be found by reading the tool's output rather than by the tool naming it directly.

title: A rejection arriving after the scene mounted calls showLoadFailure, which replaces the whole document and discards a display that was already drawn
detail: FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 8 TASK 1.3 at 66ee3414. THE STRUCTURE, read rather than guessed: `main.ts:104` is a `catch` around all of `await startHostedTheme(...)`, and that function mounts the scene at `main.ts:301` via `mountFabricScene({ host, ... })` and then keeps running the refresh cadence and the transport wiring. So a rejection raised anywhere in the display lifecycle after that mount reaches `showLoadFailure`, which now calls `document.body.replaceChildren(...)`. NOT A REGRESSION INTRODUCED BY 1.3, and this is the part worth reading twice: the previous form was `host.replaceChildren(view)` with `host` the artboard host, and the mounted canvas lives INSIDE that host, so the canvas was discarded either way. What 1.3 changed is the blast radius, not the loss -- the chrome bands now go with it. THE OPEN QUESTION is therefore older than plan 8: whether a failure arriving after a display is already drawn should replace the screen at all, or should leave the working display alone and say something smaller beside it, given that a theme whose font failed to load after mount is arguably still a theme worth showing. THE PLAN'S OWN PREMISE WAS FALSE and is corrected in place: it asserted that this runs before any scene is mounted so there is no canvas to lose, which is true of `main.ts:89` (reached when `requested === null`, before anything) and false of `main.ts:104`. The landed comment states the behaviour without claiming an intent for it. NOT REPRODUCED: the call structure is established, but no test raises a post-mount rejection, so which of `loadFontAssets` (`:316`), `reviveThemeEnvelope` (`:324`) or the direct `refresh()` (`:359`) can actually reject is unmeasured -- the reading shows the path exists, not that anything walks it. Filed rather than fixed because the answer is a design decision about what a wall display should do when it breaks late, and because the behaviour predates plan 8, which merely widened it.

title: No e2e fixture raises a data gap and a composition gap together, so the pair section 97 describes is measured as two transport-side strips instead
detail: FOUND BY THE ROOT ON 2026-10-08, correcting plan 8 Task 2.3 before dispatching it, while checking whether the theme its ceiling test uses could actually raise the two strips the test's own comment named. THE MEASUREMENT, read from the seeded packages rather than assumed: `.e2e-host-app/themes/e2e-missing-sensor/theme.json` has artboard `{width:640,height:360,contentFit:contain}` and ONE object, a `Textbox` at `40,140` sized `420x60` -- entirely inside the artboard. `.e2e-host-app/themes/e2e-hosted/theme.json` has the same 640x360 artboard and four objects, the lowest a `Textbox` at `40,300` sized `420x60`, whose bottom edge is exactly 360. Neither bleeds, so neither raises `#vigilia-crop`, and `showCropNotice` (`packages/player/src/chrome.ts:121`) is the only writer of that strip. THE PAIR THAT DOES NOT EXIST: a theme that both bleeds and binds a key no provider reports. The bleed fixtures (`HOST_BLEED_THEME_ID`, `HOST_BLEED_ALL_THEME_ID`, `e2e-bleed-*`) bind real keys, so they raise a composition gap and no data gap; the missing-sensor fixture binds an unreportable key and raises a data gap and no composition gap. SECTION 97's rationale -- that an unreadable sensor and a cropped object must be legible as different things, which is why two strips may be on screen at once -- is therefore not exercised as a pair by any browser test. WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT IN THE PLAN RATHER THAN HERE: Task 2.3's second test keeps its two-strip assertion, because the chrome ceiling is about total chrome height and not about which notices make it up, and its comment now says the pair is a data gap beside a TRANSPORT gap (`#vigilia-connection`, drawn because the test aborts `**/ws`) instead of claiming a composition gap. Filed rather than fixed because closing it means adding a fixture to `tests/e2e/host-theme.ts` that is both bleeding and missing-sensored, which is a decision about fixture inventory rather than a change to the code under test.

title: No tsconfig includes tests/e2e, so a type error in any browser spec is checked by nothing
detail: FOUND BY THE ROOT ON 2026-10-08 while running plan 8 Task 2.3's gates on a new spec file (`src/web/tests/e2e/host-chrome.spec.ts`, commit 1e52b8da), and it is repo-wide rather than this task's. THE MEASUREMENT, read from the configuration rather than assumed: `cd src/web && npm run typecheck` runs `npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present`, and `package.json`'s workspaces are `packages/renderer-core`, `packages/theme-package`, `packages/scene-fabric`, `packages/player`, `packages/editor`, `packages/fake-source` and `packages/host` -- `tests/` is not among them, so no workspace tsc program can see it. There is no `src/web/tsconfig.json` and no `tests/tsconfig.json` (`ls tsconfig*.json tests/tsconfig*.json` finds only `tsconfig.base.json`). Of the seven package tsconfigs, `renderer-core` includes `src/**/*.ts` and `theme-package` includes `src/**/*.ts`; the other five carry no `include` at all and fall back to TypeScript's default, which is `**/*` relative to the config's own directory -- so every one of them is scoped inside its own package. The one config that mentions tests, `packages/editor/tsconfig.json`, mentions them in a comment about `src/core`'s architecture tests and includes only `src/**/*.ts` and `src/**/*.tsx`. WHAT STILL RUNS: `./node_modules/.bin/biome lint tests/...` checks syntax and style but is not a type checker, and Playwright transpiles specs with esbuild, which strips types without checking them -- so a spec that reads a property which does not exist on a fixture, or passes the wrong shape to a helper, fails only at runtime and only in the branch that reads it. NOT A REGRESSION AND NOT BLOCKING: this is the state every existing browser spec has always been in, and it cost nothing in this task because the new file's helpers are copies of a spec that runs. It is filed because the absence is invisible -- a green `npm run typecheck` reads as coverage of the whole workspace, and it is not -- and because the fix is a decision rather than a one-liner: adding `tests/` to a program pulls `@playwright/test` and both DOM and Node libs into one project, which is the conflict the editor's tsconfig already documents for `@types/node`. NOW LOAD-BEARING (2026-10-09, plan 3's close): plan 3 rewrote three tests/e2e/ specs (author-journey-rebuild, inspector-sections and editor-canvas) and added four parity captures, and none of that is typechecked by any tsconfig - which the close's own reviews kept re-learning, since the standing trap 'tests/e2e/ belongs to no tsconfig' had to be stated in briefs to stop a mis-typed locator passing review. The risk is no longer theoretical.

title: The canvas context menu's e2e spec never asserts the menu lands where the pointer was, so the pointer anchoring the whole library ruling turns on has no browser coverage
detail: FOUND WHILE CORRECTING THE PLAN AFTER THE USER RULED FOR BASE UI, checking what the browser actually proves about the one surface that stopped plan 9's Phase 1. THE SURFACE: src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/canvas-context-menu.tsx computes a synthetic zero-size rect from the right-click coordinate (lines 146-157) and hands it to Base UI's `Positioner anchor`, because Radix cannot anchor a menu to a point and that is what eliminated it. That behaviour is now the load-bearing reason for the library choice (0038). THE MEASUREMENT: src/web/tests/e2e/editor-context-menu.spec.ts is 195 lines with one test, and its own readMenu() helper returns popupTop -- and nothing asserts it. Grepping the file for popupTop gives two hits, both inside the helper: the declaration in the return type and the read in the evaluate body. No expect() consumes it, and the click coordinate (point.x, point.y) is used for page.mouse.click and for nothing else, so the popup is never compared to the point it was opened at. What the spec does assert is that the menu opened, that its scrollHeight exceeds its clientHeight, that popupBottom is inside the viewport, and that End then Enter reaches and fires the last entry. All of that passes on a menu anchored to the wrong corner. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED ON THE FLY: the fix needs a design decision this row cannot make, and it is not just an added assertion. The spec deliberately runs in a 420px window against a 470px menu, so Base UI is flipping or shifting the popup by necessity and the pointer coordinate is not where the popup goes -- an assertion written in this window would pin the flip rather than the anchor, and a correct-looking failure would be the test being wrong. Pinning the anchor needs a second case in a window tall enough to leave the popup unshifted, which is a new test rather than an edit, and it needs a decision on what tolerance counts as anchored, since the renderer and the popup round to different pixels. WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT ACADEMIC: the surface whose inability to migrate is the stated reason for the library ruling is the one surface with no browser assertion of the behaviour that made it special, and plan 9's Phase 1 is about to touch the library under it. If the anchor silently broke, every assertion in this file would still pass. SEVERITY IS MEDIUM: nothing is known to be broken today -- the menu visibly opens at the pointer when driven by hand -- so this is a coverage gap rather than a defect, filed because it is the gap between what 0038 claims is verified and what a run actually checks. SAME CLASS AS vg-159/vg-160, plan 4's verification bullets that were never delivered as tests.

title: display-fabric's repaint check times out on every run, so the assertion that the update loop reaches the canvas never executes
detail: FOUND AT PLAN 9 PHASE 1'S BOUNDARY while re-reading a full browser suite that had reported 21 unexpected on a loaded box. THE MEASUREMENT, which separates this from a flake rather than from a hunch: `npx playwright test display-fabric --workers=1 --repeat-each=3` collected 144 and reported 6 unexpected, and all six are the SAME test - `keeps repainting as samples arrive`, two projects by three repeats - every one a `Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded`. One run of it alone fails 2 of 2 the same way. So this is a STANDING RED, not an intermittent: different from `vg-140`, which files an intermittent in the same file but a different test (`draws each fit mode, and every icon, in its own box`, an ink reading of exactly 0), and different from the 30 s timeouts that appeared in the same suite under load and vanished when the spec set was re-run alone. **NOT ATTRIBUTED TO THE DIFF IN THE TREE, and that was measured rather than argued:** the same spec was run at `af499716` with the 22 `@radix-ui/*` packages reinstalled and both builds rebuilt, and it fails there identically - 2 collected, 2 unexpected, both 30 s timeouts. WHAT IT COSTS: the test's whole subject is that the player repaints when telemetry samples arrive, and its own comment records that the failure was verified by sabotage - `handle.update(plan())` cut, and it goes red. A test that times out before reaching its assertion cannot play that role, so the coverage this file believes it has for the update loop is currently absent rather than passing. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED, and the shape narrows it to two candidates: the body awaits `openCanvasPlayer(page)`, reads the artboard canvas with `toDataURL()`, then awaits `page.clock.runFor(4000)` - Playwright's FAKE clock, standing in for the player's once-a-second plan rebuild - and reads the canvas again. A 30 s timeout on that sequence is a readiness wait that never resolves, so either the player never reaches the state `openCanvasPlayer` waits for, or the fake clock never advances it because the player schedules its rebuild off something `page.clock` does not drive. THE NEXT STEP is to separate those two and it is cheap: log which await the timeout lands on, and whether the artboard canvas is non-empty at the first read. A row rather than an immediate fix because the owner is not established - `openCanvasPlayer` is a shared helper several specs read, so a change there is not this file's to make alone - and because a fake clock that fails to drive a real timer is a decision about how the player is tested rather than a defect in one assertion.

title: A theme install that loses the staging rename to EPERM fails a spec outright, and the cascade reads as unrelated defects
detail: FOUND AT PLAN 9 PHASE 1'S BOUNDARY, where it was the single largest reason a full browser-suite run was unreadable. THE MECHANISM: the e2e host installs a fixture by writing into `.e2e-host-app/themes/.staging-<random>.<fixture>` and renaming it onto the fixture's own directory. Under parallel load that rename intermittently loses with `EPERM: operation not permitted` on Windows, and the spec fails at the install: `the host accepted the fixture: EPERM: operation not permitted, rename '...\.staging-muzerquni8dhlraixl.e2e-clip-parity' -> '...\.e2e-host-app	hemes\e2e-clip-parity'`. WHAT MAKES IT WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A SHRUG IS THE BLAST RADIUS, not the race. In one full-suite run that failure accounted for 17 of 21 unexpected results without appearing 17 times: every spec whose fixture did not install then fails somewhere else - five on a missing object (`no object with id authoring`, `no object with id mover`, `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'groupContext')`), three on `#status` never reaching the text the spec waits for - so ONE filesystem race presented as five unrelated defect classes across glass, clip, snapping and appearance specs. That is precisely the shape that gets misattributed to whatever diff happens to be in the tree, and it very nearly was here. THE SAMPLE THAT CLASSIFIES IT: re-running the same spec set with the box quiet left 4 unexpected, and `clip-parity` run entirely alone is 2 expected / 0 unexpected. So it is load- or handle-dependent and NOT a standing red; the remaining 4 were `vg-151` (known open) and `vg-196` (filed separately). The staging directory is left clean - no `.staging-*` survived either run - so nothing is wedged between runs. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the handle belongs to the host's own file watcher on the themes directory, to an indexer or scanner on this box, or to a previous run's host process that had not fully exited is not measured, and no other session's Chromium is implicated because none was on the box for the classifying run. THE FIX IS PROBABLY SMALL AND IS NOT TAKEN HERE: a bounded retry around the rename is the obvious repair, since the staging directory is the host's own and a lost race currently fails the spec outright with no attempt to recover. Worth pairing with whatever owns `themes/store.ts`'s install path, because `vg-174`'s LAN move work is in the same neighbourhood.

title: The docs map sends architecture decisions to adr/, while the live decision register is decisions/
detail: FOUND BY THE ROOT while adding a row to docs/README.md for the new design language, so this is a doc-map defect spotted in passing rather than the task being done. MEASURED: docs/README.md's table has the row 'Why major architecture choices were made | adr/'. Two directories exist and they are not the same register: docs/adr/ holds 0002-0010 plus its own README, and docs/decisions/ holds 0019-0039 plus its own README. AGENTS.md's *Reuse before build* section names the live one plainly - 'Land a note at docs/decisions/NNNN-<slug>.md' - and scripts/reuse-gate.mjs enforces writes against that directory, so the gate and the map disagree about where a decision note goes. The numbering is contiguous when the two are read together (0002-0010, then 0019-0039) and there is a gap at 0011-0018, which is consistent with decisions/ having replaced adr/ at 0019 rather than with two registers running in parallel. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether adr/ is deliberately kept for a different class of decision - nothing in either README says it is, and both READMEs describe the same thing, one file per decision where the way something is built was not obvious. That is the same text in both places, which is what a superseded directory looks like when it was copied and then diverged. The cost is that the canonical map - the file AGENTS.md points a fresh session at for durable project truth - sends a reader to a register that stopped receiving rows at 0010. The fix is a judgement rather than a lookup, which is why this is a row and not a drive-by edit: either the map points at decisions/, or adr/ is the live one and decisions/ is the mistake, or the two are merged and the gap at 0011-0018 is explained. Nothing here changes either directory.

title: Five rows in backlog-archive.jsonl carry `artefacts` as a string where backlog-check.mjs requires an array, so the archive would fail its own register gate the moment anything read it
detail: FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 1 TASK 1 of the editor-GUI redesign, reading the archive for the shape a verified row uses before moving vg-149 into it. MEASURED at 2c78cf68 over the archive's 123 rows: 106 carry `artefacts` as an array, 5 carry it as a string - vg-173 `9cd76a0b`, vg-176 `72edf30e`, vg-187 `26231c4a`, vg-180 `8cb99931` (lines 114-117) and vg-157 `d3549ca9` (line 118) - and 12 carry no `artefacts` at all, 9 of them withdrawn and 3 verified. `scripts/backlog-check.mjs:139` reads `Array.isArray(item.artefacts) ? item.artefacts : []`, so each of the five string rows reports "verified with no artefact commit" and would fail `check()`. NOTHING READS THE ARCHIVE TODAY: no file under `scripts/` or `.claude/` names `backlog-archive`, and the checker's `FILE` is hardcoded to `backlog.jsonl`, so the drift cannot redden a run - which is why it is filed rather than treated as urgent. THE SHAS THEMSELVES ARE NOT WRONG: each resolves and is present, so no verification is lost and no row misrepresents its finding; only the JSON shape drifted, most likely from rows hand-written before the array form settled. NOT FIXED HERE because the repair and its guard are two decisions rather than one: rewrapping five values edits verified rows the sessions that closed them never wrote, and the obvious guard - pointing `check()` at the archive as well - would first need the 12 `artefacts`-less rows judged, and those include 3 `verified` rows whose check ran without a commit to name, which is a call about plans this task is not executing.

title: The well's resting 1px boundary reads at 2.15:1 in graphite and 1.42:1 in light, below the 3:1 bible section 5 asks of a control boundary
detail: FOUND BY THE DESIGN-LANGUAGE PARITY GATE (this plan, task 4) on the gate's first green run, and it is a token rather than a control. MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER, not modelled: `design-language.spec.ts` hides the text, screenshots the page, samples the pixel under each control and composites the computed border colour over it, so the numbers include whatever alpha the token carries and whatever gradient sits beneath. Six control states pass in all six palettes - label, refusal, selected, value, checked and focus; this one does not. The well is `--panel-2` fill plus a 1px `--edge` border, which is bible section 5's vocabulary exactly, so the composite is the token's own: graphite `rgba(221,244,238,0.26)` over `rgb(11,18,22)` = 2.15:1 (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:127`) and light `rgba(38,70,56,0.20)` over `rgb(246,254,250)` = 1.42:1 (`:242`). The other four palettes read 5.5-18.4:1 because their `--shell-edge` is opaque. WHY IT IS NOT JUST A NUMBER: `--edge` is the boundary that says a value is editable (section 5 rule 1), so at 1.42:1 the light palette's control boundaries are effectively invisible, and the same hairline bounds every panel and divider the editor draws. NOT FIXED HERE because the repair is a design decision and not a task: either section 3's fine hairline yields to section 5's 3:1 by raising the alpha to something that is no longer a hairline, or the ratio is accepted for a resting boundary and only the focus boundary is held at 3:1 (which is what section 5.4 already does). Both change every surface, and neither is this plan's to choose. PINNED, NOT WAIVED, in `design-language.spec.ts` as `PINNED_FLOOR.boundary` (graphite 2, light 1.2) so a regression still fails the gate; the floor is deleted and the bible minimum restored when this row is ruled on. SEVERITY: medium - nothing errors, the boundary reads wrong. RE-MEASURED BY PLAN 7 TASK 4 (`a3d2c407`, 2026-10-11), and it is worse than this row records: graphite's well boundary is now **1.20:1**, not 2.15:1, because graphite's `--shell-edge` became the checked drawing's own `--edge` (`current/shell.html:17`, `#242b34`) verbatim - an opaque dark line where the shipped edge had been a 26%-alpha light hairline, and 1.20:1 is that line against `--panel-2` `#171c23` (1.27:1 against `--panel`). `design-language.spec.ts`'s `PINNED_FLOOR.boundary.graphite` moved 2 -> 1.2 to hold the value that ships, which the controller ruled a re-measurement rather than an allowlist widened to pass: the shipped value is mandated by the drawing, no other threshold moved, and this row stays open and owns the ruling. (This row's title says light is 1.42:1 while the pin's light entry reads 1.2 - two different measurements of light, neither corrected here.) THE DECISION IS NOW SHARPER RATHER THAN ANSWERED, and one number settles it: clearing section 5's 3:1 against `--panel-2` needs the edge at relative luminance ~0.134, a near-`#676767` hairline, which is a visibly different shell from the drawing the user ruled is the gold style. The controller's provisional reading, recorded so a later session need not re-derive it: section 5's 3:1 binds the focus boundary (rule 4, already >=3:1 in all six palettes) and a boundary that is a control's ONLY separation, while a well also carries a fill, a hover-raise to `--muted` and a label, so its resting hairline is a divider. That reading would leave this row's graphite half as a deliberate low-contrast style rather than a defect - which is the user's call to make, not an agent's, so the row stays open and the shortfall stays recorded. SECOND REGION IN THE SAME CLASS (filed 2026-10-11 as vg-318, by plan 8 Task 3's review): the settings modal's frame against its scrim reads 1.22:1 before and 1.08:1 after in graphite, 1.07:1 to 1.21:1 in editorial, and no gate reaches it - this row's own chrome-contrast test measures the rail and opens no dialog. It is not merged into this row because its remedy is a reader that does not exist rather than a token change, but this row's floor ruling settles it too, so the two must be read together. RULED BY THE USER (2026-10-11), asked as one question with three readings. The NARROW reading is the user's answer: bible section 5's 3:1 binds the focus boundary -- which section 5.4 already holds at >=3:1 in all six palettes -- and any boundary that is a control's ONLY separation. A well also carries a fill, a hover-raise to --muted and a label, so its resting hairline is a divider rather than the control's sole marker, and this row's graphite half is deliberate low-contrast style rather than a defect. WHAT CLOSES IT, and it is one change: `PINNED_FLOOR.boundary` is deleted from `design-language.spec.ts` and bible section 5 states the narrower rule in words, so the next reader does not re-file the same shortfall as a regression. This row and `vg-318` then close together, because this ruling is the answer to both.

title: `--shell-warm` stayed a pastel in ember, moss and plum while those palettes' paper is light, so every `--warn` text reads at 1.4-2.0:1
detail: FOUND BY THE DESIGN-LANGUAGE PARITY GATE (this plan, task 4) on the gate's first green run. MEASURED in the same browser pass as vg-200: a rejected numeric draft renders its reason in `text-warn` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/control-number.tsx:158`), and the composite over each palette's own panel is ember `#ff7e6e` on `rgb(247,226,210)` = 1.98:1, moss `#e8c56a` on `rgb(228,239,217)` = 1.40:1, plum `#ffb2a1` on `rgb(236,227,247)` = 1.39:1, against 5.18-9.36:1 in editorial, graphite and light. THE CONTROL SET IS NOT THE OWNER: the three declarations the pastels come from (`editor-shell.css:175`, `:199`, `:223`) are the same `--shell-warm` that `.editor-shell-diagnostic` (`:1607`) and `.editor-shell-save-state` (`:1618`) paint, so on those three palettes the footer's warnings and the unsaved marker are unreadable too - the first `text-warn` in the product is not the defect, it is the first place the defect was measured. THE FILE ALREADY RECORDS THE SHAPE OF THE FIX: the comment above `[data-shell-palette="ember"]` says the three palettes' accents were 'deepened from the pastel that named them' because 'a light accent on a light surface carries nothing' and a pastel hover 'was a hover the author could not see'. `--shell-warm` was left as the pastel it was named for, and the same deepening is what it needs - at least 4.5:1 against each palette's own `--shell-surface` and against the glass overlay. NOT FIXED HERE because it is a colour decision with currency beyond text: `--vigilia-accent` aliases `--shell-warm` (`:112`) on the canvas side, so the value that makes warnings readable also moves the canvas accent, and only the design owner can rule on the hue. PINNED, NOT WAIVED, in `design-language.spec.ts` as `PINNED_FLOOR.invalid` (ember 1.9, moss 1.35, plum 1.35), deleted and replaced by the 4.5:1 minimum when this row is ruled on. SEVERITY: medium-high - required information (why a value was rejected) is illegible in three of the six shipped palettes.

title: A well's horizontal padding is 6px, where bible section 3's table assigns 4px to inside-a-control and the mockup draws 8px
detail: FOUND BY THE MOCKUP COMPARISON this plan's task 4 owes (the difference list beside `docs/design/mockups/inspector-controls.html`). MEASURED: `src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/control-well.tsx:54` pads every well `px-[var(--space-6)]` = 6px, and the same 6px carries through the select trigger, the swatch well and the number wells. Bible section 3's spacing table is an assignment as well as a set: `4` is 'Inside a control (well padding, icon button)' and `6` is 'Between the rows of one section', so 6px here is a step that belongs to a different place. The checked target disagrees with itself: `docs/design/mockups/inspector-controls.html` draws the select and range wells at `padding:5px 8px` and the slider's value well at `4px 6px`, so it offers 8, 6 and an off-scale 5 for the same job. Three sources, three answers, which is why this is a row rather than an edit - the value is contested, not merely unspecified. WHY THE GATE DOES NOT CATCH IT: `design-language.spec.ts` asserts that every authored spacing value is a step from section 3, which 6px is; it cannot see that the table assigns that step elsewhere, and no closed assertion can without the table becoming code. NOT FIXED HERE because the repair is a design ruling between three authorities and it moves the width of every control, including the 36px value well and the 246px pane's own gutters. SEVERITY: low - the chrome reads correctly today and only the step assignment is wrong.

title: The draft/commit keyboard decision is duplicated between control-text.tsx and control-number.tsx
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 1 (gates-and-the-control-set) FINAL CODE REVIEW and PARKED by the controller, not fixed. src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/control-text.tsx:73-88 and control-number.tsx:137-150 each re-implement the same draft/commit keyboard decision - the composing ref, the Enter/IME guard, and the Escape reset - and both copies are currently correct. Extracting a helper is a real refactor of the two most intricate controls at the moment the plan closes, for a drift risk that has not bitten, so it is filed rather than fixed. OWNER: plan 3 (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-08-the-inspector.md, the per-kind inspector), the next plan to touch the text/number pair. The exit is one shared hook the two controls call; leaving it risks the two copies drifting before plan 3 reaches them. OWNER REACHED, NOT DISCHARGED (recorded 2026-10-09 when plan 3 closed): plan 3 did touch this pair - three commits, 07774ce8, 612cfdd9 and 07869755, +119/-49 across the two files - and the duplication survived it intact, so the copies are still two and both still correct. The line citations above are now stale for the number control: its composing ref is at control-number.tsx:76 and its Enter/Escape guard at :142-157, where control-text.tsx's ref is at :54 and its guard at :75-88. Plan 3's plan file now lives at docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-08-the-inspector.md, so the owner this row names is spent: IT NEEDS A NEW OWNER, and plan 4 - the panes - is the next work over this same control set.

title: The palette picker's popup lands at the window's top-left instead of beside its swatch, and the spec that measures it is red at base
detail: FOUND WHILE RUNNING plan 2 Task 1's full desktop-chromium gate, not by that task. keyboard.spec.ts:123 ("the palette picker lands beside its trigger, and its tracks answer the arrow keys") fails at keyboard.spec.ts:159, Math.abs(popup.y - (swatch.y + swatch.height + 6)) reading 340.3125 against an assertion of <= 12, so the popup's top is roughly a viewport above the swatch: the popover is unpositioned rather than offset. PRE-EXISTING, MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: the same spec text on the unmodified tree at base 2c0081b1, in a detached worktree (npm ci then npm run build, one test, desktop-chromium, workers=1, nothing else on the box), fails with the same reading, and the rail tree fails identically. So it is neither the rail's column nor a flake. The spec's own comment names the class: the popup moved from Radix's Content, which positions itself, to Base UI's Positioner, and a Popup placed straight in the portal renders unpositioned, which panel.dom.test.ts:187-192 records happening to this control once before. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED: nothing here says whether the Positioner is absent from the portal, present and unmeasured, or anchored to a containing block the Tokens pane changes; the measuring assertion is where the test stops, so the arrow-key half below it is unmeasured rather than passing.

title: The canvas dock sets data-visible but editor-shell.css styles only the true state, and a comment claims the attribute drives presence
detail: FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING plan 2 Task 2 (the panes' chrome). src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/canvas-dock.tsx:130-133 carries a comment saying the dock "is present as soon as a document is", and the element sets data-visible={bridge !== undefined}. But editor-shell.css styles only .editor-shell-dock[data-visible="true"] (editor-shell.css:1594), and a grep for data-visible across that stylesheet returns that single line - there is no rule for the false state. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the no-document case is hidden by another mechanism (a base display rule on .editor-shell-dock, an ancestor's rule, or the element not being rendered at all) is unmeasured, because the browser probe this task ran had a document open and so exercised only the true branch. The comment may simply be describing a condition the stylesheet expresses elsewhere. NOT FIXED HERE because the dock's chrome is Task 6's and Task 7's, and what is wrong here, if anything, is a comment disagreeing with the code rather than an observed defect. SEVERITY: low; unverified.

title: A pane's title bar and footer scroll with its body, against bible section 7.7, because the aside is the only scroller
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 2's task review. editor-shell.css:782-787 puts overflow:auto on aside.editor-shell-panel, and that aside contains the pane header, the body and the footer, so scrolling a long list takes the title bar and the toolbar off screen with it. Bible section 7.7 requires a pane's title and footer to stay outside the scrolling body, and layer-panel.tsx:809-810 carries a comment asserting exactly that property - "the toolbar stays put while the list scrolls beneath it" - about a structure that does not have it. The comment is corrected in Task 2's fix round; THIS ROW IS ABOUT THE STRUCTURE, not the comment. NOT FIXED THERE because the plan's own Global Constraint makes the aside the single scroller deliberately: choosePane restores each pane's scroll offset through it and shell-layout-scroll.dom.test.ts pins that, so moving to a scrolling body inside a fixed frame is a layout decision spanning the plan and the bible rather than a task. OWNER: unassigned - the plan that next restructures the pane frame. SEVERITY: low for behaviour (nothing becomes unreachable; the footer is still reachable by scrolling) and medium as a bible conformance gap.

title: layer-panel.tsx is 838 lines, past the 800-line stop, and plan 2's Task 2 widened it while moving code out
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 2's task review. MEASURED: src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/layer-panel.tsx is 814 lines at f5012d2a, 838 at ddd9ed7b and 841 at 04646669, so Task 2 added 27 net lines even though it moved the object-action footer out of the module into LayerActions and into the pane footer slot. AGENTS.md sets 500 lines as a signal and 800 as a stop for normal source files. NOT SPLIT IN THE FIX ROUND because the file's seams are the panels it owns, so separating them is a refactor of the layer tree's own module rather than a fix to the panes' chrome, and putting a structural refactor under a task whose brief is a chrome change is how a fix round grows past its finding. OWNER: the plan that next restructures the layer panel. SEVERITY: low - a maintainability stop rather than a defect, and nothing the gates check reads line counts.

title: composition-panel.spec.ts:897 fails at base, because enterLayer waits for a layer-entry control the rendered row does not carry
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 2's fix round while running the browser specs that round was told to run, not by the task itself. MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: the spec case "a group entered inside a large document" fails deterministically at both ddd9ed7b and e8c2ec92, verified by stashing the fix round's work and running the single spec against the base tree - so it is neither the panes' chrome nor a flake. It was found amid four failures whose set differed between two 8-worker runs, and it is the one of the four that is deterministic. MECHANISM, as far as it is established: editor-canvas.ts:211's enterLayer waits for a [data-vigilia-layer-entry] control, and the rendered row does not carry one because layer-panel.tsx:732 gates it behind the showEnter attention rule. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED beyond that: whether the spec should drive the attention state before waiting, or the control should be present-but-quiet, is a design question this row does not decide. NOT FIXED HERE because it is a pre-existing red in a spec the active plan does not own. SEVERITY: medium - a deterministic red in the browser suite cannot be told from a regression without re-running that spec at base, which is what this row records.

title: The Add pane's data-vigilia-panel now scopes every add-pane locator to the whole pane, so a future asset control named with a shape word would collide
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 2's fix round and confirmed by its scoped re-review. The fix round deleted new-object-panel.ts:182's duplicate attribute and moved pane naming onto the pane itself (pane.tsx writes data-vigilia-panel={id} unconditionally), which is the right resolution - but it widens what that attribute's descendants mean. Spec locators rebuild-driver.ts:139 (addButton, hasText /^label$/), editor.spec.ts:31/789/838, composition-panel.spec.ts:1064 and author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts:73 now scope the Add pane, which also holds the asset host's buttons (asset-manager/panel.ts:30-35, labelled Import, Replace, Remove). MEASURED BENIGN TODAY: the shape filters match exact shape words and the getByRole name matches (Text, Gauge, Clock, Shape) are absent from the asset labels, and no case became ambiguous in the runs. NO CSS SCOPE CHANGED: no rule keys on a [data-vigilia-panel] button descendant, and every CSS rule on the attribute is ="layers", which sat on the pane before the fix too. NOT FIXED because nothing is broken to fix - the hazard is that a future asset control whose label is a shape word becomes ambiguous in rebuild-driver.ts:139, silently, and only in that spec. SEVERITY: low; the trigger is future work and the failure would be a strict-mode ambiguity rather than a wrong assertion.

title: publish-loop.spec.ts:380 is red in the ordered suite but passes alone, at base as well as at HEAD
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 3's implementer, which verified it against the base before reporting rather than assuming. MEASURED: with the working tree stashed and the bundle rebuilt at f8181c5f, the spec gives the same 1-failed/1-passed and the same Received: "e2e-publish-loop"; run on its own it passes. So it is ORDER-DEPENDENT rather than flaky, and it is not Task 3's change. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED: nothing here says whether an earlier case in the same file leaves state that a later one reads, or whether it is a timing artefact of a shared page. NOT FIXED because it is a pre-existing red in a spec the active plan does not own, and diagnosing it means running the file's cases in different orders. SEVERITY: medium - a spec that passes alone and fails in suite makes every full-run reading ambiguous, and it joins vg-135, vg-175, vg-196, vg-197 and vg-210 as rows that must be checked before a browser result is believed.

title: No gate runs biome check, so organizeImports is never enforced and import order drifts unchecked
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 3's task review, which noticed two files it was reviewing carried unapplied import ordering and that nothing in the repo would ever have said so. MEASURED: src/web/package.json defines format (biome format --write ..), format:check (biome format ..), lint (biome lint ..) and lint:fix, and .github/workflows/ci.yml:38 and :41 run format:check and lint - but no npm script and no CI step runs biome check. In Biome 2.x organizeImports is an assist action that biome check runs and that neither biome format nor biome lint does, so a file whose imports are out of order passes every gate the repo has. The concrete instance: publish-control.tsx:7-8 and shell-layout.tsx:1 at 2eeb4516 were both unorganised. NOT FIXED because adding a step to the repo's verification surface is a decision about the gates rather than about a task, and the two files were ordered by hand in Task 3's fix round instead. OWNER: unassigned. SEVERITY: low - style debt rather than a defect, and nothing downstream reads import order.

title: HostingStore never polls, so an out-of-band host change leaves the editor's live indicator stale until a reload
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 3's task review as a caveat, then MEASURED by the controller against the source. HostingStore (packages/editor/src/editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx:201-282) reads the host once in its constructor (:207-209) and re-emits only from its own actions - toggle() emits on the success path (:273-280) and on the refusal path (:261-270), and read() is public. So the review's phrasing 'read() runs only in the constructor' overstates it: the store does follow its own writes.
