title: At the bible's 246px the Composition row fits its role column by one pixel, and the attended row clips its name and key, and no test can see either
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 1'S TASK REVIEW (2026-10-10), NOT BY A FAILING TEST - that is the finding. Plan 4 moved the Composition pane to the bible section 7.3 width of 246px (editor-shell.css:96, grid-template-columns: 46px 246px minmax(0, 1fr) 276px), superseding the 360px plan 2 had measured. At that width the worst name in the starter is group-trends-card, whose uiCopy role reads "Performance trends": it overflowed the row by 11px, so the implementer re-cut the row's mark slot from 40px to 28px (editor-shell.css:145) and it now fits with ONE PIXEL of slack on the one font stack measured. THE ROLE IS flex:none and is the only statement of what a row is on four rows in five, so a font stack or DPI that renders a hair wider clips it mid-word. NOTHING CATCHES IT: tests/e2e/composition-panel.spec.ts:205-206 asserts directions only (the role costs names; the shipped column clips at least as many as the superseded one) and never a pixel, so the case stays green while the role clips. WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the 246px is bible-mandated so the constraint is not negotiable here; the reviewer offered 26px as a one-number fix, but that does not remove a clip, it moves it from the role to the mark - the column the row is designed to give up - and nothing measured which loss is worse, so the correct behaviour needs a design decision. Plan 4 Task 2 RE-CUT AND RE-MEASURED IT (2026-10-10, commit f94f0f7a), and the answer is worse than the one-pixel fit this row was filed on. On the worst row - all four controls (twisty, rename, eye, lock) AND a bound key - the row is 205px wide with 61px of room kept, and BOTH the key column and the layer name are clipped at 246px (annotations four-control-row-width-px=205, four-control-room-kept-px=61, four-control-key-clipped=true, four-control-name-clipped=true; every structural figure identical across two gate runs, only the millisecond figures moved). It is the SELECTED or ATTENDED row that loses its name, not the resting one, and the controls that cost it are the 26px boxes bible section 5 mandates, so the plan is not free to shrink them and bible section 173 wants the name readable - the two constraints meet here. STILL OPEN, AND NOW A DESIGN DECISION RATHER THAN A PATCH: choose between narrowing the mark slot, shortening the role copy, reserving less room when a row carries all four controls, or accepting the clip on the attended row, then pin the choice with a measurement rather than a direction. Not fixed on the fly because the correct behaviour needs that decision (AGENTS.md). Task 10's ratchet and Task 12's register pass are where the choice is expected to surface. PLAN 4 TASK 3 EXTENDS THIS ROW (2026-10-10, commit 96099ba8, found by its task review): the SAME worst string at the SAME 246px width clips in the Add pane too — the card tile draws "Performance trends" as 86px of label into a 41px box in the four-column diagram grid, and the other seven card names fit. Same cause, same width, same string, so it is recorded here rather than filed as a second row. The accessibility half is discharged separately and in this task (the tile now discloses its full name on hover/focus, proved by a case that fails without it); the CLIPPING remains this row's design decision. CONTROLLER MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-10 (built bundle at 788f1448, default Composition pane): the role column does NOT fit by one pixel - .vigilia-layer-role's right edge is 291 with the row's clip at 295 and the pane column at 308, so it has 4px to the row and 17px to the column; the element that gives up width is the NAME (.vigilia-layer-name is flex: 1 1 auto with min-width 43.3px and ellipsises in nine of the ten starter rows, its glyph run reaching 256 against a box ending at 246). The role's real problem at this width is not its own slack but the 4px the absolutely-positioned .vigilia-layer-state overlaps it by - see vg-265, which owns that measurement.

title: The elevation ladder is declared twice as --elev-1..3 and --shadow-raised/--shadow-overlay, and three of the five names are consumed by nothing
detail: FOUND WHILE DESIGNING THE DESIGN.MD ADOPTION SPEC (2026-10-10), NOT BY A FAILING TEST. editor-shell.css's @theme static block declares the bible section 3 elevation ladder -- --elev-1 (0 8px 20px #00000059), --elev-2 (0 18px 44px #00000099) and --elev-3 (0 24px 60px #000000b3) -- and beside it two older shadow names that match no level the bible states: --shadow-raised (0 12px 28px #0000003d) and --shadow-overlay (0 18px 44px #0006). MEASURED USES (grep for var() over packages/ and tests/): --shadow-raised 2, --elev-1 2, --elev-2 2, --shadow-overlay 0, --elev-3 0. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED: the two pairs may be deliberately different rather than duplicates -- a softer raised shadow on one surface, with the bible ladder added later -- and nothing in the repo says which, which is why this is filed rather than fixed on the fly (AGENTS.md: a cause that is not established gets a row, not a guess). WHY IT MATTERS: one concept (how deep a surface sits) has two vocabularies and nothing reconciles them, so a new surface can be raised by either; and the same block's own comment says the declared-and-never-consumed state is what the token ratchet exists to shrink, so three dead names is that state left standing. NOT ANSWERED BY THE DESIGN.MD ADOPTION: that work (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-design-md-replaces-the-bible-design.md) deliberately changes no runtime value, and the DESIGN.md token schema has no elevation or shadow group, so elevation stays prose there. CLOSE THIS once the two vocabularies are reconciled to one ladder with a reason recorded for any name that survives.

title: Sixty-seven organizeImports findings sit in the tree invisible to every gate, because nothing in the repo ever runs biome check
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER WHILE MEASURING TASK 5 OF PLAN 4 (2026-10-10), NOT BY A FAILING TEST. THE MEASUREMENT: from src/web, npx biome check .. reports 67 errors over 605 files, and all 67 are assist/source/organizeImports (Sort these imports) in 67 distinct files, from packages/editor/src/components/ui/control-select.tsx to packages/host/src/main.ts. npx biome lint .. over the same tree reports 0 errors and 0 warnings. THE GAP: src/web/package.json wires lint to biome lint .. and format:check to biome format .., and neither subcommand runs the assist category - assist is a third mode that only biome check reaches. biome.json carries no assist key at all, so organizeImports is on by default and fires only under check, which no npm script invokes. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the only biome steps the repo has (format:check at line 38, lint at line 41) and neither is a check. So the rule is enabled, the tree violates it 67 times, and no local gate, no CI step and no hook will ever say so. WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC: import order in this tree is authored by hand and drifts, and the drift is invisible in both directions - the gate cannot fail, and an implementer who runs npx biome check on the files they touched sees findings that no gate will ever surface or fix, which reads as pre-existing noise. Plan 4 Task 4 report hit exactly that and recorded an organizeImports finding on card-insert-surfaces.dom.test.tsx as pre-existing and untouched rather than as a signal. FILED RATHER THAN FIXED because the fix is a decision with a blast radius, not a patch: running biome check in CI, or wiring assist into the lint script, turns 67 pre-existing findings into a red gate in the commit that does it, and whether this repo wants import order enforced at all is a call nobody has made. The two candidate shapes - add check to the gates and fix the 67 in the same commit, or leave check out and delete the expectation - each need a ruling first. NOT URGENT: nothing is pushed, so no CI is red today.

title: A refused colour in the Tokens pane is announced to nobody, and the control set has no channel for an invalid-but-still-editable field
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 5 TASK REVIEW (2026-10-10, commit ebe1743b), NOT BY A FAILING TEST - and that is half the finding. THE REGRESSION: before Task 5 the pane relied on the platform's own refusal, `reportValidity()` on the colour input, which announced itself to assistive technology for free. Task 5 replaced it with a local error state rendered as a bare `

` (paint-list.tsx:254-258) that is a SIBLING of the field it belongs to (the ControlText at paint-list.tsx:232-253) and is associated with nothing: no `aria-describedby`, no `aria-invalid`, no live region. A screen-reader user types an unpaintable colour, the edit is refused, and the refusal is silent. WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS NOT AVAILABLE: the control set already has this mechanism - control-well.tsx renders a reason element and control-text.tsx:70-71 wires `aria-describedby` to it - but it is reachable only through the `refused` prop, and `refused` also sets `readOnly` (control-text.tsx:68) and `aria-disabled`. That is right for a value the DOCUMENT refuses (a locked object) and wrong here: this value is refused because the author just typed something the engine cannot paint, and the field has to stay editable so they can type a different one. Using `refused` would trap them on the stale-but-valid value. Nor can the pane wire it itself: `ControlProps.data` is typed `Readonly>` (control-well.tsx:24-32), so there is no aria pass-through, and the pane does not own the input element. THE REAL FIX IS A CONTROL-SET CONCEPT - a channel for invalid-but-still-editable, distinct from `refused`, carrying `aria-invalid` plus a described-by reason without `readOnly`. That is why this is filed rather than fixed on the fly (AGENTS.md): the cause is established but the fix is a new concept in a different owner - the control set, built and closed in plan 1 - it spans subsystems, and it needs a design decision about how many refusal shapes the control set should carry. It is not Task 5's to invent, and a second ad-hoc `

` in the next pane would make three. THE TEST GAP THAT LET IT THROUGH: tests/e2e/editor.spec.ts:672-697 proves the refusal HAPPENS (not-a-colour is refused, the field stays on #123456, rgb(1, 2, 3) clears it) but never that it is announced, and jsdom cannot see platform bubbles either - so neither layer could have gone red. CLOSE THIS by adding the editable-invalid channel to the control set, wiring the Tokens pane's colour field to it, and pinning that a refused value carries `aria-invalid` and a described-by reason while remaining editable.

title: The React control set prints its refusals in hardcoded English, so a pane's own invalid-value copy became unreachable
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 8 (2026-10-10, commit 9f6252a8) IN TASK REVIEW, AND FIRST FILED WRONGLY - this row replaces a framing that was measured false, and the correction is the reason it reads as narrowly as it does. THE FINDING: `ControlNumber` (components/ui/control-number.tsx:94,99,103,107,111) writes its five refusal sentences as hardcoded English - "a value is required", "not a number", "a whole number", "at least 1", "at most 16384" - while every other user-visible string in the editor comes from `uiCopy`. The control it replaced took its message as a parameter defaulting to `uiCopy.panels.invalidNumber` (number-field.ts:88), so the artboard size pair used to say "That value cannot be applied. Enter a number in range." (ui-copy.ts:650) and now says "at most 16384". That key is not dead - it is still read by number-field.ts:88, reachable only from the settings path (settings-field.ts:115 is `numberField`'s only shipped caller) - so one editor now carries two vocabularies for one refusal depending on which numeric control a surface happens to use. WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED ON THE FLY (AGENTS.md): the cause is established but the fix is a design decision in a different owner - the copy rules are plan 6's and the control set is plan 1's, built and closed - and neither side obviously moves: `ControlNumber` could take its message from `uiCopy` (a new key, and a copy dependency the control set does not have today), or `uiCopy.panels.invalidNumber` could be retired and the hardcoded strings promoted into it (the copy module acquiring keys only one control uses). WHY THE FIRST FILING WAS WRONG, because the mistake is the useful part: I filed this as "a number field no longer says what it will accept until after a value is refused", asserting the old pane printed its bound (1-16384) at rest. It did not. `boundLine` is rendered only by `numberField` (number-field.ts:53-59), and the artboard pane used `linkedPair` (artboard-panel.ts:19,150 at 21a5135e), which calls `numberInput` directly (linked-pair.ts:1,55,66) - so no artboard author ever saw that line and the discoverability loss described did not occur. The task reviewer measured it three ways (`git log -S` over the file's whole history finds no `numberField`/`boundLine`/`field-bound`; the pane's own old tests never mention them; settings-field.ts is `numberField`'s only caller) and the controller re-read linked-pair.ts to confirm. The implementer's report Deviation 4 made the same claim, so a subagent's description of code it had already replaced became a register row unmeasured - a verify-the-claim failure, not a reasoning one, and the check that catches it is one grep of the base commit. Related: vg-113 (unit display options hardcoded English), vg-263 (a refused colour announced to nobody - the other half of the same question, what the control set owes an author whose value it will not take).

title: The Composition row's role word is painted over by the layer-state slot at the rail's normative 246px - it is covered, not clipped, and the row's own proposed check would pass
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 11 (2026-10-10) WHILE CAPTURING THE PANES FOR THE PARITY GATE, NOT BY A FAILING TEST - and that half of it stands: no gate in this repo renders the panes (design-language.spec.ts's spacing gate reads [data-fixture-root] *, carried only by the synthetic control-fixture.tsx), so the only way this was going to be seen is a person looking at a capture. WHAT THE CAPTURES SHOW: in three registered captures - composition-panel-starter, composition-panel-two-hundred and the new pane-composition - the last glyph of every row's role word is not fully rendered at 1x (Networ / Storag / Cloc / Tex), while the name column beside it ellipsises properly. RE-MEASURED BY THE CONTROLLER (2026-10-10, built bundle at 788f1448, live editor preview, default Composition pane, all ten rows), AND THE FRAMING CHANGES: the role word is not clipped, it is COVERED. Nothing reports overflow - .vigilia-layer-role's glyph extent equals its box on all ten rows (a Range over the text node gives Network 250-291 = 41px against a box of 250-291, and Performance trends 196-291 = 95px against a box of 196-291), the element is overflow: visible with text-overflow: clip, and .vigilia-layer-row reports scrollWidth == clientWidth == 220 with its box at 75-295 and the grid column at 62-308. THE CAUSE IS A SLOT THE ROW PAINTS OVER ITSELF: .vigilia-layer-state is position: absolute with left: 212.4px, right: 2px and width 6px, so it occupies x 287-293 - inside the row's own 220px box, but 4px across the role's right edge at 291 - and it carries background-color: rgba(239, 249, 242, 0.75). It is empty (, no children, no ::before/::after content), so that fill is all it paints, and a 75%-opaque six-pixel panel-coloured block laid over the role's last glyphs is what reads as a cut glyph at 1x. THIS ALSO CLOSES THE ARITHMETIC THE ROW COULD NOT CLOSE: nothing consumes the missing width, because no width is missing - the 289-293 range the row measured the cut at IS the state slot's own box. The row had the answer in hand and filed it as a width puzzle: it named the state controls as laid over the row edge by position: absolute, then asked only whether they consume width. They do not; they cover. WHAT THIS DOES TO THE ROW'S OWN CLOSURE CHECK: it would pass, so it is not the gate. 'The role element must not report scrollWidth > clientWidth inside the row at 246px' is satisfied today (41 == 41) and will stay satisfied however the overlap is fixed. The check has to be geometric or painted: the role's box must not intersect the state slot's box, or the capture must assert the last glyph's pixels. FILED RATHER THAN FIXED (AGENTS.md): the cause is now established, but more than one owner could fix it and the fix is a design decision - reserve the slot's width in the row's layout so the role stops before it, take the state out of the role's tail, or move it - and no plan owns that yet, so it needs a ruling first. HOW TO CLOSE IT: make one capture-driven geometric check (role.right <= state.left at 246px) and re-capture the three Composition images.

title: editor-shell.css is in no gate and no plan: the ratchet parses CSS but its list names no .css file, and 94 violations sit behind that
detail: FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING PLAN 5 TASK 1 (2026-10-10, commit 13984ab9), CARRIED AS A `Discovered, not fixed:` TRAILER IN THAT COMMIT, AND MATERIALISED HERE WITH THE MEASUREMENT THE TRAILER ONLY SAMPLED. The trailer named the `.editor-shell-dialog*` rules' off-scale px; the file's exposure is larger. MEASURED at 13984ab9: `scripts/design-tokens.gated.json`'s `gated` array (51 entries) names NO `.css` file (`grep -c '.css'` over it returns 0), while the guard itself parses CSS - `scripts/design-tokens.mjs:181`'s `const isCss = /.css$/.test(path)` selects a declaration-property parser for off-scale px, and eight of its self-test cases are CSS (:235-264, including "an off-scale px spacing is a violation" over `a.css`). Run with `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css` as its only gated file, the guard reports 94 violations across 1 file and exits 1: 23 spacing-property values (padding 11, margin 4, margin-right 3, gap 3, right 1, margin-top 1 - 2px, 3px, 7px, 9px, 11px, 13px, 18px, 62px, 92px, 122px among them), 11 hex literals outside the `@theme` definition block (`#ffffff1f`, `#7dd3fc`, `#0009` ...), and 60 off-scale px in properties that are not spacing (the 246px rail column, 276px, 340px, 560px, 720px, 980px). THE SECOND INSTRUMENT DOES NOT CLOSE IT: `tests/e2e/design-language.spec.ts:10-11` asserts that every gated element's resolved spacing is on the bible's scale, but it reads `[data-fixture-root] *` (:452), and that root is the control fixture's own `.editor-shell` (`control-fixture.tsx:60`) - so a rule reaching a fixture element is enforced from the browser and a shell-only rule is not. NEITHER REMAINING PLAN OWNS IT: `settings-and-appearance.md:529` and `iconography-and-copy.md:501` both record only the file's *hex* count as "the before-state for whatever follows the redesign", and neither adds the file to `gated`, so the conversion has no task - and whether the file should be gated at all, against a per-element browser assertion being the better instrument for a stylesheet whose values are mostly layout dimensions, is a design decision rather than a task. Not fixed in Task 1: adding the file would fail the guard over 94 pre-existing values, which is a plan's worth of work and not this task's. OWNER: whoever owns `scripts/design-tokens.gated.json` and the Acceptance section's "no off-scale spacing in a surface". PLAN 7 TASK 6 MEASURED IT AND NARROWED IT (2026-10-11, artefact 45ede8e4, gate work at 43e24bc5; the task review re-measured independently and the numbers held). The title's 94 is superseded - the file holds **61** violations today: 7 hex-literal, 30 off-scale px and 24 spacing px. Task 6 arrived at 67 and fixed the six whose fix is a verifiable no-op (`--shadow-raised` for `0 12px 28px #0000003d` at `editor-shell.css:358`, three `13px` for `var(--text-md)` at `:352`, and a dead `var(--shell-accent, #7dd3fc)` fallback whose token is declared on `:root` and all five palette blocks), each checked against the declaration rather than against the built output alone. THE FILE IS NOT CLEANABLE BY SUBSTITUTION, and that is why this row is still open: 24 of the 61 are spacing values whose section 3 substitution moves pixels, which is a design pass and not a task, and three of them (`margin-right: 62px/92px/122px`, `editor-shell.css:1932/1937/1942`) cannot be expressed as any section 3 step at all. The path was added to `design-tokens.gated.json`, the gate run, and the path withdrawn in the same pass - the list's contract is the files already converted (`design-tokens.mjs:9`) and ADR-0040:12 gives the reason, that a gate which starts red and stays red is turned off. OWNER: unchanged, and now with a measurement rather than an estimate. PLAN 8 TASK 9 (2026-10-11) RE-MEASURED IT AND CAPPED THE COUNT, AND THE COUNT DID NOT FALL. Measured at HEAD: **61** violations - 6 hex-literal, 31 off-scale px, 24 spacing px - so the classes moved while the total held. The two edits that moved them: the overlay's `#0009` scrim became `var(--elev-scrim)` (one hex gone, plan 8 Task 3, `51245173`) and the modal's navigation column became `width: 150px` (one off-scale added, plan 8 Task 2, `5e8ba2b0`), and a diff of the two violation sets against `43e24bc5` shows exactly those two and nothing else. NO NO-OP REMAINED TO FIX: all 61 violation literals were compared with the 114 custom-property values this file declares and none equals one, so plan 7 Task 6's substitution rule - which closed six of the 67 it arrived at - has nothing left to convert here. THE CEILING NOW LIVES IN `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` AS `CEILINGS`, a second instrument over this one file: `max: 58` (the 61 less the three named exemptions), failing when the counted violations rise above it, so it is green at HEAD and can only fall; the comparison is strict, so a count at 58 passes and 59 fails. THE THREE INEXPRESSIBLES ARE EXEMPT BY NAME AND REASON in that constant rather than in a comment: `margin-right: 62px`, `92px` and `122px` are one class - the layer row's reserved slot for n controls, `6 + 26n + 4(n-1)`, which is section 3's own 26px row rhythm plus its 6px and 4px steps and so lands off the step table by construction (`n=1` reaches the step 32 only because its gap term is zero, so 62 is not a value a step can spell). No section 3 step can express any of the three, and correcting one would move the reserved width and let the icons cover the key again. An exemption that matches nothing is itself a failure, so a licence nobody needs reddens the gate rather than sitting there silently. FOUR OF `vg-325`'s SIX DIVERGENCES ARE COUNTED BY THE CEILING, AND NAMED HERE AT `file:line` - A COUNT NAMES NOTHING, AND THE CEILING'S OWN *NAMED* VALUES ARE ITS THREE EXEMPTIONS, NOT THESE: the Close's `margin-top: 18px` (`editor-shell.css:1400`), the rail's `gap: 3px` (`:872`) and the asset buttons' `padding: 4px 7px` at `:1148` and `:1189`; the other two are not violations here (the asset-button text is a role disagreement and the nav column's `padding: 0` is off no scale). NO CLAIM OF FIXED IS MADE for the 24 spacing values or the three inexpressibles, in the commit or here. THE INSTRUMENT THIS TASK ADDED HAS ITS OWN CEILING: a count sees a rise and not a swap, so correcting one violation while another arrives leaves it green - filed as `vg-327`.

title: Three decision records name `PaletteMenu.choose` as a palette writer, and plan 5 Task 2 deleted that module
detail: FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING PLAN 5 TASK 2 (2026-10-10, commit 64fea389), CARRIED AS A `Discovered, not fixed:` TRAILER IN THAT COMMIT. MEASURED: `docs/decisions/0035-the-shells-palette-resolves-at-the-element-and-the-os-is-its-fallback.md:63` names `PaletteMenu.choose` in its prose and `:141` names it inside the table row "Writers that apply the palette today | **2** (`createShellLayout`, `PaletteMenu.choose`)" - which is presented as a measurement; `grep -rn "PaletteMenu|palette-menu" src/web --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` now returns nothing, so the module is gone and the palette is applied from the settings tab this plan builds. The implementer named the same names appearing in `0036` and `0039` as the adjacent case and did not edit an ADR. WHY THIS IS A ROW RATHER THAN THE NATURE OF A DATED RECORD: `docs/decisions/README.md:36` gives an ADR a `Status: accepted | superseded by NNNN` field, so this repo's convention for a decision that stops being true is a dated, deliberate act rather than an edit to the body - and a reader who opens 0035 to learn how the shell's palette is applied is sent to a module that does not exist, with nothing on the page saying so. The cost of the fix is one note line per record. NOT FIXED IN TASK 2 because whether a live-looking file reference inside a decision record is maintained is a ruling about the register's own practice, not a task's edit. OWNER: whoever owns `docs/decisions/`. Related: `vg-198` (the docs map's `adr/` against the live `decisions/`).

title: `editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx` is 916 lines, past the 800-line stop, and four of plan 5's six tasks open it
detail: FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING PLAN 5 TASK 2 (2026-10-10, commit 64fea389), CARRIED AS A `Discovered, not fixed:` TRAILER IN THAT COMMIT. MEASURED: `wc -l` on `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx` is 916 at that commit, against 912 at its base (`6cafe996`) - so the condition is pre-existing and this task widened it by four lines. `AGENTS.md` sets 500 lines as a signal and 800 as a stop for normal source files. The same class already has a row: `vg-209` (layer-panel.tsx at 838, widened by plan 2's Task 2 while moving code out of it). WHAT MAKES THIS ONE A DECISION RATHER THAN AN EDIT: plan 5's Task 3, Task 4 and Task 5 each name the file in their Files block (11 mentions across the plan), so a split would have to land inside the active plan's own surface and be carried by whichever task does it, and a split of a file that mounts four panels and owns the shell's hosts is a design decision about the shell's boundaries, not a tidy-up. NOT FIXED IN TASK 2 because a task does not open a refactor of the file it is editing. OWNER: whoever owns the editor-shell's composition root.

title: The design-language fixture proves the shell's global focus rule, not the portalled control's own, because it nests the row inside `.editor-shell`
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 2'S SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-10, over 64fea389..eba81b2a), WHICH CORRECTED THE FINDING ITS OWN FIX ROUND HAD FILED. WHAT THE COMMIT TRAILER CLAIMED (commit eba81b2a): that `components/ui/control-choice-row.tsx:54`'s `focus-visible:outline-*` classes are inert, because `editor-shell.css:1048`'s `.editor-shell :is(button, …):focus-visible` out-specifies them. MEASURED: the specificity half is true only for an element INSIDE `.editor-shell` - the shell rule is unlayered while the Tailwind utility lands in `@layer utilities` (built CSS: `.focus-visible\:outline-2:focus-visible` at offset 20264 inside `@layer utilities{` @7990, the shell rule unlayered at 39365) and its specificity (0,3,0) beats the class's (0,2,0). But the Appearance tab does not ship inside `.editor-shell`: the modal is a Base UI Dialog portalled to `document.body` (`components/ui/dialog.tsx:44-60`), a sibling of `#app` rather than a descendant of `.editor-shell` (`palette.ts:93-99`, `shell-layout.tsx:699`), so there the shell rule cannot match at all and the control's own classes are the SOLE focus treatment. The CSS author knew: `.editor-shell-settings-tab:focus-visible` and `.editor-shell-settings-panel:focus-visible` (`editor-shell.css:1246,1250`) exist precisely because the dialog is portalled, and no equivalent rule exists for the choice row. ACTING ON THE TRAILER WOULD HAVE BEEN A DEFECT - deleting those classes as redundant strips the shipped product's focus ring, while the design-language fixture stays green because there the shell rule paints the outline. THE REAL FINDING IS THE PROOF-CONTEXT GAP: `control-fixture.tsx:145-175` mounts `ControlChoiceRow` inside the fixture's own `.editor-shell` (`:62`), and `design-language.spec.ts`'s new §4e case (`~:866-1030`) asserts a `solid` outline of at least 2px there - which the shell's global rule supplies. So §4e passes even when the control's own focus classes paint nothing, and cannot detect a regression in the treatment that actually ships on the portalled modal. The implementer's own red proof demonstrates exactly this: removing the shell focus rule reddened the case with `paints the browser's auto ring, not §5's solid outline`, while the classes were the thing under test. NOT FIXED HERE because the fix is a decision about how a portalled surface is measured (a second fixture outside `.editor-shell`, or a browser case on the real modal) rather than a one-line change, and this plan's Task 6 owns the capture. OWNER: whoever owns `components/ui/` and the design-language fixture's context.

title: The editor bundle has no product-version source, so the About tab can name no version for Vigilia itself
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 4'S STEP 1 (2026-10-10), BY READING, NOT BY TESTING. Measured with `grep -rn version packages/editor/src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v .test. | grep -vi canvas`: the only hits are the theme's own release version (editor-session.ts:1092 bumpSemanticVersion; panes/document/metadata-fields.tsx:101 metadata?.version) and unrelated words (Fabric's scene version 7.4.0 in new-fabric-theme.ts:188, the qr-symbol.tsx version, storage-key prose) - not one product version. `grep -rn 'VERSION|SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION' packages/host/src/main.ts packages/renderer-core/src/theme/document.ts` finds the host's const VERSION = "0.1.0" at packages/host/src/main.ts:34, Node-side and logging Vigilia v${VERSION} at :250 and not in the editor bundle, and SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1 at packages/renderer-core/src/theme/document.ts:9, a schema number this build can read but which is not the product's version. packages/editor/package.json is 0.0.0 and packages/editor/vite.config.ts injects no define. So the About tab (landed in the same commit) renders the schema version and the open document's release version, and nothing claiming to be Vigilia's own version. WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: giving the product one version string both the host CLI and the editor bundle import is a host change that needs a decision rather than a task, and more than one owner could fix it, so it sits outside plan 5's scope.

title: The layer row's attended state slot can intercept a press meant for the row, so a click on a name may reach its visibility or lock control
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 4A PART I'S SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-10, over 50797965..b3805273). MEASURED, in the test harness: `tests/e2e/rebuild-driver.ts:206-222` presses a layer row through `.vigilia-layer-name` at the element's LEFT END rather than at its default centre, and its own comment records why - the centre is intercepted, and five cases of `author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts` hung on it. The comment names the interceptor: the attended row's absolutely-positioned state slot (`editor-shell.css:1707-1712`, `position: absolute; right: 2px; top: 0; height: 26px`), which sits over the name because the name is `flex: 1 1 auto` (`editor-shell.css:1658`). WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether this is a product-side hazard or only a Playwright fixed-point problem. A real pointer that hovers a row to click it has already revealed that row's state slot, so a press aimed at the row can land on the slot's own controls (visibility, lock) instead of selecting the layer - but nobody has measured the slot's width against the row's, or what a press at the name's centre actually hits in a browser. The CSS author calls the related shift deliberate: the attended row's name narrows by whatever its key does not take, "charged to the one row the pointer is on, and it is deliberate" (`editor-shell.css:1700-1708`). That states the SHIFT is intended; it does not say the slot may swallow a press aimed at the row. NOT FIXED HERE because the cause is not established and the fix, if needed, is a layout decision about the attended row rather than a test edit; the harness works around it, which also means nothing reddens if the layout changes. OWNER: whoever owns the layer row's layout (`selection-inspector/` and `editor-shell.css`'s `.vigilia-layer-*` rules).

title: Two editor specs claim a fresh starter trips the dirty guard, which the session mechanism contradicts, while a third records the opposite sample
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 4A PART I'S SECOND SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-10, over b3805273..846e451c), which retired the same claim from a fourth file. THE CONTRADICTION: `tests/e2e/author-journey-display.spec.ts:231-235` and `tests/e2e/composition-panel.spec.ts:556-558` both assert that a fresh starter "counts as unsaved work", so opening another theme asks the dirty guard. The mechanism says otherwise: `editor-session.ts:1004-1020` asks only when `isDirty`, and `persistence-manager/index.ts:34,42` compares the current key against `#savedDocument` - the snapshot the session opened on, built at `editor-session.ts:498-501`. `editor-main.ts:233-238`'s `onNew` mounts a fresh session, so a document that has just been created IS its own baseline. MEASURED, by the implementer, against the built bundle during round 2: after Create a fresh editor shows zero `[role="dialog"]`, and Open library opens the chooser with no question - which is why the fourth file's comment (`tests/e2e/rebuild-driver.ts:132-138`) was corrected in `bdce766e`. WHAT MAKES IT A FINDING RATHER THAN A TYPO: `tests/e2e/reference-theme.spec.ts:490-492` records the OPPOSITE sample - five prompts in six save-then-Ctrl+N rounds on an unchanged starter. So at least one of the three is wrong, they disagree about product behaviour rather than wording, and nobody has measured which path differs (Ctrl+N against the menubar's New is the obvious candidate, and neither the session nor the specs distinguish them). WHY THE SPECS SURVIVE: `answerDialogIfShown` tolerates the absence of a dialog, so a spec asserting a prompt that never comes still passes - the tolerant call was the right one: the driver's absolute "asks nothing on the path every caller takes" is not what `reference-theme` observed. NOT FIXED HERE because establishing which claim is true needs a browser run per path, and the fix is to the claim rather than to behaviour. OWNER: whoever owns the editor's browser journeys (`tests/e2e/`) and the dirty-guard's own contract (`persistence-manager/`).

title: No command runs the rebuild or display Playwright suites, because playwright.config.ts testIgnores them and nothing passes --config, so their reds are invisible to every gate
detail: SPLIT OUT OF vg-119 BY PLAN 5 TASK 4A PART I'S CLOSE (2026-10-10), because vg-119's title carries two independent claims and only one of them was fixed. vg-119's first half - the display proof suite red on a run colour the document does not carry - is verified fixed (see that row's addendum). Its second half, "and no command runs that suite", is this row, and it is the reason the first half stayed red long enough to be filed at all. MEASURED BY THE CONTROLLER at head 846e451c: `src/web/playwright.config.ts:114-124` puts both projects' `testIgnore` over `REBUILD_SPEC`, `DISPLAY_SPEC`, `HOST_SPECS` and `PUBLISH_SPEC`; `playwright.rebuild.config.ts:20` and `playwright.display.config.ts:21` are the only runners those two specs have, and each matches exactly one of them; **`grep -n -- '--config' src/web/package.json` returns nothing, and `grep -rn -- '--config' .github/workflows/` returns nothing** - `.github/workflows/ci.yml:104` runs bare `npx playwright test`, and `visual-evidence.yml:49` runs `npx playwright test --project=… --grep=…`, both against the default config. So the two suites run only when a human or an agent types `--config` by hand. CONSEQUENCE, and it is not hypothetical: the harness reds that plans 3, 4 and 5 each discovered separately - vg-119's colour, vg-253's 16 selectOption sites, and the `sectionIds` scoping plan 5 Task 4a part i fixed on the fly - were all reachable by a plain `npx playwright test --config playwright.display.config.ts` and by nothing else, so every gate reported green while three suites were red. `inspector-sections.spec.ts` is in the DEFAULT config, which is why the same round's re-point break was reachable - and was still missed, because the round ran targeted greps rather than the suite. NOT FIXED HERE because the fix is a decision about the gate rather than about the specs: adding a script changes what every future session pays for a full run, and the display suite alone took 11.4 minutes when vg-119 was measured. OWNER: whoever owns the browser-gate scripts (`src/web/package.json` and `.github/workflows/`). Related: vg-192 (tests/e2e belongs to no tsconfig, so a type error there is caught by neither typecheck nor Playwright) - the same class of invisible-to-every-gate defect.

title: FontPicker has no production mount in any package, so its 357 lines and 984-line test are kept alive by tests alone while the live font surface is FontControls
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 4A PART II (2026-10-10, over 8c666ea1..9fa7b7b4). The implementer raised it as its own concern and the controller confirmed it independently. MEASURED at head 9fa7b7b4: `grep -rn 'FontPicker' packages/*/src` returns exactly two consumers, both tests - `packages/editor/src/ui-copy.test.ts:19,238` (which mounts it because a copy literal inside it would otherwise be invisible to the copy audit) and `packages/editor/src/font-picker/font-picker.dom.test.tsx`. No production module in any package renders it and it is not in the editor's barrel, so nothing a user can reach shows this component. THE LIVE SURFACE IS A DIFFERENT ONE: `packages/editor/src/panes/tokens/preset-list.tsx`'s `FontControls` (`:357`) owns the font controls an author actually uses, and it was already on `ControlSelect` (`:370`, `:402`, `:446`) before this task - plan 4 converted it. So the product's zero-native-select outcome did not depend on this file. WHY IT STILL MATTERED, AND WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN NOTHING: the three native `<select>`s at `font-picker.tsx:233,260,279` were the last in the editor's source, so converting them is what makes the census true (`grep -rnE '<select|type="range"' packages/editor/src` now returns comments only, zero non-comment production hits) - but the conversion touched ~155 source lines and ~253 test lines of a surface no user reaches, and the 984-line test file now exceeds the repo's 800-line stop keeping a dead component alive. The census is honest; the maintenance cost is not addressed by it. DECISION NEEDED, which is why this is not a one-line fix: either delete `FontPicker` and its test (and then `ui-copy.test.ts`'s mount of it, which exists only because it carries copy), or wire it to the surface it was written for - and nobody has established which. The archived font-catalogue plan is the likeliest origin. OWNER: whoever owns `font-picker/` and the Tokens pane's font controls.

title: keyboard.spec.ts:275 asserts the ? sheet's <kbd> count and never a chord, so no browser assertion distinguishes the effective chord from the default
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 5 (commit 4698f233), while proving every locator this plan re-pointed red. keyboard.spec.ts:275 is `await expect(sheet.locator("kbd")).toHaveCount(20)` — a COUNT, and the count is a property of the projection's membership (`productShortcutIds()` reads PRODUCT_SHORTCUTS either way), not of the chord each row prints. MEASURED, not reasoned: with `activeShortcuts()` in shortcut-manager/bindings.ts forced to return PRODUCT_SHORTCUTS, `npx playwright test keyboard.spec.ts` is 4 passed — the sheet still renders twenty rows and the file never rebinds, so nothing in it measures effective-vs-default. The behaviour IS guarded, but only in jsdom, and by two files: settings-keyboard.dom.test.tsx:190 and shortcut-reference.dom.test.tsx:70-91 both redden on the same break (`expected 'Ctrl+Shift+P' to be 'Ctrl+J'`). So a rebind that reached the Keyboard tab but stopped reaching the `?` sheet would ship. NOT FIXED HERE: it is not a broken locator but missing coverage, the fix is a rebinding step in a suite this plan does not own, and plan 6 (iconography-and-copy) owns the accessible-name/copy census this file sits in. The fix is one step in keyboard.spec.ts: rebind a chord through the tab, then assert the sheet prints the rebound chord rather than the default.

title: A browser run at playwright.config.ts's default worker count reports 30s locator timeouts as failures at a clean HEAD, on this box
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 5 (commit 4698f233), while taking a browser baseline at 7d31622c with nothing broken. The same four specs, same commit, same built bundle: 4 failed / 23 passed at the default 10 workers, every failure a 30s locator timeout or `no control matches [data-vigilia-palette-token]`; 27 passed at --workers=2. The four: keyboard.spec.ts:18 (locator.evaluate timeout), panel-labels.spec.ts:136 (locator.count timeout), panel-labels.spec.ts:208, shell-appearance.spec.ts:85 (locator.click waiting for visible/enabled/stable). CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED beyond "the machine": another session was busy on this box at the time (AGENTS.md, a long run holds the machine), and a single sample proves nothing about load or concurrency. It matters because a green suite read as red at the default worker count costs a false fix round: plan 5 Task 5's first browser baseline read exactly this way. ADJACENT ROW, DIFFERENT MECHANISM: vg-216 is two configs sharing test-results/ and deleting each other's traces; this is one run under load. What would settle it: run the same specs at 10 workers on an otherwise idle box, and if they still time out, bisect the worker count. CONTROLLER MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-11, WHICH NARROWS THE CAUSE RATHER THAN CONFIRMING THE ONE OFFERED: running the palette sweep (shell-appearance.spec.ts:97) ALONE at the default worker count, on an otherwise idle box at 7309eb1d, takes 8.6s and 8.5s in two consecutive runs, a whole run 12.1s - roughly 3.5x inside the 30s limit. So that test's own runtime is NOT what tips it over, and the most plausible inherent explanation is now falsified rather than merely untested. Plan 7 Task 2's fix round reported the same test timing out at 30,722ms with durations of 26.8s, 28.2s and 33.3s, and those figures did NOT reproduce: they were taken while this session was itself running Playwright against the same built bundle, which is exactly the contention this row's first paragraph names. The cause is therefore CONCURRENT BROWSER RUNS ON ONE BOX AND ONE BUNDLE, and two things follow - a red at the default count is worth nothing until the spec is re-run alone at the same commit (AGENTS.md already asks this, and this is the measurement that makes it cheap to obey), and raising this spec's timeout would not fix it, because on an idle box there is nothing to fix.

title: The ratchet's gated list has no rule for test files, so a hex literal or off-scale px asserted in a browser spec or a test fixture is unchecked
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 5 (its Step 1 coverage census), and sharpened by that task's review, which re-ran the checker over every file the plan touched rather than only the directory the report listed. MEASURED: 9 plan-touched files under src/web/ carry violations and are ungated, 6 of them under tests/e2e/ — editor.spec.ts, shell-appearance.spec.ts, rebuild-composition.ts, design-language.spec.ts, editor-rail.spec.ts, panel-labels.spec.ts. The other three are packages/editor/src/accessible-names.dom.test.ts (6 hexes), ui-copy.test.ts (7 hexes, theme fixtures at lines 114/133/141/142/146/367/368) and editor-shell.css (68), the last being vg-274. The gated list is not production-only by design: it names four test files (control.dom.test.tsx, control-choice-row.dom.test.tsx, display-switch.dom.test.tsx, settings-keyboard.dom.test.tsx, pane.dom.test.tsx and others), so the actual blind spot is that NO RULE decides which test files belong — membership was chosen file by file as each task converted something. CONSEQUENCE: a browser spec that pins a rendered colour or an off-scale spacing is a second owner of that value and no gate reads it; the violations measured today are mostly fixture data and selector strings rather than surfaces drifting, so this is a coverage hole, not nine defects. NOT FIXED HERE: widening the audit is plan 6's (2026-10-08-iconography-and-copy) and the plan's own Tasks 2 and 5 both say not to widen a coverage contract mid-sequence. SAME FAMILY as vg-274 (no .css file is gated) and vg-271 (a replacement control emits its own native input, which no <select> grep counts): each is the acceptance instrument claiming more coverage than it has. What would settle it: decide whether *.dom.test.tsx and tests/e2e are ratchet material and express that as a rule in the checker rather than as a list.

title: Nothing detects a committed capture that a later plan invalidates, so the shell-palette and keyboard-reference images sat two plans stale
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 6 (commit b602dd13), by reading the images it was about to re-capture rather than by any test. The seven files committed until then under docs/evidence/screenshots/ (shell-palette-* x6 and keyboard-reference) were pictures of the PRE-PLAN-2 shell: no rail, a `Layers | Insert | Assets | Document` pane bar, a palette chip in the header, `Save package`. Plan 2 rebuilt all of that, and nothing noticed, because a capture is only ever refreshed by the action that owns it running again — and every registry in docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md and docs/design/mockups/README.md names an action and a file, never a surface version or a plan that produced it. Re-captured here against rebuilt bundles. CONSEQUENCE: visual evidence in the repo can contradict the product for an arbitrary number of plans while every gate stays green, which is the opposite of what spec §13 asks a capture to be. NOT FIXED HERE: the fix is a detection mechanism (a marker recording the commit or shell generation each image was taken against, checked by a gate, or an ownership link from a surface to its captures), which is design work no active plan owns. What would settle it: decide who owns a capture's freshness and express it as a check rather than as a habit.

title: No document the test harness can load carries metadata.version, so the About tab's release row has no rendered proof and the parity gate cannot give it one
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 6 (commit b602dd13), while discharging Task 4's obligation that the parity capture show the About tab under a document carrying a release version. MEASURED, by scanning rather than by assuming: the starter and blank-theme builders write metadata with no version (new-fabric-theme.ts), and no fixture, fake-source theme, host envelope or library stub carries one, with every JSON under docs/ and src/web/packages/ scanned for the key. The six new settings captures therefore show the About tab with the release row ABSENT, asserted as absent by the run rather than tolerated, and no version was invented to make a better picture. So Task 4's release-version thread (the `releaseVersion` prop, fed by editor-main.ts:306's documentIdentity() through bridge.ts:174) still has no rendered proof anywhere. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any product path can produce a document carrying one - editor-session.ts:1092's bumpSemanticVersion suggests saving or publishing may bump a theme version, so the gap may be in what the harness can load rather than in the product. ADJACENT ROW, DIFFERENT OWNER: vg-279 is the product's own version, which the editor bundle has no source for; this is a document's version, which the harness cannot supply. What would settle it: trace bumpSemanticVersion's writers and either give the harness a loadable document that carries a version or record that no authoring path produces one.

title: ACTION_BUTTON is declared three times, one class string drifting across the three converted dialogs
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5'S WHOLE-BRANCH FINAL REVIEW, by reading the branch (opus, range 13370dc5..95a9bd11), and confirmed at source: the same class-name constant is declared in packages/editor/src/new-document-chooser.tsx:42, packages/editor/src/persistence-manager/replace-document-prompt.tsx:14 and packages/editor/src/theme-library-dialog.tsx:43, and used at new-document-chooser.tsx:253,261, replace-document-prompt.tsx:56 and theme-library-dialog.tsx:181,194,202,237. All three files are Task 4a's own output, so this is one concept with three owners the moment the second copy was written, and the review found them ALREADY DRIFTING. CONSEQUENCE: the dialog family's action button can diverge in treatment without any test noticing, which is exactly the drift the control set exists to prevent; it is also the shape AGENTS.md's one-owner rule names. NOT FIXED IN THE PLAN'S FINAL FIX ROUND because where the single declaration belongs is a decision (a new components/ui module, or the shared dialog primitive) and plan 6 (2026-10-08-iconography-and-copy) owns the single-owner census over the surfaces plans 1-5 landed. What would settle it: name the owner and import from it in all three, then delete the other two declarations.

title: RESERVED_LETTERS refuses a bare-modifier chord but not its Shift variant, so Ctrl+Shift+T, N and W are accepted as bindings and can never fire
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5'S WHOLE-BRANCH FINAL REVIEW, range 13370dc5..95a9bd11, and confirmed at source. shortcut-manager/bindings.ts:75 lists the reserved letters (l, n, p, q, r, t, w) and :299-305 refuses one only when `binding.modifier && binding.shift !== true`, so every Shift variant of those letters passes validation and is stored as a binding the browser owns: Ctrl+Shift+T (reopen closed tab), Ctrl+Shift+N (new private window) and Ctrl+Shift+W (close window) are taken in every Chromium build, so the author binds a chord and nothing ever happens. The rule's own doc comment states the Shift exclusion as fact without stating why, which is the claim-without-a-reason shape this plan hit repeatedly. CONSEQUENCE: the refusal exists precisely so the author is told where the limit is rather than binding a chord that will never fire, and it does not cover the case that is most likely to be tried. NOT FIXED IN THE PLAN'S FINAL FIX ROUND because the correct membership is a data decision - which chords the editor's actual browser matrix reserves - and over-refusing is its own defect (it would reject chords that do work). What would settle it: state which browsers the editor runs in, measure the Shift variants against them, and make the reserved rule and its comment reflect that evidence.

title: The mockup was never replaced where a surface was deliberately rebuilt differently, so the checked reference still draws a design the product does not ship
detail: FOUND BY THE USER on 2026-10-10, looking at the captures Task 6 had just re-taken: the gap between them and docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html is still large. WHICH GAP IS NOT ESTABLISHED: the new set includes -editorial (flat cream) and shell-palette-light captures, while the mockup is drawn on graphite (#0b0e12 per Task 6's D9), so comparing a light capture to it shows the palette rather than drift, and that has to be ruled out first by naming the files compared. THE USER THEN NAMED THE GAP, on 2026-10-10: "The panels on both sides, rail, top menu bar are all on their separate islands with rounded corners. That's completely different from the mockup. The graphite color scheme is different from the mockup's, too." Both are shell-level - plan 2's chrome and 0035's palette - not plan 6's glyphs or copy. The bible's own §3 makes panels `--radius-lg` (8px) and reserves `--radius-xl` (10px) plus backdrop blur for floating clusters OVER THE CANVAS (dock, view controls, identity chip), while the shipped stylesheet carries four literal `border-radius: 12px`, a value the closed scale (4/6/8/10) does not contain. A read-only measurement of both halves - per region, per palette role - is running as .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-settings-and-appearance/mockup-vs-shell-measurement.md, and this row's detail gets the measured values when it lands. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED is the structural cause. docs/design/mockups/README.md's "Keeping them current" section ends: "If a surface is rebuilt differently on purpose, capture the new state and replace the mockup file - the reference is always the current target, never a historical one", and its opening line is "These are the target." Neither parity gate did that. Plan 2's Task 10 adjudicated 22 shell differences and plan 5's Task 6 eleven settings differences, ten of them deliberate (horizontal tab strip where the mockup draws a vertical sidebar; 2-column radio choice rows with one ground+accent chip where the mockup draws a 3x2 grid of two-bar cards; no printed description under the heading; a Close the mockup omits; a Keyboard tab header and Reset placement the mockup predates; the modal painting the palette's glass), and every one was recorded in a commit while the drawing stayed as it was - so the rule the README states was applied as "say why" rather than "replace the file". CONSEQUENCE: the repo's own reference is now a historical target for two surfaces, which the README calls worse than no mockup because it is believed; the shell half carries the same shape in vg-217, vg-219 and vg-230. NOT FIXED HERE: replacing the mockup is design work over the adjudicated lists, it needs a home (plan 6's closing parity capture, or design-md-replaces-the-bible which decides the mockups' standing beside DESIGN.md), and the alternative - pulling the product back to the drawing - would reopen plans 2 and 5 and needs the user's call. What would settle it: name the files compared, then replace the settings section and the shell features the two lists adjudicated, or rule the drawing the target again and schedule the product work. UPDATE 2026-10-10, THE USER'S RULING: the mockup is NOT replaced ("Do not replace the mockup."), so the product-vs-drawing fork this row left open is closed in favour of the product, and what survives here is this row's process half alone — nothing signals that a mockup and the product have drifted, and docs/design/mockups/README.md's "replace the mockup file" rule was applied as "say why" for two surfaces across two plans (plan 2's 22 shell differences, plan 5's eleven settings differences, ten called deliberate). ADJACENT ROW, DIFFERENT DEFECT: vg-292 is the missing comparison itself — no gate anywhere compares a built surface to the mockup, so §13's parity capture could not fail; this row is the stale file, that one is the absent instrument, and the instrument is the cause.

title: The parity gate accepts any reason for a divergence, so a plan can grade its own surface 'deliberate' against a drawing it does not resemble — the rule that the mockup governs where the written rules are silent was absent
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER on 2026-10-10, answering the user's "why is it so hard to stay on target when we already have a clear visual mockup?" — the question was the finding: the process had no instrument that could report drift. MEASURED, by reading what each parity gate actually did rather than what it promised: plans 1-5 built to docs/design/design-language.md (the bible — §3 space/radius/elevation, §4 colour roles, §5 the closed control vocabulary, §7 per-surface rules) plus the spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-editor-design-language-design.md), and BOTH ARE PROSE ABOUT A LANGUAGE. A surface can carry every correct token, every control in the vocabulary, no hex literal and the right rhythm, and still look nothing like docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html — which is exactly what shipped: the shell insets its four regions 8px apart at an off-scale 12px radius where the drawing is flush (editor-shell.css:726,729,749,814,1130,1784, filed as vg-231), and the settings modal the just-closed plan built departs from the drawing's settings section in its frame, tab strip and palette cards (evidence: .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-settings-and-appearance/settings-vs-mockup-measurement.md). Spec §13 makes "a capture beside the mockups" a gate item, so every plan did produce one — six images for the settings modal alone — and every plan also produced a WRITTEN LIST of differences, ten of eleven called deliberate at plan 5 Task 6 and 22 at plan 2 Task 10. A written list is an argument; it has no failing state, so the gate could not redden and each plan closed green on accumulating drift. The controller compounded it by ruling those differences legitimate instead of treating the drawing as the acceptance test. CONSEQUENCE: the acceptance instrument claims coverage it does not have, the same family as vg-271 (a replacement control emits its own native input, which no <select> grep counts), vg-274 (no .css file is gated at all) and vg-286 (no rule decides which test files the ratchet covers). ADJACENT ROW, DIFFERENT DEFECT: vg-291 is the mockup file left stale; this row is the absent comparison, and this one is the cause. NOT FIXED HERE: the fix is a check or a rule — either measure a built surface's treatment and compare it to the drawing's, or make the drawing's own values the source a surface resolves from so the two cannot diverge — and that is the mockup-parity plan the user's 2026-10-10 ruling requires. What would settle it: state which surface-to-mockup comparison is enforced, name the owner, and prove it reddens on the state shipped today. CORRECTED 2026-10-10, BY THE USER, who said the verify step was requested at the outset: "I specifically requested to add a verify step to each of the plan to compare the current state against the mockup." That is true and this row's first version was wrong to say no comparison existed. VERIFIED: the requirement is in the spec — §12's table is followed by "Every plan above ends with a mockup-parity gate (§13) ... a completion condition of each plan", §13 steps 1-4 specify capture, placement beside the drawing, a difference list and an empty-diff finding, and the Acceptance section carries it as an item — and all six plans carry the gate (parity-step hits: gates 4, shell 3, inspector 4, panes 2, settings 4, copy 5). So the step existed, ran in every plan, and produced exactly this. THE REAL DEFECT IS THE ADJUDICATION RULE, at §13 step 3 as it stood: "Every difference is either fixed, or recorded in the commit as deliberate, with the reason." Any reason satisfied it. Plan 5 Task 6 listed eleven differences and recorded ten as deliberate, each citing a section's SILENCE as the warrant — D1 kept a horizontal tab strip because "§7 fixes the three tabs and what each holds, not their axis"; D2 kept two-column radio rows where the drawing has a 3x2 grid of cards; D3 kept the drawing's explanatory line absent; D9 kept the palette's glass where the drawing is opaque — and the aggregate of those locally-reasonable reasons is a modal the user described as looking nothing like the mockup. Plan 2's Task 10 has the same shape at 22 differences. A verdict that cannot be wrong is not a gate, and the missing premise was that silence in the bible is the drawing's jurisdiction rather than a licence. FIXED IN THE SPEC, 2026-10-10: §13 step 3 now requires a deliberate difference to name the bible §N, ADR or spec section that POSITIVELY requires the product's treatment; a new paragraph states that the mockup governs wherever the written rules are silent and quotes this failure as why it exists; the mockup-current paragraph now records the user's ruling that replacing the drawing is not an available disposition, allowing edits only to repair a stale or self-contradictory drawing; and the Acceptance item now reads for what a citation proves. STILL OPEN: the product surfaces are not yet brought to the drawing — that is the mockup-parity plan, scoped from the measurements in .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-settings-and-appearance/. What would settle it: a parity report whose deliberate differences each cite a rule that requires them, or none. SECOND MECHANISM, SAME ROW, FOUND BY THE MEASUREMENT OF 2026-10-10: a plan can license its own divergence. Exactly one of the settings modal's 19 measured regions is backed by a bible section, and that section - §5's "Choice row" - was ADDED TO THE BIBLE BY THE SAME PLAN that then cited it to justify drawing palette choices as radio rows instead of the mockup's cards. Amending the written language is legitimate (the control set is closed and the plan had to name the control it added), but a section written in the same commit is evidence of what was decided, not a rule that required it, and it cannot discharge the gate. The spec's §13 amendment of 2026-10-10 carries this as well as the silence rule: only a licence that predates the divergence counts.

title: The settings modal fails the drawing on 13 of its 19 measured regions, and no ruling authorises the deviation
detail: FOUND BY A READ-ONLY MEASUREMENT OF 2026-10-10 (opus), dispatched after the user reported that "even the setting panel you just built looks nothing like it" and ruled that the mockup is not replaced. EVIDENCE: .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-settings-and-appearance/settings-vs-mockup-measurement.md — 19 regions compared, verdicts 13 drift / 1 mockup stale / 2 match / 2 undefined. THE LARGEST IS COMPOUND, not one property: the mockup draws the palette choice as a 3x2 grid of bordered cards each carrying TWO 16px bars (ground and accent) plus a capitalised name, under the explanation "Colors the editor, not your theme"; the product draws a 2-column grid of radio choice rows carrying ONE 14x14 chip (shell-surface with an accent inset ring), the palette's lower-case id, and no explanation at all — four drifts (columns, card-vs-row, swatch, missing copy) that the plan's difference list recorded as four separate deliberate items. Others named by the measurement include the modal's frame and inset, its 13px lead, its tab strip axis and the glass panel where the drawing is opaque. OF THE 13, EXACTLY ONE IS BACKED BY A BIBLE SECTION and that section was written by the same plan (see vg-292's second mechanism); two are outright bible VIOLATIONS rather than questions and are filed separately as vg-294 (the scrim) and vg-295 (the lead); the rest are implementation choices no section names. NO AUTHORISATION FOUND: the measurement grepped docs/decisions/, docs/architecture/, the spec's §7 and the plan, and found nothing ruling on the treatment. COLOUR, the user's other report: the drawing's palette is hand-written CSS inside the mockup with zero hits anywhere under src/web/packages, only --accent #72e0c0 agrees with the product's, every other role differs (the drawing is flat and opaque where the product is alpha glass over a gradient), and bible §4 names ROLES not values - so the bible names nothing that can break the tie and a value decision is owed. BLAST RADIUS: about 5 files (editor-shell.css, settings.tsx, settings-keyboard.tsx, ui-copy.ts, possibly control-choice-row.tsx), and three of them leak to shared surfaces - the dialog frame, its lead and the kbd chip are shared with the ? sheet (shortcut-reference.tsx) and ControlChoiceRow is shared with the control-set fixture - so this is not a modal-local edit. NOT FIXED HERE: it is the mockup-parity plan's work, and the modal's 12px radius is the SAME rule as the shell's four, so the frame is one defect with one fix (vg-231), not two. What would settle it: a capture of the settings surface placed beside the drawing's Appearance and Keyboard specimens whose remaining differences each cite a rule that requires them.

title: The checked drawing declares four values that contradict the bible - two 9px cluster radii, three #0007 cluster shadows and a bordered follow-the-system row - and no mechanism compares the drawing to the bible at all
detail: FOUND BY TASK 1 OF THE SHELL-PARITY PLAN (2026-10-10), adjudicating every region of the two measurements into .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/adjudication.md. MEASURED, each against a bible section that states the value: (1) `editor-shell.html:178` and `:185` put the identity chip and the view cluster at `border-radius:9px`, where `design-language.md:93` gives `--radius-xl` 10px to exactly those clusters (dock, view controls, identity chip) and section 3 declares the radius scale closed; (2) `editor-shell.html:178`, `:185` and `:195` write the cluster shadows as `0 8px 20px #0007` and `0 10px 26px #0007`, where `design-language.md:103` fixes elevation 1 as `0 8px 20px #00000059`; (3) `editor-shell.html:288` wraps the follow-the-system toggle in `border:1px solid #242b34;border-radius:8px;padding:9px 10px`, a bordered container section 5 has no vocabulary for and section 1 forbids in the words "Chrome does not decorate". CONSEQUENCE: spec section 13 says "A mockup that no longer matches the bible is worse than no mockup, because it is believed" and requires the bible, the mockup and the spec to move in one commit - but the drawing is compared only to the PRODUCT (this plan reads it as the acceptance instrument and pulls the product to it), so a value the drawing gets wrong is inherited by the product rather than caught. This is the mirror of vg-291, which records the product diverging from a current drawing; here the drawing itself is off the bible and is the artifact that is stale. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a 9px cluster radius or a #0007 shadow is a deliberate drawing gesture or drift - the drawing has no commit trail of its own and every value is a literal in one file. What would settle it: a ruling on whether section 3's elevation 1 and the 10px cluster radius bind the drawing as tightly as they bind the product, and if they do, the three cited lines corrected in one commit that names this row. NARROWED BY TASK 3 OF THE SHELL-PARITY PLAN (2026-10-11), reviewing `42283107` and `be54cfc5`. THE SHELL DRAWING'S PART IS DONE: the two `9px` cluster radii and the three `#0007` shadows are corrected in the current set, where the lines are `current/shell.html:150`, `:157`, `:170` - this row cited `editor-shell.html`, the frozen original, which stays as it was - and the correction went wider than the four values cited here: twenty-one literals were off section 3's closed scale (eighteen `7px`, three `5px`; seventeen dock buttons, three view-cluster buttons, the follow-the-system track) and each is now its section 3 or section 5 entry. REMAINING: the third case, the bordered follow-the-system row at `current/settings.html:89-93`, is the modal's and is plan 8's (`vg-303` is its `padding:9px`). AND THE INSTRUMENT CLAUSE IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: no parity row reads any of these literals - putting one `7px` back into the drawing at `be54cfc5` leaves `design-language.spec.ts` green (5 passed) - so the correction this row asked for is not one the suite can hold in place. What would settle the clause is a row that reads a drawing's `border-radius` against section 3's scale; Task 6's gate is its natural owner. DISCHARGED IN PART BY PLAN 7 TASK 6 (2026-10-11, artefact 43e24bc5): the radius clause now has its mechanism - `design-language.spec.ts:2397-2436` reads every border-radius the drawing declares (75 declarations) and asserts each is a section 3 scale step (4, 6, 8, 10, 999, transcribed from `design-language.md:86-94`) or one of three named degenerates (1px, 2px, 50%, each carrying its reason in the row), with a positive control so an empty read cannot pass. The check is the row itself: putting one 7px back into `current/shell.html` reddens it naming the file and line, where at `be54cfc5` the same plant left the suite green. STILL OPEN: this row's other two clauses - the three #0007 cluster shadows and the bordered follow-the-system row - are read by no row, so the title's claim that no mechanism compares the drawing to the bible at all is now false of radii and still true of shadows and borders. THE MECHANISM CLAUSE WAS AN OVERCLAIM FOR ONE ROUND, AND IS NOW TRUE (2026-10-11, artefact c64c4c16, the whole-branch review of the shell-parity plan). The paragraph above says the gate reads every border-radius the drawing declares; at artefact 43e24bc5 it read `MOCKUP_PATH` and the shell drawing alone, and the file it named in a failure was a hardcoded constant - so the clause was true of one drawing of the four in `docs/design/mockups/current/`, which is the same failure this row exists to record, one level up. THE CLASS HAD MOVED RATHER THAN GONE, and the review found it where the gate was not looking: `settings.html` still declared twelve `3px` swatch chips and a `26x14` toggle track at `7px`, `controls.html` and `controls-light.html` the identical track, and `settings.html` a `0 10px 26px #0007` shadow - the same off-scale values Task 3 corrected in `shell.html`, in three files no row opened. WHAT LANDED: the gate now reads the directory through `currentDrawings()` (`mockup-values.ts:104`, a sorted directory read, so a fifth drawing is read the moment it lands) and each failure names the file and line it is in, with a per-drawing positive control; the test now sits at `design-language.spec.ts:2445`. Each corrected literal takes its section 3 entry - `--radius-sm` 4 for the swatch, `full` 999 for the track, as `current/shell.html:338` already read - and the settings dialog frame takes section 3 elevation 3, `0 24px 60px #000000b3`, not the elevation 1 the fix brief implied: the element is the modal frame, its product counterpart `.editor-shell-dialog` paints `--elev-3` (`editor-shell.css:1302`, token at `:362`), and section 3 reserves elevation 1 for floating clusters. RED PROVED: a planted `7px` in `controls.html` reddens the gate naming `controls.html:159`.

title: docs/design/mockups/README.md still discharges a visual difference by recording it as deliberate, the disposition spec §13's 2026-10-10 amendment removed
detail: FOUND by Task 9 of plan 7 while narrowing the neighbouring clause. THE SENTENCE: "How a gate uses them" ends "Each difference is then either **fixed**, or **recorded in the commit as deliberate** with its reason" (docs/design/mockups/README.md). SPEC §13 as amended 2026-10-10 rules the opposite: a difference between the drawing and the product is a defect unless a PREDATING rule — a bible §N, an ADR, a spec section — positively requires the product's treatment, and `ParityRegion.licensed` is the field the instrument already carries for naming it. "Deliberate" names no rule, which is the self-licensing that amendment removed. Task 9 narrowed "Keeping them current" for the same reason — the plan's own words for that clause are "the escape hatch that let two plans record divergences and leave the drawing standing" — and left this section alone, because the brief named only the table and that clause. CONSEQUENCE: a capture gate can still discharge any difference by calling it deliberate, so the instrument's discipline holds only where a PARITY row happens to exist. OWNED BY plan 7 Task 7, whose subject is the gate. What would settle it: the disposition reading "fixed, or licensed by a predating rule named in the commit", with `licensed` the word both the table and this section use.

title: The drawings invent the treatment of two controls no original draws - the segmented control and the in-button chord - so a surface the product has is given a gold target that no normative source states
detail: FOUND BY TASK 9'S TASK REVIEW (2026-10-10), reviewing commit 5773f652 against the user's ruling that the original mockup style is the gold target while the content is corrected to the product. THE GAP: `docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html` and `shell.html` draw two surfaces that no original draws and that the bible's closed control vocabulary does not name - the segmented control (Left/Centre/Right, Top/Middle/Bottom; the product's `control-segmented.tsx`) and the chord drawn INSIDE the publish trigger (the product renders `<kbd class="editor-shell-primary-key">` as a child of the trigger at `publish-control.tsx:145`, where the original drew a standalone chip). The drawings are right that the surfaces exist - that is content, and the user's ruling puts content on the product's side - but their **treatment** is invented by extending the well idiom, and treatment is the half the user ruled is gold. CONSEQUENCE: the in-button chip's border is `#06131a59` in the drawing, about 35%, where the product composes `color-mix(currentColor 45%, transparent)` (`editor-shell.css:1304`) - a numeric drift between the drawing and the product that no `PARITY` row asserts, because no row reads either drawing today. Under spec section 13 as amended a deliberate difference must name a normative source that requires it, and there is none for a treatment nobody has ruled on. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the drawn treatment is what the original's author would have drawn, or the implementer's reasonable extension - the review found no original that draws either control, so the question cannot be answered from the drawings. FLAGGED AS MINOR BY THE REVIEW, and filed rather than fixed because the fix is a ruling on the treatment, not an edit. OWNED BY NO PLAN: plan 7 Task 8 makes the two control drawings read by a test (its Step 1 adds the PARITY rows), which is what would catch the drift once the treatment is settled. What would settle it: a ruling naming the treatment for a control the originals do not draw - most cheaply, the product's own composed value adopted as the drawing's, since the drawing is otherwise a copy of the product's treatment for every surface that has an original.

title: A parity row is never checked against the property set its drawing declares, so a row - or its prose - can claim a comparison it does not make and still pass
detail: FOUND by plan 7 Task 8 fix round 2 on 2026-10-11, from the same audit family as vg-292. WHAT HAPPENED: `control-well.tsx`'s `ControlShape` doc said the boxed and headed shapes' `border-radius`/`gap` are read from their drawings 'rather than chosen here'. Reading was true. But both `PARITY` rows compared `border-radius` alone (`tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts`) while the drawings declared `gap:10px` and `gap:6px` too, so the product's `gap-[var(--space-10)]` and `gap-[var(--space-6)]` were compared to nothing. Round 2 added the two gap rows and each was shown failing against a one-step drift, and the controller reproduced the drift independently. WHY IT GENERALIZES: the failure is SILENT - a row that over-claims its coverage still passes, and only a reader who cross-checks the drawing notices, which is the same shape as vg-292 and vg-299 and the reason this plan exists. A `PARITY` row names exactly one `mockupProperty`; nothing relates that to the set the drawing selector actually declares, and nothing fails when the two disagree. Owner: the reader and the `PARITY` table (Task 1's instrument), which plan 7 has closed, so this needs either a small hardening task or a Task-6-style ratchet. What would settle it: a check that a row naming a property its drawing selector does not declare throws - the same 'fail loudly rather than resolve to nothing' rule the reader already applies to an unresolved or ambiguous selector.

title: The drawing's view cluster draws its three zoom/fit buttons at 22px where section 5's icon button starts at 26px, so the checked drawing shows a glyph control the bible has no vocabulary for
detail: FOUND BY TASK 3 OF THE SHELL-PARITY PLAN (2026-10-10), reviewing `42283107` at `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/task-3-review.md` finding 3. MEASURED: `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html:158,161,164` draw the zoom-out, zoom-in and fit buttons as `width:22px;height:22px`, while `design-language.md:154` defines the icon button as "A 26-30px square at `--radius-md`, glyph only" and the product's own `.editor-shell-view-step` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:2125`) is a 26px square. So the bible's only vocabulary for a glyph square starts 4px above what the drawing draws, and the drawing is the artifact the plan pulls the product to. CONSEQUENCE: this is a size divergence, not a radius one, which is why it is not Task 3's: Task 3 corrected the same three buttons' `5px` radius to `--radius-md` (`42283107`), and folding a 4px geometry change into a radius task would move the drawn cluster's width and every gap around it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the drawing's 22px is a deliberate compact gesture for the cluster (the drawn readout beside them is `min-width:34px`, and section 7 makes the top-right cluster wrappable) or drift from the document the cluster's own chips are drawn from. What would settle it: a ruling on whether section 5's 26-30px bound is the floor for every glyph square in the drawing, and if it is, `current/shell.html:158,161,164` drawn at 26px, with whatever the cluster's own layout then needs. No parity row reads this geometry today, so nothing reddens in the meantime.

title: The derived-palette ladder is asserted as order only, so a palette whose three surface rungs collapse to steps of 0.0001 keeps its ordering and passes every assertion
detail: FOUND BY TASK 4 OF THE SHELL-PARITY PLAN (2026-10-11) IN ITS OWN DELIVERABLE, reviewing `a3d2c407` at `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/task-4-review.md` finding 4. MEASURED BY READING THE ASSERTION: `design-language.spec.ts`'s derivation case compares `--bg`/`--panel`/`--panel-2` by luminance ordering (`bg < panel <= panel2`), which is what the plan's Step 5 asked for - "the luminance ordering ... matches graphite's" - and the plan's Step 3 asks for more: "takes from graphite the relationships between roles: the luminance separation". A palette whose three surfaces sit 0.0001 apart satisfies the ordering and shares nothing of the separation, so the assertion that exists to keep six transcribed value sets from drifting apart cannot see a collapse. TASK 4's FIX ROUND TIGHTENS WHAT CAN BE STATED WITHOUT INVENTING A NUMBER: strict `bg < panel < panel2` for the five derived palettes, editorial's equal `panel`/`panel-2` named as the one licensed exception. What is left is the magnitude, and that is why this is a row rather than a constant: a floor of "at least X luminance" has no rule behind it in the bible, and picking one is the move this plan has already had to undo once (the `biblePx` allowlist entry added to make a gate pass, R25). NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a magnitude floor is worth having at all, since a derivation is re-derived rather than edited, or whether the bible should state a minimum surface separation - section 4 gives the roles and no spacing between them. What would settle it: a bible rule naming the minimum separation between a ground and the panel above it, and then an assertion reading it. PLAN 7 TASK 6 SEARCHED FOR THE RULE AND FOUND NONE (2026-10-11). Read, and this is the search rather than the conclusion: section 3 (`design-language.md:64-109`, the spacing, radius and elevation tables) states no surface separation; section 4 (`:111-140`, the role table) gives the roles and no relationship between `--bg`, `--panel` and `--panel-2`; section 5 (`:141-206`) gives contrast ratios only (3:1, 4.5:1), which bind a boundary against its ground rather than the distance between two grounds; the drawing (`current/shell.html:17-18`) declares three literals with no stated relationship. No constant was added and this row stays open, because a magnitude floor with no rule behind it is the `biblePx` move (R25) this plan has already had to undo once.
