title: The drawing's token table is read as a set from the one element the width selector matches, so a token the drawing declares at the root or on a child of the drawn shell is invisible to the assertion that exists to catch it
detail: FOUND BY TASK 4'S SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-11) OF ITS OWN NEW ASSERTION, at `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/re-review-task4-round1.md`. MEASURED BY READING THE READER: `mockup-values.ts`'s `mockupDeclaredProperties` resolves the drawing's table through the element that carries the table (`[style*="width:1180px"]`, unique in `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html`), and the new set-equality case asserts that element's declared token names equal the eleven the test maps. That closes the hole it was written for - a twelfth token added to that same declaration is now red, where before it was invisible, which is how `--hot` arrived unnoticed by a row that listed ten. What it cannot see is a token declared anywhere else the drawing draws from: `:root`, or a child element that re-declares a `--shell-*` shadowing the table. CONSEQUENCE: a palette role the drawing gains outside its own table would still be invisible, so the assertion's coverage is 'the table', not 'the drawing'. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the drawing's style block does declare anything at `:root` today - the shell's tokens are on the one element, and nothing was found elsewhere - so this is a ceiling rather than a live miss. What would settle it: a ruling on whether the reader should walk the drawing's whole style block for `--*` declarations, or whether the one element is the drawing's contract by definition and a token anywhere else is a drawing defect to correct. Related: `vg-304`, which records that a parity row is never checked against the property set its drawing declares.

title: light is the one palette whose chrome is still translucent, so "chrome is opaque" holds in five of six palettes and light composites against a gradient ground
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 5 (2026-10-11) while making the chrome opaque, and reported to the controller as the brief asked rather than settled here: "where a palette's chrome has no derivation to read that is a finding for me, not a literal invented here". MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER after the change, reading `getComputedStyle().backgroundColor` on `.editor-shell-rail`: editorial `rgb(255,253,247)`, graphite `rgb(18,22,28)`, ember `rgb(247,226,210)`, moss `rgb(228,239,217)`, plum `rgb(236,227,247)` - all opaque - and light `rgba(239,249,242,0.75)`. CAUSE ESTABLISHED: `.editor-glass` now paints the palette's own `var(--panel)`, and light is the only palette whose surface roles carry alpha at all - `--shell-surface: #eff9f2bf` and `--shell-surface-strong: #f8fffbdf` - while its `--shell-backdrop` is the set's only gradient, so no role light declares is an opaque surface and plan 7 Task 4's derivation (graphite's relationships: the luminance ladder, the edge's weight against its surface) produces none. It is not expressible in CSS either: deriving the composite needs `color-mix` over `--shell-backdrop`, which is a gradient and is invalid inside `color-mix`. CONSEQUENCE: the rail, both panes, the inspector and the header each composite 25% of the mint gradient behind them, so light's chrome contrast is not one composited value and its boundary ratio (measured 1.40:1, `vg-200`'s pin) moves with the ground. The treatment assertion in `shell-appearance.spec.ts` names light as its one exemption and reads the translucency it carries, so a value that lands reds the gate and the exemption has to be deleted rather than left to excuse a regression. NOT FIXED IN TASK 5: choosing an opaque light surface is a palette value decision, and the task that owns the derivation is the one that should make it.

title: The built stylesheet emits only the prefixed -webkit-backdrop-filter, so the glass blur applies in no browser that has dropped the alias and the cluster treatment is a gradient and a shadow alone
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 5 (2026-10-11) while writing the treatment boundary assertion, which wanted to read a cluster's `backdrop-filter` and found it unreadable under every palette. MEASURED IN THE BUILT BUNDLE: `packages/editor/dist/assets/index-*.css` carries `-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(10px)saturate(135%)` and `-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(6px)` and NO unprefixed `backdrop-filter` declaration at all (a `[;{]backdrop-filter:` sweep returns zero matches), while `editor-shell.css` declares both properties on both rules. MEASURED IN THE BROWSER: in this Chromium (HeadlessChrome/153.0.8010.12) `CSS.supports("backdrop-filter","blur(1px)")` is true and `CSS.supports("-webkit-backdrop-filter","blur(1px)")` is false; `getComputedStyle().backdropFilter` reads `none` on the dock, the view cluster and the identity chip under all six palettes; and a probe that sets the STANDARD property inline computes `blur(10px) saturate(1.35)`, so the property works and the shipped declaration is what does not. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED: whether this Chromium has dropped the alias or the packaged build differs from Chrome stable; what is established is that the bundle ships only the prefixed form and this browser does not apply it. The build is Vite 8 (Rolldown) with the editor's `vite.config.ts` setting no `css.lightningcss.targets` and no browserslist, so lightningcss picks the prefix and the standard longhand is dropped - a configuration gap rather than a stylesheet one. NOT FIXED IN TASK 5: the fix is a build target, and Task 5 owns the treatment boundary, not the toolchain. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GATE: the cluster half of the boundary is asserted as translucency + gradient + elevation shadow and cannot assert the blur as a computed value, which is also why `shell-appearance.spec.ts` had already chosen `box-shadow` rather than `backdrop-filter` as its discriminator.

title: `--shell-flat` is declared in two palette blocks and consumed by nothing, so the file carries a token whose only reader is a name list in a test
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 5 (2026-10-11), which reported it as an observation rather than filing it. MEASURED: `--shell-flat` is declared at `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:45` (editorial, `1`) and `:136` (graphite, `0`), and a sweep of `packages/editor/src` finds no consumer - no `var(--shell-flat)`, no `@media`, no rule keyed on it - while `editor-shell.tokens.test.ts:238` names it only inside `NOT_A_COLOUR`, a list of tokens that are not colours. After Task 5 the token is more plainly metadata: it was never what chose the flat treatment, which the palette selectors decide. CONSEQUENCE: a declared-but-unread token reads as a live knob and is not one, so anyone changing it sees no effect and no test fails. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether it was declared ahead of a consumer on purpose - ADR 0040 records `--stage`, `--hdr` and `--edge-2` as the three roles declared ahead of their first consumers on the user's instruction, and `--shell-flat` is not among them, but the same pattern would look identical. What would settle it: a ruling on whether a per-palette flat flag is wanted at all (the treatment is selector-driven today), and if not, the two declarations and the `NOT_A_COLOUR` entry deleted in one commit.

title: The boundary assertion names its chrome and cluster sets as literals on the test side, so an element added later escapes half the check
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 5'S SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-11) as two Minor notes, both non-blocking, and filed rather than fixed because what should define membership is an instrument decision and not a patch. NOTE A: `shell-appearance.spec.ts`'s `GLASS_CLUSTERS` is a literal pair (`[`.editor-shell-dock`, `.editor-shell-zoom`]`), so a further element carrying `editor-glass` is read for translucency and shadow but never for the sheen that class gives it - the escape is invisible precisely because the new element resembles the two that are checked. NOTE B: the chrome half holds every surface's rendered alpha against a probe painted `var(--panel)`, while the header paints `--shell-surface` (`editor-shell.css:548`); the two are equal only because all six palettes alias `--panel: var(--shell-surface)`, so a palette that decoupled them by alpha would false-red the header and one that decoupled them by colour alone would pass. MEASURED BY THE REVIEWER rather than carried from the report: `--panel` is declared on `:root` and on `[data-shell-palette=`light`]`, both on the element `choosePalette` writes (`shell-palette.ts:66`), so the body-appended probe does read the palette's value and the assertion is not vacuous. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether either note is worth closing - a set derived from the stylesheet can hide the same gap in the other direction (an element that loses `editor-glass` leaves the sheen check silently), and Note B is a fact about today's aliasing rather than a defect. What would settle it: a ruling on whether an assertion may name the elements it covers, and if it may not, which side of the boundary owns membership.

title: `current/shell.html` draws no Add-pane asset preview, so the surface the product renders at `file-section.tsx:189` is one no gate can check
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 7 (2026-10-11, as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `7efea17f`) and adjudicated by its task review rather than left as the implementer's observation. MEASURED: `current/shell.html:128-140` draws the Add pane's Asset group as a select, then `Import a file`, then Replace/Remove, and a case-insensitive search for `preview` in that file returns nothing, while the product renders an `img.vigilia-asset-preview` carrying `data-vigilia-asset-preview` at `panes/add/file-section.tsx:189-194`, styled at `editor-shell.css:1107`, and both `editor-shell-add-desktop-chromium.png` and `pane-add-desktop-chromium.png` show it. DISPOSITION: `drawing-stale`, not `fix` - pulling the product to the drawing would delete a real capability (the thumbnail and its hidden-when-unpreviewable rule), spec section 13.1 does not let a visual difference waive a required capability, and Task 9's own rule sends a capability the product has and the drawing lacks into the drawing, because a gate cannot check a surface the drawing never draws. The frozen original `docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html` stays as it is; the repair belongs to `current/shell.html` and was in flight as Task 7's fix round 1 when this row was filed. CONSEQUENCE UNTIL IT LANDS: the plan's own completion condition (section 13: every difference fixed or backed by a cited rule) is not met, and the Asset group is the least-comparable region besides, because the 1280x720 capture clips `Import a file`, `Replace asset` and `Remove asset` below the fold where the 1180x1040 drawing shows them. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the repair should be paired with a reader row, since that needs machinery the parity table does not have today. THE DRAWING HALF IS DISCHARGED (2026-10-11, artefact 221bf1a1, Task 7 fix round 1): `current/shell.html` now draws the preview well between the Asset select and the `Import a file` row, in the drawing's own idiom, with the class it stands for named in a comment beside it - `height:120px;aspect-ratio:1672/941` taken from a live measurement of `[data-vigilia-asset-preview]` on the built bundle (213.3x120 at the pane content's left edge, flush under the select), and a gradient standing in for the chosen picture. The frozen original is untouched and nothing was renumbered. The parity table re-ran green with the drawing changed and no row's answer moved (9 passed at `--workers=1`, re-run by the controller against `design-language.spec.ts` rather than taken from the report). WHAT REMAINS, AND WHY THIS ROW STAYS OPEN: the title's second clause is untouched - a surface the drawing omits is still one no gate can check. No reader row was built, and the reason is measured rather than laziness: the product's contract is `max-height:120px` with `object-fit:contain`, a bound and not a size, and the Add pane is `display:none` while Document is open, so a row would read no element. This class - a drawing that omits a surface the product renders - needs a surface-inventory check and belongs to `vg-304`'s family; the row stays open as that family's member rather than closing on the half that was repaired.

title: Shipped source cites a plan's git-ignored execution state, so the citation points at a file no clone has
detail: FOUND WHILE CLOSING PLAN 7 (2026-10-11, as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `0c6a17c0`). MEASURED: `src/web/tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:494` introduces the `PARITY` table with "The shell's regions, as the census adjudicates them (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/adjudication.md`)" - a path inside `.superpowers/sdd/`, which the repo's own plan README (`docs/superpowers/plans/README.md:7`) calls "ignored execution state", and which the subagent-driven-development skill deletes when a plan's final review comes back clean. So the citation names a file no clone has, and the census it points at (the region-by-region adjudication every `PARITY` row's licence and disposition comes from) has no durable home. THE CONVENTION IS ALREADY IN USE IN TRACKED DOCS, which is why this is a question rather than a one-line fix: `.github/bug-player-chart-throw.md:123`, `docs/decisions/0003-authored-text-box-outlives-the-text.md:186` and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-dashboard-authoring-design.md:605` each cite a different `.superpowers/sdd/` workspace the same way, and `docs/decisions/0003` is an accepted ADR, so the pattern predates this file. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the right answer is to keep the workspace (the plan's evidence then outlives the plan, at the cost of a git-ignored directory nothing prunes), to move a census worth keeping under `docs/evidence/` when the plan closes, or to treat the citation as provenance that a reader is expected to reconstruct from the archived plan plus the register. The third is the cheapest and is what the other three sites already rely on; the second is the only one that makes the claim checkable. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a user ruling on where a closed plan's evidence lives, since this decides whether the census a parity gate argues from is reviewable by anyone but the session that wrote it. Owned by whoever closes the next plan, not by plan 7, which is closed.

title: The settings modal's Close button is `--shell-text` on `--vigilia-control-bg` where the drawing draws `--muted` on `--panel2`, and no plan-8 task owns it
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 1 (2026-10-11, census row #19, filed as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `9a6667ac`). MEASURED: the re-adjudication of the closed plan's region #19 - the drawing at `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html` draws the modal's Close control in `--muted` on `--panel2`, and the product renders it in `--shell-text` on `--vigilia-control-bg`. The census classifies it `fix` - no predating rule requires the product's treatment - but no task in plan 8's ten touches the control, so it is filed here rather than folded into a task it does not belong to. WHY IT IS NOT IN PLAN 8: the plan's tasks were written from the measurement's own region list, and region #19 moved when the drawing did - the measurement's row read `undefined`, because the superseded `editor-shell.html` drew no Close control at all, and the current set does. So the row is new evidence the plan could not have scheduled, and adding a task for it now would put an unscheduled edit in a plan whose phases are already dispatched. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a §4 colour-role correction on the Close control's rule in `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css`, with plan 8 Task 1's settings row (or a fifth row) reading `--muted` against `--panel2`, and the §13 capture in Task 10 showing it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the product's treatment is deliberate - the control is a `ControlButton` and `--vigilia-control-bg` may be the control set's own resting fill rather than a second declaration of the same value. If it is the control set's, the fix is the control's owner and the blast radius is every surface using it, which is why this is a row and not a one-line change. SECOND INSTANCE - PLAN 8 TASK 7 (2026-10-11): the Keyboard panel's return-to-default actions render the same fill against the same drawn treatment. The drawing draws `border:1px solid var(--edge);border-radius:6px;background:var(--panel2);color:var(--muted)` on every one of them (`docs/design/mockups/current/settings-keyboard.html:50`, `:61`, `:70`, `:79`, `:92`, `:101`, `:110`, `:119`, `:128`) while `.editor-shell-keyboard-action` renders `background: var(--vigilia-control-bg)` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1586-1594`), so the class is the Close button plus these - and the text colour is NOT part of this instance, because the product's `--shell-muted` is the drawing's `var(--muted)` renamed. Task 7 reported it rather than fixing it, because the fill belongs to the control set's owner and the blast radius is every surface using it, which is what this row already says. The correction belongs to that one owner, not to three edits. PLAN 8 TASK 10 RE-CONFIRMED THIS ROW'S FIRST INSTANCE AGAINST THE SHIPPED BUILD (2026-10-11, commit b78ee264): the Close renders --shell-text on --vigilia-control-bg, left-aligned, padding 6px 12px, margin-top 18px (`editor-shell.css:1397-1416`) where `current/settings.html` draws --muted on --panel2, right-aligned, padding 4px 12px, margin-top 16px - and no section names this control's fill or text colour, so it is a fix with no predating licence. Its 18px is also one of the four vg-325 values Task 9's ceiling counts by name, and the left alignment is visible in the committed capture beside the drawing.

title: A dialog's own body type resolves no §2 role — it inherits the portalled document's 13px (`packages/editor/index.html:21`), so the `?` sheet's rows render at §2's `--text-md` by accident where §2 gives list rows `--text-sm`
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 3 (2026-10-11, as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `51245173`). MEASURED: `packages/editor/index.html:21` declares `html, body, #app { font: 13px/1.5 ... }`, and `.editor-shell-dialog` declares no base `font-size` of its own, so every dialog opened through the portal inherits that 13px — the `?` sheet's 20 rows included. §2 (`design-language.md:49`) gives list rows the 12px role, and `:50` separately names the 13px role for panel bodies, so the sheet's rows land on the right number for the wrong reason: no rule in the dialog's own sheet chose it, and the day the host document's base moves the sheet's rows move with it. WHY PLAN 8 TASK 3 DID NOT FIX IT IN PASSING: that task moved two rules whose values were wrong (`.editor-shell-dialog kbd` to `--text-xs`, `.editor-shell-dialog > button` to `--text-sm`), each of which declares its own size; this one is a size nothing declares, and giving the dialog a base role would set the type of every surface inside every dialog — five leads, two titles, the settings navigation, the palette grid and both sheets' rows — which is a region each of plan 8's later tasks owns and none of them would find green afterwards. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a §2 role on `.editor-shell-dialog`'s own body rule, chosen per region rather than as one blanket base, with plan 8's drawings gate reading the row that lands on it, and the §13 capture in Task 10 showing the sheet. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the intended fix is a base on the dialog plus per-region overrides, or per-region declarations alone — the first re-moves Task 2's lead row if the override is missed, and the second leaves the portalled document as the base for anything a later surface adds.

title: The modal frame's own boundary against the scrim reads 1.22:1 in graphite and 1.08:1 in editorial, below the 3:1 section 5 asks, and no gate measures a dialog at all
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 3'S REVIEW (2026-10-11, finding F1, `task-3-review.md`), which rejected the implementer's discharge of its own measured regression. MEASURED RENDERED, not modelled, before and after `51245173`: the frame's `--shell-edge` composited over the pixel behind it, the same arithmetic `vg-200`'s pin uses - graphite 1.22:1 before, 1.08:1 after; editorial 1.07:1 before, 1.21:1 after. The scrim is the page's dimming, so replacing the overlay's `#0009` (60% black) with section 3's `#00000073` (45%) moves every colour behind it; graphite got worse and editorial got better, and both sit far below 3:1 either way. WHY `vg-200` DOES NOT OWN THIS, which is the whole finding: `vg-200` pins the well and chrome hairline over `--panel-2`, read by a chrome-contrast test that measures the RAIL's own surface pixel and opens no dialog (`design-language.spec.ts:1985-2043`, `PINNED_FLOOR` at `:137`), so the modal's frame is measured by no gate and pinned by nothing - and `vg-200` is itself `open`, awaiting the user's ruling on a different region's floor, so citing it as this region's floor cites an open question. Plan 8's Review Focus 4 and Task 3 Step 3 ban a SILENT third cell, not a recorded finding, so the reviewer's remedy was a row rather than a revert. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a modal frame's resting boundary is a control's only separation - section 5's 3:1 binds that - or a frame that also carries a fill, a shadow and a radius, which is `vg-200`'s provisional reading and would make it a divider. The user's ruling on `vg-200` decides this row too, which is why the two are cross-referenced rather than merged. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a gate that measures a dialog's frame against whatever is behind it - the parity table cannot, because the drawing draws no scrim at all (`mockup-values.ts:946-948`) - together with the resolution of `vg-200`'s floor ruling. RULED BY THE USER (2026-10-11): the narrow reading, which is `vg-200`'s ruling and therefore this row's too -- a modal frame carries a fill, a shadow and a radius and is not a control's only separation, so its resting boundary against the scrim is a divider and the 1.08-1.22:1 readings are deliberate low-contrast style rather than defects. WHAT REMAINS, and it is not the contrast: no gate measures a dialog at all, so this row's other half is real and stands -- `design-language.spec.ts`'s chrome-contrast test measures the rail and opens no dialog. SUPERSEDED IN PART: the user has since ruled that Settings should be a PANE rather than a modal (`vg-330`), which retires the scrim this row measures; the reader gap is re-read there rather than closed here.

title: The dialog's shared `h3` and read-only `dl` rules resolve no bible role: a group heading is `--text-xs` where §2 gives the eyebrow `--text-2xs`, the row pads 3px where §3's steps have no 3, and §5 rule 2's 74px label column is drawn by neither side
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 4'S REVIEW (2026-10-11, findings F1 and F4, `task-4-review.md`) and NOT carried by its commit - `6ca510ce` has no `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer, so it is materialised from the review instead, which is why the provenance names a finding number rather than a message. THE THREE FACTS, each measured at the line it rests on. ONE, the group heading: `.editor-shell-dialog h3` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1353-1357`) is `font-size: 11px` with `letter-spacing: 0.12em`, while §2 (`docs/design/design-language.md:47`) gives the eyebrow role `--text-2xs` 10px and `:55-57` fixes an eyebrow at `--text-2xs`, `600`, `letter-spacing: .11em`, muted, 'always labels a region, never a control' - 11px is `--text-xs`, whose role at `:48` is 'Panel rows, hints, status bar'. Task 4's drawing is right and the product is wrong: `current/settings-keyboard.html:54` draws `font:600 10px/1.2 ...;letter-spacing:.11em`. TWO, the read-only row's inset: `.editor-shell-dialog dl > div` (`editor-shell.css:1368`) is `padding: 3px 0`, and §3's steps (`design-language.md:69`) are `4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, 32` - there is no 3. The drawing takes 4px (`current/settings-about.html:50`). THREE, §5 rule 2's grid: the rule (`:163-165`) says read-only rows 'share the grid with controls so a section does not jump between shapes' and that 'the grid is a 74px label column and one value cell', while the product's rule is `justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px` with a content-sized label and the drawing copied that shape - so the column is implemented by neither side. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN AN EDIT: all three live on two shared element rules, and those rules are rendered by three surfaces across two dialogs - `settings-keyboard.tsx:153-154`, `settings.tsx:146` and `:214`, `shortcut-reference.tsx:39-40` - so a per-surface patch would fix the settings modal and leave the `?` sheet's group headings wrong, which is the defect Task 3 already fixed once at its owner. WHY NO ROW READS ANY OF IT TODAY: the parity table's About and Keyboard rows read the panels' own declared properties and pass, and plan 8 Task 8's widened gate reads the DRAWINGS' literals, not the product's - so the three facts are invisible to every gate in the repo. THE 74px HALF IS THE ONE THAT NEEDS A DESIGN DECISION rather than a value: whether §5 rule 2 binds a dialog's read-only `dl`, or whether the shared grid is the control rows' alone, decides whether the About panel's rows must take a column the Appearance panel also uses. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a §2 role on the `h3` rule, a §3 step on the `dl` row's inset, a ruling on the grid question, and a parity row that reads each - with the §13 capture in Task 10 showing the result. RELATED, NOT THE SAME: `vg-317` is the dialog body's UNDECLARED 13px base, `vg-295` (verified) was the class one level up - the dialog's lead - and `vg-302` (verified) is the same 74px column on CONTROL rows, which plan 7 Task 8 landed as `ControlRow`'s `column`/`boxed`/`headed` shapes; this row is the READ-ONLY row's half, which that one did not cover. SECOND MEASUREMENT - PLAN 8 TASK 7 (2026-10-11): the Keyboard panel's group heading is this same shared rule, and the divergence is two properties with one cause. The drawing declares `font:600 10px/1.2 system-ui;letter-spacing:.11em;text-transform:uppercase` (`docs/design/mockups/current/settings-keyboard.html:54`) and `.editor-shell-dialog h3` renders `font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.12em` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1367-1372`), which is section 2's eyebrow rule (`design-language.md:55-57` - `--text-2xs` at 10px, weight `600`, `letter-spacing: .11em`) read one step and one thousandth off. CORRECTED BY TASK 7'S REVIEW (2026-10-11): the first version of this sentence gave the wrong reason - that sharing puts it out of reach, 'the same reasoning that scoped the chord chip'. Those are opposite moves. Scoping the chip fixed the panel WITHOUT touching the sheet, and a `.editor-shell-keyboard h3` scope would fix this panel's eyebrows without touching the sheet either, so sharing is not what puts the value out of reach. The reason is OWNERSHIP: a per-surface patch would fix the settings modal and leave the `?` sheet's group headings off section 2, splitting one concept across two owners, so the fix belongs at the shared rule's owner, which is where this row already puts it. The divergence is live and correctly deferred either way; what was wrong was the reason, because a later reader could have reused it to defer something genuinely in scope. The Keyboard panel alone is off section 2 on twenty eyebrows until the shared rule moves. This is evidence for the row, not a second row. A THIRD INSTANCE, MEASURED BY PLAN 8 TASK 10 AND FILED AS ITS TRAILER IN b78ee264 (2026-10-11): the Appearance drawing's own heading is `font:600 12px/1` sentence case (`current/settings.html:42`) where the Keyboard drawing draws its group headings at `font:600 10px/1.2;letter-spacing:.11em;text-transform:uppercase` (`current/settings-keyboard.html:54` and four siblings), and the product renders both through the shared `.editor-shell-dialog h3` at 11px / .12em uppercase - so the DRAWING side does not hold the treatment section 2 reserves for a section eyebrow either, and the two sides are wrong in opposite directions. The eyebrow rule is `design-language.md:54` (a first pass cited `:56`, which is the middle of the sentence). Task 4 and Task 7 reported the product side identically.

title: A drawing's value that is on §3's scale but not the original's treatment is read by no gate, so the keyboard drawing shipped a 4px row container where the original draws 6px and only a reviewer's eye caught it
detail: FOUND IN PLAN 8 TASK 4 (2026-10-11), and found the only way it can be found today: the task review read `current/settings-keyboard.html` against the frozen original by eye. MEASURED: the row container carried `border-radius:4px` where `docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html:311` draws `border-radius:6px` and `docs/design/mockups/README.md:120-123` says the treatment - 'colour, spacing, radii, type, elevation, hairlines' - 'is copied from the original drawings' and 'is never redrawn from the product'. WHY NO GATE SAW IT, which is the finding rather than the value: the drawings gate asserts membership in §3's CLOSED SCALE - `design-language.spec.ts:2531` 'every radius the checked drawings declare is on §3's scale', `const SCALE = new Set(["4px", "6px", "8px", "10px", "999px"])` at `:2541` - and 4px IS on that scale, being `--radius-sm`, 'swatches, inline chips, the slider thumb's container' (`design-language.md:90`). So the gate answers 'is this a value §3 has?' and never 'is this the value the original draws?', and a drawing can diverge from the original in any on-scale direction while every gate stays green. THE OTHER INSTRUMENTS CANNOT REACH IT EITHER: no `PARITY` row names that container, because it paints no fill and no border, so no colour or border row can address it; and plan 8 Task 8's widening to spacing and type is scale-based the same way, so it inherits the hole rather than closing it. The value was fixed in `3b46efb8` (4px to 6px, all 20 rows) after the review named it. NOT ESTABLISHED: what the right instrument is. Two candidates, and they are not equivalent - (a) a gate comparing the declarations of the elements a drawing COPIES from its original (the frame, the navigation, the Close control, the row containers) against the original's declarations, which needs a named list of copied elements because the current set is redrawn with the product's real content and a whole-file diff would be noise, or (b) the copied treatment declared once and imported by every drawing so it cannot drift, which is the stronger fix and changes how a drawing is authored. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: one of those two, plus a ruling on which elements are copies rather than redrawings. RELATED: `vg-314` is the sibling class - a surface the drawing OMITS is one no gate can check - and this row is a value the drawing STATES wrongly; both are gaps in the drawing-versus-something comparison rather than in a value's own legibility. NOT THE SAME AS `vg-296`, which was a file nothing read at all.

title: The settings drawing's six palette preview bars depict a different token per palette — four a `--shell-surface`, light a backdrop gradient, graphite a gradient `a3d2c407` retired — where the product paints all six from `--shell-backdrop`, and no row reads a bar's colour
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 5 (2026-10-11, as the first `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `411dbe91`). MEASURED: `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html:46-83` draws twelve bars inside six cards, and the first bar of each card holds a different role depending on the palette - `#fffdf7` for editorial, and editorial's own `--shell-surface` IS `#fffdf7` while its `--shell-backdrop` is `#f5f1e8` (`editor-shell.css:32-34`), so that bar draws the palette's SURFACE; ember, moss and plum likewise; light's bar is its `--shell-backdrop` gradient; and graphite's bar is `linear-gradient(145deg,#101923,#071116)`, the first two stops of the three-stop graphite backdrop gradient `a3d2c407` REMOVED from the token. The product paints all six bars from `--shell-backdrop` (`editor-shell.css`), which is §4's 'The window behind everything' and the plan's and the measurement's own word for this bar, 'the palette's ground'. WHY IT IS NOT SETTLED HERE: the drawing is gold for treatment and README `:120-123` lists COLOUR among the treatment that is copied from the original and 'never redrawn from the product', so correcting the drawing's six bars to the product's reading is exactly the move that rule forbids; but the drawing contradicts itself across its own six cards, so it cannot be read as one rule either, and the four-of-six majority reading would put `--shell-surface` where §4 puts no ground. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the bar depicts the palette's surface (the drawing's majority) or its backdrop (§4's one ground role). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a ruling on which role the ground bar depicts, then either the drawing's six bars corrected or the product's one declaration changed, plus a `PARITY` row that reads a bar's colour - the row that exists reads the bar's HEIGHT (`mockup-values.ts:1050`), so today the instrument cannot see either reading and both pass every gate. HOW IT WOULD SURFACE OTHERWISE: plan 8 Task 10's §13 capture is the only place a person would look at the six cards beside the drawing. RELATED: `vg-320` is the same shape one step further out - a drawing value no gate reads. PLAN 8 TASK 10 READ THIS ROW AGAINST THE SHIPPED BUILD (2026-10-11, b78ee264) and found no predating rule that decides it, so it stays open and blocked on the same question. The six palette cards now render in `docs/design/mockups/current/settings-capture-graphite.png` and `-editorial.png` beside the drawing: twelve bars whose grounds are visibly not the light ground, while the drawing gives a different role per palette (four a shell surface, light a backdrop gradient, graphite the retired a3d2c407 gradient) and the product paints all six grounds from --shell-backdrop and all six accents from --shell-accent (`editor-shell.css:777-784`). Section 7.8 (`design-language.md:412`) requires only that palette choices retain visual swatches and names no role, and section 4's --bg (`:123`) is a definition of a role rather than a requirement that a preview bar depicts it. RULED BY THE USER (2026-10-11): the bar depicts the palette's GROUND, `--shell-backdrop`, which is the product's reading today and section 4's 'the window behind everything'. The drawing's six bars are the stale side: it gives a different role per card rather than stating one rule, which is an internal contradiction and so correcting it is a treatment fix rather than the redraw `README.md:120-123` forbids. WHAT CLOSES IT, and it is two changes: the drawing's six bars are repainted to --shell-backdrop, and a `PARITY` row is added that reads a bar's COLOUR -- today the only row on those bars reads their height (`mockup-values.ts:1050`), so the instrument cannot see either reading and both pass every gate.

title: The settings drawing's frame is a fixed 560px while the modal is content-sized, so it measures 405px on Appearance and every drawn region inside it renders half-size — and no row reads a drawing's frame width
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 5 (2026-10-11, as the third `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `411dbe91`). MEASURED: `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html:20` draws the modal's frame at `width:560px` fixed, while the product's `.editor-shell-dialog` is `min-width:340px; max-width:560px` and content-sized (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1311-1312`), so Task 5's report measures it at 405px on the Appearance tab, 507px on Keyboard and 393px on About. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE POINT: the palette cards render about 58px wide against the drawing's about 120px, so the grid is the drawing's three columns while each card is half the drawn width and the drawn proportions are not reproduced anywhere in the modal. WHY NO GATE SEES IT: the one row on the frame reads its `border-radius`, and no row reads a drawing's width - the same gap `vg-292` names for another geometry and `vg-320` names for a drawing's value. WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE: it is the frame's geometry rather than the palette group's, and Task 5's outcome is the group; the plan's ten tasks name no frame width, and the three panels' content differs (Keyboard is already 507px), so taking the drawing's fixed width is a ruling about the modal rather than an edit inside it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the modal should take the drawing's 560px, or a width per panel, or whether a content-sized modal is right and the drawing is the stale one - the drawing's `width:560px` may simply be how a static drawing is authored rather than a property the product must match. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: that ruling, plus a row that reads the frame's width so the next divergence is visible. IT IS NOT THE SAME AS THE GLASS OR THE RADIUS: the modal's frame radius is a green row and stays green. PLAN 8 TASK 10 MEASURED THE PRODUCT SIDE, WHICH THIS ROW DID NOT HAVE (2026-10-11, b78ee264): the modal is content-sized today at 405px on Appearance, 507px on Keyboard and 393px on About, against the drawing's fixed `width:560px`; the Appearance pane's palette cards therefore render about 58px wide where the drawing draws about 120px, and the difference is visible in the committed capture beside the drawing. NO PREDATING RULE NAMES A DIALOG'S WIDTH: section 3's table is spacing, and the bible's two dialog rules are the title's type (section 2) and the scrim (section 3), so this is not licensed and stays open. REJECTED RATHER THAN ANSWERED, BY THE USER (2026-10-11), and this is the larger finding: 'Setting should not be a modal but a panel like add, composition.' The question was whether the modal takes the drawing's fixed 560px; the answer is that there should be no modal to measure, so this row's width question and the 405/507/393px measurements are about a container that is going away. Filed forward as `vg-330`, which owns the change and the drawing redraw. This row stays open only so the measurement is not lost; it closes when `vg-330` does.

title: The gate list a plan's tasks run contains no test run, so plan 8 Task 6 closed a commit with `vitest run` red and only CI - which never ran, nothing being pushed - would have caught it
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 7 (2026-10-11, as the third copy of a literal Task 6 was told to update). MEASURED: from `src/web/`, `package.json`'s six gate scripts are `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `design:check`, `status:check` and `backlog:check`, and `test` is a separate script (`vitest run`) that none of them invokes. Commit `f735c81b` (Task 6) corrected the drawing's boxed follow-the-system row from `padding:9px 10px` to `8px 10px`, and `tests/e2e/mockup-values.test.ts:112` addressed that row by the old literal, so `mockupDeclared` threw 'the drawing addresses nothing' and the unit suite was red from `f735c81b` until `90187a82` - across Task 6's implementer run, Task 6's review, its close-out commit `96d44901`, and my reading of both. Task 6's review ran the browser specs and the six gates, all clean, which is exactly what its brief asked for. WHY THE REVIEW COULD NOT SEE IT: none of the six gates executes a test, and Task 6's brief carries no test-run step while Task 7's Step 4 does ('Run the whole editor unit suite and record its counts') - so of ten tasks, one asks for the suite and the other nine can close with it red. WHY CI IS NOT THE ANSWER: CI does run it (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:61-62`, 'Unit tests: npx vitest run'), so a push or a PR would have caught it - but no push is authorised while this plan runs, so the tree sat red with every local signal green. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the durable fix is a seventh gate (`vitest run` in the gate list), a test-run step in every task brief, or a controller instruction in every dispatch - the last is what plan 8 adopted from Task 8 onward, because it reaches the implementer without amending a plan's text. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: one of those three, plus evidence that a drawing edit which strands a reader now reddens something the task itself runs. IT IS NOT `vg-320`: that row is a drawing's value being on section 3's scale but not the original's treatment; this one is the absence of any run that would notice a value's readers disagreeing.

title: No drawing in the checked set draws the `?` shortcut sheet, so one modal surface is outside the acceptance instrument and two plan-8 rulings leaned on that absence
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 7 (2026-10-11, while scoping the chord chip). MEASURED: `docs/design/mockups/current/` holds six drawings - `controls.html`, `controls-light.html`, `settings.html`, `settings-keyboard.html`, `settings-about.html`, `shell.html` - and **not one of them draws or mentions the shortcut reference sheet**. `settings-keyboard.html` contains the word 'shortcut' because it is the Keyboard panel's own drawing; a search for the reference itself ('shortcut reference') matches nothing in the directory. The sheet is not a fringe surface: `shortcut-reference.tsx:36-45` renders `h2.editor-shell-dialog-lead`, one `section` per group and a `kbd` per row directly into the dialog, so it is the second consumer of the modal's shared rules and it is on the keyboard-only walkthrough (spec `:516-521`, 'open and close a popup', 'cancel shortcut capture'). TWO RULINGS LEANED ON THIS ABSENCE, both soundly: Task 7 scoped the chord chip to `.editor-shell-keyboard kbd` rather than moving the shared `.editor-shell-dialog kbd`, because moving it would move a surface no drawing governs; and `vg-319` defers the shared `h3` eyebrow for the same reason. Neither ruling is wrong - the point is that the instrument's hole became load-bearing twice without being named. WHY IT MATTERS: the sheet has behaviour proof (`vg-284` names what that proof misses) and no treatment comparator at all, so every pixel of it is unmeasured against the gold target - the same shape as `vg-314`, which names the Add pane's asset preview as a surface no gate can check. Spec `:506-507` is explicit that a visual difference cannot waive keyboard access or contrast, and those are exactly the properties a drawing is the instrument for. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a drawing of the sheet in `current/`, in Task 4's pattern for the Keyboard and About panels - or a ruling that the sheet's treatment is wholly inherited from the modal's drawing and needs a comparator of its own nowhere. NOT ESTABLISHED: which of those two is right, and whether the sheet is in scope for the drawing set at all - the plan's Out of scope assigns the shell and its clusters to plan 7 and says nothing about the sheet.

title: The drawings now declare six values `editor-shell.css` contradicts, and no gate reads the product side of a drawing comparison
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 8 (2026-10-11), materialised from the six `Discovered, not fixed:` trailers in the fix commit `f5e6870d`. The implementation commit `80ae353f` carried the same six in prose only and no trailer, which is why they nearly reached the register as nothing at all. MEASURED, each verified at the line by the controller before filing: (1) the Close - `settings.html` draws `margin-top:16px`, `.editor-shell-dialog > button` declares `18px` (`editor-shell.css:1400`); (2) the rail - `shell.html` draws `gap:4px`, `.editor-shell-rail` declares `3px` (`:872`); (3) asset buttons - `controls.html` draws `padding:4px 8px`, the rule declares `4px 7px` (`:1146`); (4) asset-button text - the drawings say `12px`, the rule inherits `13px` (`:1147-1154`, a role disagreement rather than an off-scale value); (5) the Add pane body - `shell.html:62` draws `10px 10px 14px`, `.editor-shell-panel` declares `12px` (`:931`); (6) the nav column - `settings.html` draws `10px 6px`, `.editor-shell-settings-tabs` declares `padding: 0` (`:1460`) because the 150px is a border-box width and a padding there would shorten the content box the parity row reads (`:1438-1441`). WHY THE CORRECTIONS CREATED THEM: Task 8 moved 268 off-scale drawing literals onto section 3's steps and section 2's scale; where the product counterpart lives in `editor-shell.css` - which appears in no `design-tokens.gated.json` entry - the drawing lands on the step while the product keeps the old number. Three of the six are product-off-scale (18px, 3px, 7px), one is a role disagreement, and TWO ARE COMPOSITION DIFFERENCES WHERE BOTH SIDES ARE ON SCALE (the Add pane body and the nav column), so this is not a single remedy. WHY NOBODY OWNS THEM: Task 9 Step 3 explicitly refuses a fix that moves pixels ('a design decision ... belongs to vg-274's own pass - do not fold it in'), so the three off-scale values are not its work either, and plan 8's ten tasks name no product file for any of the six. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a correction should have been withheld where it created a divergence. The controller ruled it should not - the bible wins where the current set disagrees with it (`docs/design/mockups/README.md`) and spec `:481-483` makes a drawing that disagrees with the bible worse than no drawing - so the six are the price of the instrument being right, and the remedy is a product pass rather than a drawing retreat. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the two composition differences disposed of in Task 10's section 13 difference list if a predating citation exists (the nav column's border-box invariant is the strongest candidate, and it must be verified against a rule that predates this plan rather than against the `:1438-1441` comment plan 8 wrote), and the four scale and role differences as a named product pass of their own. IT IS NOT vg-231, which is the shell's four body regions at an off-scale 12px radius - a different set of values in the same file - and it is not vg-274, which counts that file's residuals rather than its disagreements with the drawings. PLAN 8 TASK 10 SUPPLIED THE DISPOSITION THIS ROW ASKED FOR (2026-10-11, b78ee264), and the answer is NOT the candidate the row proposed: the `editor-shell.css:1438-1441` comment is one plan 8 itself wrote (Task 2, 5e8ba2b0), and a comment the plan wrote cannot license the plan's own divergence, so it was refused rather than cited. The nav column's `padding: 0` was disposed instead as the other face of the composition difference the census already records for its rows 4 and 7 - the product places the dialog's inset on the frame at `20px 24px`, which section 3 (`design-language.md:79`, the 20-24 between-regions and dialog-padding row) positively licenses, so its children declare none; a literal fix of the nav column alone would give it a 10px inset IN ADDITION to the frame's 24px, matching neither the drawing nor the product. The Add pane body's inset was disposed the same way, licensed by section 3 (`design-language.md:77`, the 12-14 section-padding and panel-gutter row; a first pass cited `:79`, which is the other row). Both composition differences are therefore dispositioned rather than open, and the four scale values remain a named product pass - capped and counted by name in the ceiling Task 9 landed (`vg-274`): margin-top 18px at `editor-shell.css:1400`, gap 3px at `:872`, and padding 4px 7px at `:1148` and `:1189`.

title: Section 3's row-density rhythm is read by no gate: the drawings gate holds spacing to the step list and never to the 26/30/32 rule, which is where 75 corrected well insets would have shown
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 8'S REVIEW (2026-10-11). MEASURED: section 3's density rule (`docs/design/design-language.md:82-84`) gives the row rhythm 26, 30 and 32 - values that are deliberately NOT on the spacing step list at `:69` - and Task 8's widened drawings gate holds a spacing declaration to the step list alone, so a row drawn at the wrong density passes as long as its padding is a step. The scale where it would show: the 75 `5px -> 4px` well insets, because `control-well.tsx:52-56` pins `h-[26px]` in the product while the drawing expresses the same row through padding, so the drawn well height is font-metric-dependent - the `font` shorthand the drawings use sets no line-height - and the two sides can disagree with neither gate nor report examining it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the drawings and the product actually disagree on any row's height - the review that found this did NOT claim a break, only that nothing examines it. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: either a rule that the density values are outside the spacing arm's reach with a reason, or an arm that reads them (which needs a rendered height rather than a declaration, so it is a different kind of check from everything else in this gate). IT IS NOT vg-320, which is a drawing measured against the frozen original; this is a drawing measured against a written rule no arm reads.

title: The ceiling over editor-shell.css counts violations, so a swap - one violation corrected while another arrives - leaves it green and the file's residual set unread
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 9 (2026-10-11), while landing the ceiling it names. `scripts/design-tokens.mjs`'s `CEILINGS` caps `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css` at 58 violations, and it is green at HEAD. It compares a *count*, so it cannot see WHICH violations they are: fix one of the 24 spacing values and let a different literal arrive in the same commit and the count is unchanged at 58 - green - while the set the exemptions were measured against has moved. Three of the 61 are keyed on their own text (`margin-right: 62px`, `92px`, `122px`) and so cannot be swapped silently; the other 55 can. CONSEQUENCE: the instrument reads as capping the file's residuals while it caps only their number, so a surface can drift in one place and be repaired in another with no failure anywhere. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: read the violation SET rather than its size - a per-key allowlist of rule plus value (the shape the three exemptions already use, extended to the whole file) or a comparison against the recorded list - each a different instrument from the one this task was scoped to build. NOT FIXED HERE: the plan mandates the count shape (Task 9 Step 1, a row that fails above the measured count and passes at or below it), and widening it decides what the file's residuals are *allowed to be*, which is a design decision rather than a task. SECOND INSTANCE, ONE RUNG FURTHER - PLAN 8'S FINAL WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW (2026-10-11): an exemption is not a site either. `scripts/design-tokens.mjs:283-289` filters the exemptions on `violation.text`, so a second `margin-right: 62px` added anywhere in the file would be exempt too - the count would not rise and the dead-exemption guard would not fire, because the keyed text still exists once. The finding above says a count is not a set; this says a key is not a line. NOT FIXED: the exemption shape is Task 9's mandated one, and keying on site as well as text is a different instrument. IT IS NOT `vg-274`, which is the file's exposure to the ratchet at all; this is the coverage of the instrument built to cap it. Same family as `vg-271`/`vg-274`/`vg-286`/`vg-292`: an acceptance instrument claiming more coverage than it has - and here the count IS the deliberately chosen shape, so the finding is the limit of the fix rather than a defect in it.

title: The settings drawing names the surface as an eyebrow inside the nav column while the product names it once as the dialog's title, and neither side draws the other's
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8'S FINAL WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW (2026-10-11), which caught the difference list claiming to be exhaustive without it: `adjudication.md` says task 10's list disposes of every drawing-versus-product difference still open after the re-run, and this one is in neither L1-L4 nor D6-D10 nor any row in `vg-316`-`vg-327`. MEASURED, both sides at `file:line`: the drawing draws `Settings` as a nav eyebrow - `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html:23`, `font:600 10px/1`, `letter-spacing:.11em`, uppercase, `color:var(--faint)`, `padding:4px 8px 8px`, inside the `width:150px` column - while the product renders no nav eyebrow and names the surface once, above the whole nav-plus-panel row, as `<h2 class="editor-shell-dialog-lead">` at `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/settings.tsx:336`, which `editor-shell.css:1348-1352` sets to `--text-lg` (the declaration is `:1351`). Neither side draws the other's element. THE LICENCE CANDIDATE, and it covers half the difference: §2 `:51` gives `--text-lg` 15px to "Dialog titles", so the product's title role and its size are on-bible and are not a defect - the census's row `#5` rules exactly that, and the parity row `settings modal — lead type` holds it. THE QUESTION THE LICENCE DOES NOT ANSWER: whether the nav should ALSO carry the surface name, which is the duplication `task-2-report.md:49-53` refused when it ruled one name for one surface. That refusal was reasoned, so this is a design question rather than a defect - but it lived only in `task-2-report.md`, which is git-ignored scratch, which is why it is filed here rather than left to prose. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a ruling on whether the drawing's eyebrow is how the drawing labels a column (and the current set is the stale side, which `docs/design/mockups/README.md`'s treatment-copied-from-the-original rule argues against correcting), or whether it is a second place the surface is named and the drawing is stale on it - then a `PARITY` row either way, because the eyebrow is a value of one element on the drawing's side and nothing on the product's. IT IS NOT `vg-319`, which is the shared `h3` group heading's type at 11px / `.12em` against §2's eyebrow; this is the nav's missing eyebrow, a different element. RULED BY THE USER (2026-10-11): one name. Plan 8 Task 2's refusal stands -- one name for one surface -- and section 2 (`:51`) already licenses `--text-lg` for 'Dialog titles', so the product's title role and size are on-bible and are not a defect; the drawing's eyebrow is how the drawing labels a column rather than a second naming. The refusal is written here because it lived only in `task-2-report.md`, which is git-ignored scratch. RE-READ UNDER `vg-330`: with Settings as a pane the surface is named once in the pane's own header rather than in a dialog title, so the PRINCIPLE survives and the location moves.

title: backlog-check validates only docs/product/backlog.jsonl, so the archive's verified rows are checked by nobody - about twelve carry no artefacts and vg-303 holds a bare string where 121 hold an array
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8'S FINAL WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW (2026-10-11), which reported it and left the hand-check to the controller. MEASURED: `scripts/backlog-check.mjs:45` resolves `FILE` to `docs/product/backlog.jsonl` and nothing reads `docs/product/backlog-archive.jsonl`, so every rule in that file - a `verified` row needs a `check` naming a word from its own title, and an `artefacts` sha that resolves and is an ancestor of HEAD - is enforced on the live register alone. THE COST IS THAT THE CLOSED REGISTER IS UNREAD WHILE THIS BRANCH CITES IT AS EVIDENCE: plan 8's commits print `backlog:check: 186 items, all valid`, and 186 is the live file's count, so the sentence says nothing about the archive. TWO SUB-FACTS: (1) about twelve archive rows carry no `artefacts` at all, which the live-file rule would reject as "verified with no artefact commit"; (2) `vg-303`, closed by this branch, holds `artefacts` as a bare string where 121 archive rows hold an array - a shape the array-only reader (`Array.isArray(item.artefacts)`) cannot consume. THE SUBSTANCE HOLDS, measured by the controller by hand on the three rows this branch touched (`vg-294`, `vg-295`, `vg-303`): all three shas resolve and are ancestors of HEAD, and all three `check` fields name a word from their own titles. So this is a coverage gap rather than bad data, and the correction is not a rewrite of the archive. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: point the checker at both files with the same rules, and normalise the `artefacts` shape - either by accepting a bare string or by fixing the rows that are not arrays. NOT DONE HERE: plan 8's fix round is a review-driven fix, and widening a gate's scope to a second register is a change to what the gate owns rather than a fix to a finding.

title: Settings is a modal today and the user has ruled it should be a pane like Add and Composition, opened from the rail's gear, with the settings drawing redrawn as a panel
detail: FOUND BY THE USER (2026-10-11), reading the current mockup capture, in answer to the modal width question this round put to them: 'Setting should not be a modal but a panel like add, composition.' Three further sub-rulings came with it, each asked with a recommendation and each answered as recommended. (1) HOW IT OPENS: the rail keeps its FOUR slots -- Composition, Add, Tokens, Document -- and the gear opens Settings as a pane in the same area, exactly like Add and Composition; the pane's own header then names the surface, which is also this round's answer to `vg-328` (one name). A fifth rail slot was offered and declined: it would change the drawing's 46px rail and leave the gear redundant with the slot, which is two controls opening one surface. (2) THE DRAWING: `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html` is REDRAWN without the scrim and the modal frame, as a pane at the shell's pane width. The user was told this edits the gold artefact and chose it anyway, because they had ruled the drawing is the acceptance instrument and a panel that is not drawn as a panel cannot be compared against anything -- Task 9's parity item could not be met for Settings at all. (3) SEQUENCING: after plan 6, not now. WHY IT IS A SPEC AND NOT A TASK: it touches the rail, the shell layout, `ownership.md` and the drawing, and AGENTS.md requires brainstorm then spec then plan for something of that shape; it also cannot run beside plan 6, because exactly one implementation plan is active at a time. WHAT IT INVALIDATES, recorded here so the future spec re-reads them rather than rediscovering them: plan 6 Task 8 Step 3's acceptance item -- 'the rail's gear opens the settings modal rather than a fifth pane' -- which is TRUE while Settings is still a modal and is superseded the moment this lands (that item is deliberately NOT corrected in plan 6, since plan 6 finishes first and the item is accurate for its duration); `vg-318`'s scrim measurement, which measures a container that will not exist; and `vg-322`, whose whole subject is the modal's width. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the spec and its plan landing, with the redrawn drawing committed beside the shipped pane and a PARITY row on the pane's frame so the next divergence is visible.

title: The palettes carry one accent and the user has asked for a second highlight, orange for graphite, whose role is an attention or in-flight state and must be defined before any colour is chosen
detail: FOUND BY THE USER (2026-10-11), looking at the current mockup capture: 'graphite needs another highlight/accent color, like orange, on top of the current pallete (other themes to follow once we define the role of this color).' THE ROLE WAS ASKED AND ANSWERED FIRST, because a colour chosen before its job is a colour that will be used for the wrong thing: it is an ATTENTION or IN-FLIGHT STATE -- something that is neither the primary action nor destructive, such as unsaved or unpublished changes, a reading that is stale or awaiting the author, or a pending operation. Two alternatives were offered and declined: a second colour for emphasis with no state meaning, and re-hueing graphite's existing --shell-accent to orange instead of adding a role. WHAT THE ROLE REQUIRES BEFORE ANY HEX IS PICKED, and each is a decision rather than a lookup: a name that says the JOB and not the hue (--attention, not --orange); a bible section 4 clause saying when it may appear, since section 4 already rations --accent to at most one accent-filled element visible and a second colour with no stated job is exactly the competition that rationing exists to prevent; and a rule keeping it off the same element as --accent, so the two can never both claim a surface. IT IS NOT GRAPHITE'S ALONE: the user's own framing is that the role is defined once and the other five themes follow, so the output is a section 4 role plus a per-palette value in each of the six, not a graphite-only token. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the section 4 clause and the six values, which is spec work rather than a task, together with whatever gate reads a state colour -- the contrast instrument measures text and boundaries and has no state-colour row today. RELATED: `vg-330` is the other change the user asked for in the same sitting, and both are sequenced after plan 6.

title: biblePx carries 1.6, 1.7 and 1.8 as stroke widths but the scanner regex needs a px suffix, so those three entries can never fire and the plan states they guard stroke widths
detail: FOUND WHILE APPLYING THE WEIGHT RULING (2026-10-11) in plan 6 Task 2b, by asking the brief's question empirically instead of assuming the answer. The task was to decide whether the new 10px tier weight of 2 had to be added to `scripts/design-tokens.gated.json`'s `biblePx`. It does not, and the cause is not about 2: `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` matches px with the regex `(d+(?:.d+)?)px`, which requires the literal suffix. A bare numeric literal is invisible to it, so the three stroke-width entries already in `biblePx` -- 1.6, 1.7 and 1.8, alongside 3, 11, 14, 26, 30, 32, 36, 46, 74, 246, 276 and 999 -- have never gated anything. The proof is in the tree rather than in a reading: `icons.ts` is a gated file and it held `GLYPH_STROKE_WIDTH = 1.75` for two commits, a value absent from `biblePx`, with `design:check` exiting 0 throughout. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A DEAD ENTRY, and this is the part that is a defect rather than a tidy-up: plan 6 Global Constraints states the opposite belief in words -- "section 6's 1.6-1.8 are already in biblePx, so a stroke width is legitimate where a spacing value would not be" -- so a future reader is told the allowlist is what licenses a stroke width, when the allowlist cannot see one and the DOM assertion is the only thing that ever has. That sentence is now the misleading half and needs correcting wherever the weight ruling propagated, which Task 2b did not do because the brief scoped propagation to the rule itself. NOT FIXED ON THE FLY: removing the three dead entries and correcting the sentence are both small, but they are a decision about whether biblePx should keep values that only a px-suffixed CSS stroke could use -- `editor-shell.css` may legitimately write `stroke-width: 1.7px` -- and that is a read of the CSS before anyone deletes anything. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: either the three entries are shown to be reachable from a px-suffixed site and kept with a comment saying which, or they are removed, and Global Constraints says plainly that the text scan does not gate stroke widths and the DOM case does. RELATED: `vg-192` is the same family of claim -- a gate believed to cover something it cannot see.

title: The gradient editor is missing from the accessible-name audit, so its control names are attested by nothing
detail: FOUND WHILE REVIEWING plan 6 Task 4 (2026-10-11). Its first evidence line went stale on 2026-10-11 and is corrected here rather than left to mislead: Task 4's fix round 1 (`a512efb7`) made `control-icon-button.dom.test.tsx` import and mount `GradientEditor`, so the grep that returned nothing no longer does. THAT MOUNT DOES NOT CLOSE THIS ROW, and reading it as closure would be the mistake: the icon-only census excludes the stop dots by its own glyph clause -- a control is icon-only when its whole content is a glyph, and the dots draw none -- so mounting the editor there attests nothing about their names. The gap is the NAMING audit: `accessible-names.dom.test.ts`'s `mountPanels` still does not list the gradient editor. THE CONTROL THAT PUT THIS IN VIEW: `components/ui/gradient-editor.tsx:72-74` renders each stop as a drag handle carrying an `aria-label` built from the row's own label and the stop's index, plus `aria-valuenow` -- so it IS named, deliberately, in source; it simply is not checked by any test. WHY THAT IS THE DEFECT AND NOT A TIDY-UP: the same file's own doc comment states the contract in words -- adding a panel to the editor means adding it to `mountPanels`, and an unmounted panel is not audited, rather than audited and clean -- a distinction it learned from `vg-114`, where the asset pane and the new-theme chooser had gone years without appearing. The gradient editor is that case again, in a file this plan has since touched. WHAT MAKES IT SHARPER RATHER THAN MERELY STALE: Task 4 ruled the stop dots out of the icon-only census on the grounds that a drag handle draws no glyph, which is defensible on its own terms -- but it means the population that covers icon-only controls excludes them AND the population that should cover their names does not mount them, so the control sits between two audits with neither looking at it. The Task 4 fix round removed the weaker half of that complaint (the census now mounts the editor and is explicit about why the dots are outside it); the naming half is what remains. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the gradient editor joins `mountPanels`, or a stated reason says why it cannot be mounted there and what covers it instead. RELATED: `vg-114` is the same contract failing once before; this row is its third known instance rather than a new rule.

title: gradient-editor.tsx draws a 1px outline with a raw #000 literal, which is a colour value no token owns
detail: FOUND WHILE REVIEWING plan 6 Task 4 (2026-10-11); reported by the implementer as pre-existing and left untouched, which is the right call for a task about accessible names, but unfiled is not the same as recorded. `components/ui/gradient-editor.tsx:79` sets `boxShadow: "0 0 0 1px #000"` — a raw hex where every other value in the editor comes from plan 1 tokens (bible section 4 names colour ROLES, and `editor-shell.css` owns the palette). Task 4 added this file to `scripts/design-tokens.gated.json`, so it is now under the scanner, which is how the literal came into view at all. CAUSE IS ESTABLISHED AND IT IS NARROW: a hard-coded outline colour. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and is why this is filed rather than fixed: which ROLE that outline is. It reads as a hairline separating a stop dot from the track beneath it, which could be section 4 boundary (the focus boundary already has a 3:1 requirement per the user ruling on `vg-200`) or a shadow role (`--elev-*`), and picking one is a read of the drawing and of what the outline is for rather than a substitution anyone can make from the literal alone. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the role named, the literal replaced with its token, and the gated count falling by one.

title: The copy walk reads no opened menu popup, no Settings Keyboard/About tab and no canvas context menu, though all four are reachable in jsdom
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 6 TASK 5'S REVIEW (2026-10-11), which checked the implementer's claim that these surfaces were Task 9's and found the claim false: Task 9 is the browser PARITY capture, so it will not close a unit-test coverage hole. THE MEASUREMENT, from the reviewer's own walk of the source: opened menu popups ARE reachable -- `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx:1042` opens the View menu and `:1159` the Edit menu, both reading `[role=menuitem]`; the Settings Keyboard tab is reachable -- `accessible-names.dom.test.ts:586` clicks the `[role=tab]` named `uiCopy.settings.keyboard`, and the About tab is the same gesture; and the canvas context menu is reachable -- `canvas-context-menu.dom.test.tsx` mounts it and reads its `[role=menuitem]` after a `contextmenu` dispatch. All four are reachable in jsdom, so the hole is the copy walk's. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED, and the reviewer's sweep is the reason it is not urgent: NO LITERAL CURRENTLY LIVES IN ANY OF THE FOUR. The walk's author swept every non-test source for a literal-valued `aria-label`/`title` and found none besides the three Task 5 moved and `document-identity.tsx`'s `title={documentName}`, which is the document's own name and therefore data. So this is a coverage hole, not a live defect -- and the controller's ruling was to state the boundary in `ui-copy.test.ts`'s doc comment rather than pay for it now, because opening a menu under jsdom costs 50-90 s (`vg-135`, measured in `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx`) and three opens plus new gestures is a poor trade for a hole with nothing in it today. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the walk mounts the opened Edit/View/File popups, the Settings modal's Keyboard and About tabs, and the canvas context menu, each with the per-surface non-empty assertion the walk already uses for its four mounted surfaces. The cost is the jsdom menu-open time, so whoever closes it should decide whether those cases belong in the focused gate or in a slower tier -- that decision is why this is a row and not a task. RELATED: the boundary is stated in `ui-copy.test.ts`'s own doc comment, which names these four and the reason, and the commit that recorded it is `869da1a9`.

title: The colour picker's four track sliders announce their test id, so a screen reader reads out a CSS-selector-shaped token instead of a word
detail: SURFACED BY PLAN 6 TASK 5'S REVIEW (2026-10-11) while adjudicating the copy walk's skip rule, and it is THE ROW `vg-194` HANDED OFF AND NOBODY FILED: that verified row's own closing paragraph ends 'each track's `aria-label` is its `testId`, so what a screen reader announces is `picker-saturation, slider, 0`, and the words an author would want are a copy decision rather than a mechanism one. That is a separate row, not a reopening of this one.' This is that row; the mechanism half `vg-194` owned is done and is not re-opened by it. THE MEASUREMENT: `components/ui/colour-picker.tsx`'s `Track` renders `aria-label={testId}`, so each of the four tracks (the saturation/brightness area, hue, and the two strips) has an accessible name of `picker-saturation`, `picker-hue` and so on -- a token shaped like a selector rather than a word. `vg-194` closed the keyboard path and the declared `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` in the same component, so the value announcement is sound; what a person hears first is the name, and the name is the defect. WHY THE COPY WALK DOES NOT CATCH IT, which is the part worth recording: the walk's rule skips any element whose `aria-label` equals its `data-testid`, and the reviewer ruled that rule CORRECT -- a driver's hook is not a word a translator would change, and forcing these into `uiCopy` would be wrong. So the net is right to skip them and the label is still wrong: the two facts are independent, and the skip rule must not be weakened to catch this. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: each track's `aria-label` reads a word from `uiCopy` (`Saturation`, `Hue`, `Alpha`, `Value`) while the `data-testid` hooks keep their current values, so the skip rule stays and the announced name becomes a word. The wording is a copy decision, which is why it is not an agent's to take silently. RELATED: `vg-194` (verified, archived) is the row that identified this and deferred it; `vg-179` is an unrelated picker row.

title: ui-copy.ts is 869 lines, past the 800-line stop, and the copy table is growing while nothing records an exemption for a data table
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER PREPARING PLAN 6 TASK 6 (2026-10-11), while checking that task's own instruction to add two cases to `ui-copy.test.ts`. THE MEASUREMENT, at `7ae6d519`: `wc -l` gives `packages/editor/src/ui-copy.ts` **869** and `packages/editor/src/ui-copy.test.ts` **783**. The repo's rule is 500 lines a signal and 800 a stop for a normal source file, and this register already carries the same class three times -- `vg-209` (`layer-panel.tsx` 838), `vg-255` (`selection-inspector/index.ts` 822) and `vg-276` (`shell-layout.tsx` 916) -- so the observation is not new, only this file's. THE DECISION THIS NEEDS, WHICH IS WHY IT IS A ROW AND NOT A TASK: `ui-copy.ts` is a string table, most of its bulk being doc comments that state why each word is the word. The stop is written for source files and the repo does allow an explicit exception for proven vendored source, so the honest questions are whether a copy table is a file the stop aims at, and if not whether the exception should be written down rather than assumed. Splitting it by namespace (menus, panels, inspectorFields, view, actions) is the obvious repair if the stop does apply, and the test file would follow the split. THE IMMINENT HALF, which is why this was noticed now: plan 6 Task 6 instructs two new cases in `ui-copy.test.ts`, which sits at 783 -- so the task that owns the copy rules is the one that would take the test file past the stop. The controller's instruction to that task is to record the crossing explicitly rather than let it happen silently, and to prefer a focused file if the additions would cross. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an exemption written down with its reason, or a split of both files with the test following. Nothing is broken by the length itself; what is broken is that the rule exists and this file is past it with nothing said.

title: The copy walk reads no paragraph text, so shell-layout.tsx renders a hint with no owner in uiCopy
detail: FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING plan 6 Task 6 (the copy defects). src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx:908 renders a paragraph whose only text is: Move and lock the selection with the canvas dock. It renders whenever a selection exists, and the sentence is a literal - not in ui-copy.ts and returned by no accessor. ui-copy.test.ts reads a surface through label text, aria-labels and button text (spokenIn), and the pictograph rule sees only the table, so a paragraph is read by neither net: a word an author reads with no owner, which is the class the copy rule exists to catch. MEASURED across packages/editor/src for a bare JSX text line: this is the one rendered instance (composition-pane.tsx:629 is the same shape inside a comment, not rendered); single-word and inline forms were not exhaustively enumerated, so the class may hold more. NOT FIXED HERE because the regression test needs the walk to read paragraph text, which is Task 5 own net and outside Task 6 file set, and whether the net should read every text node or only these three kinds is a coverage decision rather than a one-line edit. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: widen spokenIn (or the copy rule) to the surface own text nodes, then move this sentence into uiCopy behind an accessor.
